title: Joint space narrowing progression quantification with joint angle correction in rheumatoid arthritis
source: Biomedical Engineering International Conference
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a form of autoimmune disease characterized by synovitis that can ultimately cause joint deformities and impaired functioning. The cartilage destruction is one of the most important indicators for diagnosis and treatment of Rheumatoid arthritis, and it is radiographically manifested as joint space narrowing. In this study, we propose a joint location detection method and a sub-pixel accurate method for quantifying joint space narrowing progression with a joint angle correction. The proposed joint location detection method can detect the location of 14 joints from a given hand radiographic image, the error of 89.13% joints is less than 3 pixels (spatial resolution: 0.175 mm/pixel). In our previous works, we measured joint space narrowing progression between a baseline and its follow-up finger joint images by using partial image phase only correlation. We found that the inconsistency of joint angles may lead to characteristic mismatch and thus affect the accuracy of joint space narrowing quantification. In this work, we introduce rotation invariant phase only correlation in joint space narrowing quantification for joint angle correction. In our experiment, the improved quantification method can effectively manage the mismatch due to the inconsistency of joint angles.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; joint space narrowing; sub-pixel accuracy; phase-only correlation; radiographic images; finger joints; cartilage destruction

title: Automatic Measurement of Joint Space Width from Hand Radiographs Using Deep Learning Models
source: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
abstract: Joint Space Width (JSW) is a measurement to diagnose hand osteoarthritis from radiographs. This study proposed an automatic method to measure JSW using a modified VGG19 model and U-net segmentation as the pre-processing step. With a dataset of 3591 hand radiographs, 34,597 DIP/PIP/MCP joints were cut. The ground truth was labeled by healthcare professionals. We first trained individual models for each type of the DIP, PIP, and MCP joints and finally trained a combined model for all. The individual models produced correlation coefficients of 0.88, 0.88, and 0.90 and mean square error (MSE) of 0.02 mm, 0.02 mm, and 0.03 mm for DIP, PIP, and MCP joints, respectively. The combined model further improved the performance to 0.89, 0.89, and 0.98 in correlation and the same MSE. The result demonstrates that the proposed method is robust to different sizes and shapes of hand joints and can save the time of manual labeling.
keywords: joint space width; hand osteoarthritis; hand radiographs; automated measurement; U-Net segmentation; joint segmentation; distal interphalangeal joint; proximal interphalangeal joint; metacarpophalangeal joint

title: Deep Residual Network (ResNet) for Multi-Class Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis in Radiographic Images
source: International Conference on Advances in Computation, Communication and Information Technology (ICAICCIT)
abstract: Millions of people worldwide suffer from knee osteoarthritis (KOA), a degenerative joint disease. It is characterized by a decreased quality of life, decreased mobility, and chronic discomfort. For KOA to effectively be managed through early intervention, early and accurate detection of KOA by the patient also becomes paramount. The Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading scale was utilised in this study's distance-learning (DL) approach to automatically classify the severity of KOA from knee x-ray images using the ResNet-18 architecture. The training dataset, 8,260 radiographs, comprised training, validation, and test datasets, each classified according to our five KL grades. Pre-processing steps to standardize input images included resizing, normalization, and RGB conversion. The model showed good multi-class classification accuracy as measured by performance metrics on the test set: 95.00% accuracy, 85.60% precision, 76.00% recall, and 71.01% F1 score. In order to increase interpretability and confidence for a clinical user, we additionally employed Grad-CAM visualizations to demonstrate users where in the knee x-ray the model was influencing the predictions.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; radiographic image classification; ResNet; ResNet-18; knee X-ray images; multi-class classification; Grad-CAM; model interpretability; early disease detection

title: A Sub-Pixel Accurate Quantification of Joint Space Narrowing Progression in Rheumatoid Arthritis
source: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that primarily affects peripheral synovial joints, like fingers, wrists and feet. Radiology plays a critical role in the diagnosis and monitoring of RA. Limited by the current spatial resolution of radiographic imaging, joint space narrowing (JSN) progression of RA for the same reason above can be less than one pixel per year with universal spatial resolution. Insensitive monitoring of JSN can hinder the radiologist/rheumatologist from making a proper and timely clinical judgment. In this paper, we propose a novel and sensitive method that we call partial image phase-only correlation which aims to automatically quantify JSN progression in the early RA. The majority of the current literature utilizes the mean error, root-mean-square deviation and standard deviation to report the accuracy at pixel level. Our work measures JSN progression between a baseline and its follow-up finger joint images by using the phase spectrum in the frequency domain. Using this study, the mean error can be reduced to 0.0130 mm when applied to phantom radiographs with ground truth, and 0.0519 mm standard deviation for clinical radiography. With the sub-pixel accuracy far beyond usual manual measurements, we are optimistic that the proposed work is a promising scheme for automatically quantifying JSN progression.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; joint space narrowing; phase-only correlation; sub-pixel accuracy; finger joints; phase spectrum; early rheumatoid arthritis

title: ResEffiNet: A Hybrid Efficientnet and ResNet Approach for Automated Kellgren-Lawrence Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis Images
source: International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease where early and accurate diagnosis is critical for effective management. The Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system is the standard radiological metric for assessing OA severity, but manual grading is subjective and time-consuming. To address this, we propose ResEffiNet, a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that synergistically combines EfficientNetB3 and ResNet-18 for the automated KL grading of knee Xrays. EfficientNet-B3 excels at extracting fine-grained features efficiently, while ResNet-18 enhances feature learning stability through its residual connections. Feature maps from both networks are fused to form a comprehensive representation, which is then classified into the five KL grades ($0-4$). Evaluated on a public dataset of 4,950 knee radiographs, our model achieved a state-of-the-art accuracy of 98.2 %, a precision of 98.0 %, and an F1score of 98.0 %, significantly outperforming existing benchmarks. These results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach offers a robust, highly accurate, and clinically valuable tool for automating OA diagnosis, with the potential to streamline radiological workflows.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; knee X-ray images; EfficientNetB3; ResNet-18; hybrid deep learning model; feature map fusion; osteoarthritis severity assessment; computer-aided diagnosis

title: An Investigative Approach to Knee Osteoarthritis Detection Using Deep Learning on X-ray Radiographs
source: IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A chronic joint condition called osteoarthritis affects the ligaments, capsule, synovium, subchondral bone, and articular cartilage. Osteoarthritis most frequently develops in the knee joints. A scoring system developed by Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) is used to measure the severity of osteoarthritis. The range of the KL score is 0–4. Grades 0 through 4 represent normal, doubtful mild, moderate, and severe, respectively. In this work, we classified 3 levels of Osteoarthritis by modifying the KL scoring system. This research identifies grade 0 for normal and doubtful, grade 1 for mild and moderate, and grade 2 for severe. To identify these classes from knee radiograph images, we used a deep-learning architecture namely ResNet-50, and customized it. Using our proposed model, we achieved 97% training accuracy. Clinical researchers will find this research useful in effectively determining the degree of osteoarthritis in the knee.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray images; ResNet50; deep learning; articular cartilage; subchondral bone

title: Segmentation and Classification of Joint Space Narrowing in Rheumatoid Arthritis Using Deep Learning
source: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease, with joint space narrowing (JSN) as a key diagnostic marker. This study presents a deep learning-based approach for classifying JSN severity using X-ray images. Joint regions were segmented using YOLOv5 and bone masks via a fine-tuned Segment Anything Model (SAM). We compared three masking methods, including our proposed Halo Edge Mask (HEM), which applies edge-aware smoothing. HEM outperformed others across all metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, and AUROC. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of AI-assisted JSN assessment in resource-limited settings and support broader applications of AI in musculoskeletal disorders.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; joint space narrowing; X-ray images; joint segmentation; YOLOv5; Segment Anything Model; severity classification; AI-assisted diagnosis; resource-limited settings

title: Automated Detection of Rheumatoid Arthritis in X-Ray Images: An Enhanced and Optimized Deep Learning Framework
source: International Conference on Evolutionary Computing and Mobile Sustainable Networks (ICECMSN)
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a progressive autoimmune disease where by the time it is radiographically diagnosed, irreversible bone erosion and joint deformity has often occurred. To overcome the shortcomings of X-ray detection by a human radiologist, we therefore developed a more sophisticated deep learning approach to automatically identify features of rheumatoid arthritis in hand radiographs. Preprocessing consisted of standardizing all 480 images to 512512 pixels, and contrast enhancement, from a total of 4812 images from 1130 patients. A residual network with a channel-spatial attention mechanism was trained with 3300 images, validated with 812 images, and tested with 700 images. The model achieved a sensitivity of 93.41%, specificity of 92.08% and accuracy of 93.02% outperforming a baseline residual network by 5.17%. These results provide a dependable radiographic inference to guide the initial clinical decision.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; hand radiographs; automated disease detection; bone erosion; joint deformity; ResNet; channel and spatial attention; image preprocessing; contrast enhancement; radiographic diagnosis

title: Radiographic Analysis of Knee Osteoarthritis with Deep Learning: Focus on Joint Space Narrowing and Alignment
source: International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is becoming very common with the increase in obesity and elderly population. In order to anticipate and treat knee osteoarthritis (KOA), many researchers employ artificial intelligence analytics. Most studies are dependent on use of MRI or X-ray. In our study, we suggest using a Dense Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to improve the accuracy of joint space narrowing analysis for knee osteoarthritis identification. This work presents a sophisticated method that makes use of Dense CNN's special capabilities in recognition of the urgent need for an accurate and timely diagnosis of osteoarthritis. The model seeks to capture complex spatial and channel-wise dependencies in knee radiography pictures by decreasing interdependence between layers. This will enhance the model's ability to detect minor changes in the course of osteoarthritis, especially inside the joint space. Based on the experimentation for joint space narrowing, Densent show significant improvement in results. For detection of joint alignment Densenet extracts relevant features from scanogram images and classifies images into Varus, Vulgus and Neutral.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; joint space narrowing; joint alignment; varus deformity; valgus deformity; knee radiography; DenseNet; osteoarthritis detection; radiographic image classification

title: Radiographic knee osteoarthritis detection using liquid neural networks
source: International Conference on Distributed Computing and Electrical Circuits and Electronics (ICDCECE)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a non-traumatic, slowly progressing form of arthritis that affects millions globally. The radiographic assessment of the knee can only be effective if conducted as early as possible, but routine radiographic investigation strategies frequently battle with exactness and consistency. Human diagnosis is subjective based on experience, whereas artificial intelligence (AI) techniques have shown promise, surpassing human diagnosis in some cases. In this research, the field of radiographic knee osteoarthritis detection using AI is being progressed by utilizing Liquid Neural Networks (LNN). CNN, LSTM, cross-breed models combining CNN and LSTM, CNN with bidirectional LSTM (bi-LSTM), and LNN are tested. The models were prepared on a comprehensive radiographic dataset of osteoarthritic knee joints. The LNN model accomplished a classification accuracy of 91.57%, illustrating efficiency in recognizing osteoarthritis-related irregularities. This research highlights that liquid neural networks are an effective tool for radiographic knee osteoarthritis classification.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; radiographic detection; liquid neural networks; X-ray image classification; convolutional neural networks; bidirectional LSTM; CNN-LSTM hybrid model; early diagnosis

title: GoogleNet-Based Classification System for Knee Osteoarthritis Detection in Radiographic Images
source: Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease significantly impacting quality of life, particularly among older populations. This paper presents a sophisticated deep learning-based approach for identifying and categorizing knee OA. Radiographic images were processed with Faster R-CNN for precise localization of pathological features and GoogleNet for classification into four grades of severity. A dataset of 1650 manually annotated grayscale X-rays was used, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 91.9%, with grade-specific accuracies as follows: Grade 1 (90.57%), Grade 2 (90.63%), Grade 3 (93.71%), and Grade 4 (96.11%). The model exhibited high sensitivity across all grades, reaching 93.7% for Grade 3, and specificity values remained strong, peaking at 99.3% for Grade 4. Error rates ranged from 3.89% to 9.43%, while F1 scores demonstrated reliable performance, averaging above 91%. This automated method improves efficiency and lowers diagnostic subjectivity, particularly in advanced cases where the model showed its highest performance. The system's capacity to reduce diagnostic workloads and facilitate individualized treatment plans is highlighted by its telemedicine adaptability and clinical environment scalability. To improve musculoskeletal illness management and increase reliability in real-world applications, future improvements will concentrate on increasing classification accuracy for intermediate grades.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; radiographic image classification; X-ray images; Faster R-CNN; GoogLeNet; automated diagnosis; telemedicine; musculoskeletal disorders

title: Classification and Detection of Knee Osteoarthritis Using X-Ray Images with Machine Learning Algorithms
source: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
abstract: Osteoarthritis of the knee is the utmost dominant usage of arthritis, caused by the degeneration of joint tissues. It is characterized by symptoms such as severe pain and reduced mobility, which can be observed through X-ray imaging. Radiographic evidence often includes narrowing of the joint space, formation of bone spurs (osteophytes), tissue degradation, sclerosis, and structural distortions of the bone. Among imaging techniques, plain radiography (X-ray) is the best cost-effective and broadly accessible method for diagnosing knee osteoarthritis. The Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) classification system provides a systematic approach to assess the severity of knee osteoarthritis by grading X-ray images based on the extent of tissue degeneration. This study aimed to enhance the knee osteoarthritis detection and classification using advanced machine learning techniques like KOA based Random Forest classifiers, to improve the accuracy of the KL grading system. The dataset comprised X-ray images of knee joints, which were divided into training and testing subsets in a 80:20 ratios. The proposed ML based KOA-RF approach achieved an impressive accurateness of 87 percentages, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting and classifying knee osteoarthritis.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; osteoarthritis severity grading; random forest; osteophytes; machine learning diagnosis

title: Automatic Localization of Knee Joint Area in Plain Radiographs using Adaptive Faster RCNN
source: International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Knee joint Osteoarthritis (OA) is a very important reason for the functional limitations and physical illness seen in older people, typically diagnosed from the radiographic assessment. Practitioner evaluation is highly dependent on the experience. Computer-assisted machine learning techniques could enhance the accuracy level of knee joint OA assessment. The initial stage of arthritic knee joint analysis is to locate the knee joint space area region of interest (ROI) automatically in X-ray images. This paper introduces a model for automatic location of knee joint OA based on deep learning approach. Robust and efficient localization of the knee joint task remains a challenge and existing works do not provide satisfactory results. Our aim is to design an effective deep learning driven method to overcome this problem. We trained an adapted deep neural network, namely a faster region convolutional neural network (RCNN) to attain the main objective which is the extraction of the intraarticular knee joint space region from the X-ray images. Results of the proposed improved Faster RCNN based system shows that we obtain a mean average precision of nearly 0.971 indicating the potential use of automatic detection in OA. This proposed work delivers, the best performance on knee joint ROI detection from X-ray images and can be used to quantify the knee joint OA.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; region of interest detection; plain radiographs; Faster R-CNN; computer-aided diagnosis; X-ray image analysis

title: Edge Deployable CORA Net for Real Time Knee Osteoarthritis Monitoring using Variable and Radiographic Data
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive musculoskeletal disorder requiring timely diagnosis and continuous monitoring for effective clinical management. While recent deep learning frameworks such as CORA Net have demonstrated high accuracy and reliability in radiographic KOA grading, their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments remains limited due to computational complexity and lack of real-time capabilities. This paper proposes an Edge Deployable CORA Net (ED-CORA-Net) framework for real-time knee osteoarthritis monitoring by integrating radiographic analysis with wearable sensor data. The proposed system extends the CORA-Net architecture with model compression techniques, including quantization-aware training, structured pruning, and lightweight attention modules, enabling efficient deployment on edge devices such as embedded systems and mobile platforms.Additionally, a multimodal fusion strategy is introduced to combine radiographic features with wearable-derived biomechanical signals (e.g., gait dynamics, joint movement patterns), enhancing early detection and continuous monitoring capabilities. The framework incorporates latency-aware inference optimization and energy-efficient processing to ensure real-time performance under hardware constraints. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that ED-CORA-Net achieves comparable diagnostic performance to the original CORA-Net while reducing inference latency by over 60% and model size by up to 70%. The proposed system enables scalable, cost-effective, and accessible healthcare solutions, particularly in remote and resource-limited settings.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; edge deployment; real-time monitoring; model compression; quantization-aware training; structured pruning; lightweight attention module; wearable sensors; multimodal fusion; radiographic grading; gait analysis; inference latency; energy efficiency; resource-constrained devices

title: A Graph-Driven Approach to Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Classification
source: European Signal Processing Conference (EUSIPCO)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, with diagnosis and management predominantly reliant on radiographic analysis, particularly the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scale. Current deep learning methodologies for the automatic diagnosis of KOA primarily utilize raw X-ray images, which are often compromised by noisy texture artifacts. These artifacts can obscure critical shape cues that clinicians prioritize to determine the KL grading system. In this study, we present a novel morphological approach that emphasizes the geometric structure of the knee joint, thereby simplifying the model's inductive bias and directing training towards meaningful bone shapes. Our method employs the segmentation of input images to automatically extract precise anatomical landmarks on the femur and tibia, utilizing the Segment Anything Model (SAM). These landmarks are represented as nodes within a graph, with edges defined by geometric relationships, such as distances, thereby encoding both local and global structural information of the joint. An EdgeConv-based Graph Neural Network (GNN) classifier is subsequently employed to process this graph representation, effectively capturing interand intra-bone relationships to predict the KL grades of KOA severity. By adopting a graph-centric framework, our approach exhibits inherent invariance to translation, rotation, and scaling, while robustly representing subtle morphological changes that are critical for accurate diagnosis. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first deep learning method that leverages morphological features for KOA assessment. Validation experiments conducted across various KL grade configurations (including all classes,$0-1$, and$0-2$) consistently demonstrate state-of-the-art classification performance.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; severity classification; graph neural networks; Segment Anything Model; morphological features; translation, rotation and scale invariance

title: Comparison of Machine Learning Methods for Predicting Modified Total Shape Score in X-ray Radiography
source: World Automation Congress (WAC)
abstract: It is predicted that there are 600,000 to 1,000,000 patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in Japan. To quantitatively diagnose RA using X-ray images, the modified total sharp score (mTSS) has been used, although, the evaluation method depends on the experience of the physicians. It desires computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems to improve the quality of diagnosis for RA patients. In this study, we compare a method using ridge regression (RR) and methods using 3 models (VGG16, DenseNet201 and Xception) of convolutional neural network (CNN) on mTSS prediction methods for hand rheumatoid arthritis of the hand. To compare the 4 method, we conducted an experiment on 90 RA patients using X-ray images of their hands. The experimental results showed that the mTSS prediction of erosion was best with RR, and the mTSS prediction of JSN was best with VGG16.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; modified total Sharp score; computer-aided diagnosis; radiography; hand radiographs; erosion prediction; joint space narrowing; ridge regression; convolutional neural networks; VGG16; DenseNet201; Xception

title: KneeGradeNet: An EfficientNet-Driven Framework for Automated Multi-Grade Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Assessment from Radiographs
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is one of the common joint conditions which implies joint damage and restricted mobility of the patient. Thus, it becomes crucial to evaluate the severity level of the knee OA in order to solve the problem efficiently. Nevertheless, traditional methods implying evaluation of X-rays manually are inconsistent, biased, and ineffective. The proposed approach utilizes EfficientNet-B3 deep learning technique enhanced with transfer learning. The training of the model is performed on multiclass data set with the help of five levels of Kellgren-Lawrence osteoarthritis severity scale. The results reveal that the accuracy of classification by the proposed method is 92.4%. It should also be mentioned that overfitting problem is not observed during the training and testing phases. In addition, the confusion matrix is seen to have perfect class-wise results. Furthermore, it can be noted that the developed model is highly capable of distinguishing between the various classes, specifically the severe classes, although there are some minor errors made by the model in the intermediate classes.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; radiograph classification; EfficientNetB3; transfer learning; automated severity assessment; X-ray image analysis

title: Categorization of Osteoarthritis Using Vision Transformer for Knee X-Ray Analysis
source: International Conference on Networking and Communications (ICNWC)
abstract: Osteoarthritis(OA)is one of the most common cause of mobility limitations in the world and radiographic evaluation is still the main method used in the clinical evaluation of the disease. In practice, knee radiographs are graded according to the Kellgren Lawrence (KL) scale; however, the grading is subjective, time consuming and difficult to standardize in a clinical setting. In order to close this gap, we designed an automated OA severity classification framework that is based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. The training data used to develop this model and the testing data used to validate the model consisted of 1,525 knee radiographs from open-access sources, including the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI), each of which was classified into KL Grades 0-4. In our experiments, the ViT model was found to better the performance of a ResNet-50 baseline model consistently, with an overall accuracy of 95.2%, and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.886. The reason for this improvement is because the ViT has a patch-based representation and has the ability to capture long-range patterns in the structure with in the joint space more effectively than CNN. These findings suggest that transformer-based architectures can provide a reliable clinical decision support tool providing more objective and reproducible evaluation of OA severity.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; knee radiographs; vision transformer; clinical decision support; Osteoarthritis Initiative; image classification

title: Siamese-Gap Network for Early Detection of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
abstract: Knee OsteoArthritis (OA) is a common musculoskeletal disorder, which causes reduced mobility for seniors. Due to the semi-quantitative nature of the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system, medical practitioners’ grading is subjective, being entirely based on their experience. With the development of computer vision, Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems based on deep learning methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown success in knee OA diagnosis. In this paper, we propose a new approach, the so-called Siamese-GAP Network, for the early detection of knee OA through a KL-grade classification. More precisely, a set of Global Average Pooling (GAP) layers is integrated into the Siamese network used to extract features from each level. The obtained features are then combined to improve the classification performance. Our experimental results on baseline X-ray images from the OsteoArthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset show that the proposed approach presents potential results for the early detection of knee OA.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; early detection; Siamese network; global average pooling; computer-aided diagnosis; X-ray images; multi-level feature fusion

title: Hand X-ray Image Processing System for the early detection of Rheumatoid Arthritis
source: International Conference on Advances in Electrical, Computing, Communication and Sustainable Technologies (ICAECT)
abstract: One of the chronic diseases that has been increasing in each year and is the cause of 60% of morbidity worldwide is rheumatoid arthritis, which has been affecting mostly older people, limiting them to perform some activity due to the strong pain or swelling generated by this disease due to the erosion of the bone in the part of the hand. The treatment of patients in medium or advanced state is based on medications or therapies to relieve pain or delay this disease, in addition to the fact that their diagnosis by the doctor is based on the experience they have when treating patients with this disease through palpation or x-rays that would complicate the patient by misdiagnosing the patient's condition, even worse knowing that this disease is progressive, being worrying. In view of this problem, in this article a hand radiography image processing system was made for the early detection of rheumatoid arthritis, in such a way that the doctor accurately detects the state of this disease to perform the appropriate treatment to the patient and prevent this disease from worsening to the point of causing bone erosion or deformity in the joints of the hand. Through the development of the system, it was observed that it works in the best way and detects with an efficiency of 96.78%, resulting in a reliable and safe system to diagnose rheumatoid arthritis early in patients who have this disease.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; early detection; hand radiography; X-ray image processing; bone erosion; automated disease diagnosis; medical image analysis

title: Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis Pain Severity through A Deep Hybrid Learning Model: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
source: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Knee pain is the most common disabling symptom in osteoarthritis (OA). High correlation between knee pain and multiple OA features is reported in literature, but it has not been validated using deep learning models. In this study, we aim to develop a deep hybrid learning model for pain prediction directly from radiography images. We obtain an optimal hybrid model with VGG16, GAP, and KNN combination that gave a maximum of 89.75% accuracy and 0.91 Cohen’s kappa scores. The pain prediction of our proposed approach has achieved 0.99 of receiver operating characteristic area under curve (ROC-AUC). Binary pain classification has demonstrated better precision-recall curve pattern as compared to 11-class, 4-class, and 3-class pain prediction tasks. Based on Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (GradCAM) analysis, joint center was identified as a key area that significantly contributes to the network’s decision-making process. The results of this study demonstrate the capability of hybrid deep learning model in predicting baseline pain severity from plain radiographs, therefore improving future OA pain assessment efforts.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; radiographic images; hybrid deep learning model; VGG16; k-nearest neighbors; Grad-CAM; Osteoarthritis Initiative
