title: Feasibility Study of a Diffusion-Based Model for Cross-Modal Generation of Knee MRI From X-Ray: Integrating External Radiographic Feature Information
source: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent musculoskeletal disorder, often diagnosed using X-rays due to its cost-effectiveness. While Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides superior soft tissue visualization and serves as a valuable supplementary diagnostic tool, its high cost and limited accessibility significantly restrict its widespread use. To explore the feasibility of bridging this imaging gap, we conducted a feasibility study leveraging a diffusion-based model that uses an X-ray image as conditional input, alongside target depth and additional patient-specific feature information, to generate corresponding MRI sequences. Our findings demonstrate that the MRI volumes generated by our approach are not only visually closer to real MRI scans compared with other methods but also achieve the highest quantitative performance in terms of Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). Furthermore, by increasing the number of inference steps to interpolate between slice depths, we enhance the continuity of the generated volume, achieving higher adjacent slice correlation coefficients. Through ablation studies, we further validate that integrating supplemental patient-specific information, beyond what X-rays alone can provide, enhances the accuracy and clinical relevance of the generated MRI, which underscores the potential of leveraging external patient-specific information to improve the performance of the MRI generation.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; diffusion models; knee MRI; radiological features; medical image synthesis

title: Estimating the severity of knee osteoarthritis using Deep Convolutional Neural Network based on Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization technique
source: International Conference on Engineering & MIS (ICEMIS)
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease that affects larger joints, including the knee, foot, hip, and spine by infecting the cartilage, which causes bones to rub against each other in extreme pain. Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) manual inspections demand a skilled physician to examine the x-ray image. In this paper, a method for detecting the severity of knee osteoarthritis using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) is proposed in order to benefit physicians by examining the X-ray images. Here, the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) technique is used to enhance contrast in images, and this strengthens the current approach. This study presents two models: one for identifying and categorizing normal (KL 0,1) and osteoarthritic results (KL 2, 3, 4). The second model is to assist in distinguishing between severe grades (KL 3, 4) and non-severe grades (KL 2) or normal findings (KL 0,1). For examination, X-ray images from the Knee Osteoarthritis severity grading dataset and the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset are used. Experimental results have demonstrated that the proposed technique achieves accuracy rate of 85.50%, outperforming a number of existing approaches.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; X-ray images; CLAHE; image enhancement; 3D convolutional neural networks; computer-aided diagnosis

title: Evaluation Method of Rheumatoid Arthritis by the X-ray Photograph using Deep Learning
source: IEEE Global Conference on Life Sciences and Technologies (LifeTech)
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is evaluated using the Sharp/van der Heijde scoring system that is currently the most widely used X-ray photograph scoring system. However, it is also difficult for the doctor who is not major in RA cannot evaluate it exactly since this diagnosis relies on implicit knowledge which is difficult to transfer to another person by the text or figures. Therefore, it is desirable to develop a system that enables the condition of RA to be evaluated automatically. Our objective is to develop an automatic evaluation system that is improved by the evaluation and the modification by the doctor in diagnosis in the hospital. This paper proposes the method for the realization of both recognition and classification at the same time using deep learning. And the experiments are performed using X-ray photographs. As a result, we confirm that the effectiveness of the system is verified.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; radiographic scoring; Sharp/van der Heijde score; X-ray images; deep learning; computer-aided diagnosis

title: Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis using Deep Neural Network
source: IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative knee disease that affects the independence, quality of life, and motivation of millions of people. Early detection and accurate prediction of KOA can facilitate timely intervention and improve patient outcomes. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to predicting the onset and progression of knee OA using deep neural networks (DNNs). We use advanced neural network architectures to pull out complex patterns and relationships from the data. This lets the model learn and predict how knee OA will progress. The proposed models are tested and validated on historic data such as X-ray and MRI images. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed DNN-based approach in accurately predicting knee OA outcomes, surpassing traditional methods.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease progression prediction; early detection; deep neural network; X-ray images; MRI images; knee imaging

title: RheumaVIT: transformer-based model for Automated Scoring of Hand Joints in Rheumatoid Arthritis
source: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease that causes chronic inflammation, joint destruction, and extra-articular manifestations. Radiography is the standard imaging modality for diagnosing and monitoring joint damage in RA. However, the commonly used Sharp method and its variants, which evaluate radiographic progression, are time-consuming and subjective. Automated joint evaluation using deep neural networks can address these challenges. This study introduces RheumaVIT, a novel vision transformer-based pipeline for automatically scoring hand joints affected by RA. The method consists of two stages: a regression model for joint localization and a transformer-based architecture for assessing erosion and joint space narrowing (JSN). Our approach demonstrates superior accuracy (up to 12% higher for erosion and 2% higher for JSN) compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, it has a promising ability to detect common patterns of erosion and JSN through roll-out interpretation. To promote further research, we are open-sourcing our clinical collection since there is no annotated dataset on RA available in the public domain. Our paper contributes to the progress of automated joint assessment in rheumatoid arthritis, offering potential applications in both clinical practice and research.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; joint space narrowing; radiographic damage; vision transformer; radiographic interpretation; Sharp score

title: The Role of Convo-Neur-Net in the Assessment of Tibia and Femur Integrity: Allopathic Treatment V/S Ayurvedic Healing Practices
source: International Conference on Communication, Security and Artificial Intelligence (ICCSAI)
abstract: Recent in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have significantly enhanced the classification of knee X-rays, particularly in evaluating osteoarthritis using KL (Kellgren-Lawrence) grading. CNN methodologies utilize deep learning to automatically extract features from X-ray images, allowing for improved accuracy in determining the severity of osteoarthritis. State-of-the-art models, such as ResNet and DenseNet, have been applied to large datasets of annotated knee X-rays, achieving high precision in differentiating between the KL grades. These systems can aid radiologists by providing rapid assessments, thus facilitating timely interventions. Parallel to these technological advances, Ayurvedic treatments continue to play a vital role in managing knee osteoarthritis. Ayurveda emphasizes holistic healing through herbal remedies, dietary modifications, and physical therapies, aiming to alleviate pain and enhance joint function. Research indicates that certain Ayurvedic formulations, such as Ashwagandha and Guggulu, can reduce inflammation and improve mobility in patients with osteoarthritis. Combining CNN methodologies with Ayurvedic treatments presents a promising interdisciplinary approach, where precise imaging and classification tools guide personalized Ayurvedic therapies. This integration may lead to optimized treatment plans that address both immediate symptoms and underlying health conditions, ultimately enhancing patient outcomes in knee joint health.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; convolutional neural networks; Ayurvedic treatment; Withania somnifera; Guggulu; herbal medicine; radiological assessment

title: GEN-AI Multimodel Prediction and Prescriptive Care for Knee Osteoarthritis Progression
source: International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Information and Control Systems (ICOIICS)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is one of the leading sources of musculoskeletal disorders that results in a chronic pain experience for the elderly population, makes them lose their mobility and leads to a lower quality of life. Despite the high prevalence of KOA, clinical practice remains reactive and primarily focuses on symptom control. To close this gap, the project achieves an early detection generative AI-based multimodal prediction and a prescriptive care framework for personalized management of KOA progression. The introduced framework is a fusion of radiographic imaging (X-rays), Electronic Health Records (EHRs), laboratory data, and patient-reported outcomes to provide structural, clinical, and behavioural facets of the disease evolution. The paper leverages deep learning techniques from sophisticated architectures such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based temporal models to capture spatial and sequential patterns for the heterogeneous data. The major novelty is the development of digital twin models serving as patient-specific, dynamic simulations for visualizing disease trajectories and testing the counterfactual “what-if” interventions. The system is equipped with explainable AI modules that deliver simplified information on risk sources and recommended lifestyle or clinical strategies. The fusion of multimodal, generative modelling, and prescriptive intelligence aims to make a radical change in the treatment of KOA by eliminating reactive symptom treatment and thus introducing proactive, preventive, and personalized care leading to the improvement of the patient's outcome and reducing socio-economic burden of osteoarthritis in the long term.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease progression prediction; multimodal fusion; radiography; electronic health records; patient-reported outcomes; digital twin; explainable AI; personalized treatment; early detection; generative AI

title: Implementation of AlexNet for Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is one of the common musculoskeletal disorders and is also called degenerative disease. Accurately diagnosing and treating will slow down the progression of this illness. Knee x-rays and MRI Images are the essential criteria for osteoarthritis. Radiologists and clinicians diagnose the KOA by their experience. However, a huge quantity of x-rays and minor variations between stages place significant pressure on clinicians, causing them to make errors in judgment. Deep learning technology, often known as artificial intelligence (AI), has become a frequent solution to medical problems due to its rapid progress in recent years. An aim of this work is to examine the AlexNet model to classify the severity of KOA and analyzing the performance of the model for this task and comparing this with various models.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; AlexNet; osteoarthritis severity classification; knee radiographs; knee MRI; computer-aided diagnosis; deep learning; model comparison

title: A Simplified Method of Detection and Predicting the Severity of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Computing, Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease caused by the gradual wear and tear of the knee's articulatory cartilage. It is most typically found in adults. It is a progressive illness that can cause impairment if it is not treated or diagnosed in its early stages. This paper presents a simplified approach for detecting and predicting knee osteoarthritis based on the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system using Residual Networks. The baseline of the X-Ray images was obtained from Mendeley Data. The following four approaches are proposed for grading the severity of Knee Osteoarthritis: the first distinguishes severity according to the original KL Grading System, the second distinguishes normal (KL 0-I) from osteoarthritic knees (KL II-IV), the third distinguishes severity as normal (KL 0-I), non-severe (KL II), or severe (KL III-IV), and the fourth distinguishes severity level from KL Grade 0 to KL Grade III. The empirical results showed that the performance improved with fewer multiclass labels being used, with binary class labels and three class labels surpassing all the other models proposed in this paper. The model for binary class labels achieved a 90% accuracy rate and weighted Precision, Recall, and F1 scores of 90%, 90%, and 90%, respectively whereas the model for three classes labels achieved a 90% accuracy rate and weighted Precision, Recall, and F1 scores of 90%, 90%, and 89%, respectively. The proposed models also showed how they might be used to classify patients early in the course of the disease, slowing its progression and raising their quality of life.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; severity prediction; X-ray images; ResNet; computer-aided diagnosis; cartilage degeneration; early disease detection; multi-class classification

title: Deep Learning Approaches for Detecting and Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis Severity
source: International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology for Sustainable Development (ICRAIS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis stands as one of the most prevalent musculoskeletal ailments globally. Its initial signs include joint stiffness, discomfort, and limitations in functionality, marking it as a significant joint disorder. Older adults are more likely to have arthritis, and it normally gets worse with age. If there are no early, effective therapies used, it can lead to impairment in older people. Therapy must be started as soon as possible; otherwise, a full knee replacement may be necessary. The very subjective nature of the standard procedures creates a barrier to early illness progression detection. This study involves in-depth exploration and examination of the application of deep learning techniques for knee osteoarthritis detection and severity prediction. In this work EfficientNet-B6 was chosen for its superior performance in balancing accuracy, speed, and resource efficiency. Unlike models such as MobileNet or ResNet, X-ray images are used to train the model to predict the severity of knee osteoarthritis. The model classifies the data with an accuracy of 87%. A website for OA prediction is developed, the user needs to drag and drop an X-ray image in the dialog box given. The predicted output along with the severity will be shown within a few seconds. This website is very easy to use.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; deep learning classification; knee imaging; web-based prediction tool; early disease detection

title: Effects of Region of Interest Location on Osteoarthritis Detection Using Deep Feature Learning
source: International Conference on Image Processing Theory, Tools and Applications (IPTA)
abstract: Knee OsteoArthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disorder requiring early detection for effective treatment. In this study, using a sequential approach assisted by the BoneFinder algorithm, we propose a method for the early classification of knee OA by examining the impact of several extracted Regions of Interest (ROIs) from the tibial bone. First, the knee joint region is segmented from plain radiography of the knee. Secondly, a sub-contour detection technique is employed to extract distinct sub-regions from the tibial bone. Then, seven specific ROIs are selected on each sub-contour. Thirdly, a Stacked Sparse Autoencoder (SSAE) is employed to extract informative features from the selected ROIs. Finally, the extracted features are then used to train a Support Vector Machine with Radial Basis Function (SVM-RBF) classifier. The proposed ROI extraction as well as the selected SSAE enable improving notably the classification results.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis detection; region of interest selection; tibia; radiography; stacked sparse autoencoder; feature extraction; support vector machine; early diagnosis

title: ICLM: Empirical Evaluation of Rheumatoid Arthritis Disorder using Image Classification and Linear Mapping Principles
source: International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
abstract: Deformity and analysis can occur in the later stages of Rheumatoid Arthritis because joints are eroded like bones. Hand and wrist joints are most commonly impacted in the early stages of this illness, making radio graphs of the hands crucial. Arthritis patients' hand X-ray digital radio graphs have recently been used to evaluate JSW manually because of its inaccuracy and unpredictability across readers. In addition, radiologists have a tough time analyzing hand radio graphs since there are 14 hand joints in all. Computer-aided analysis is necessary to eliminate observer dependence. Image Classification and Linear Mapping Principles (ICLMP) using MATLAB may be used to investigate joint space narrowing, according to our research Active Form Model is used to define bone boundaries in this work, which includes a statistical model of the bone shape and texture. Local linear mapping using textural characteristics identifies joint locations. We've analysed five RA-infected hand radio graphs. 92 percent of joint location estimates are accurate. The use of computerized analysis lessens the demand for highly trained employees. In addition, remote diagnosis and treatment can be accomplished.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; joint space narrowing; computer-aided diagnosis; textural properties; image classification; remote diagnosis

title: Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis Progression from Structural MRI Using Deep Learning
source: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
abstract: Accurate prediction of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) progression from structural MRI has a potential to enhance disease understanding and support clinical trials. Prior art focused on manually designed imaging biomarkers, which may not fully exploit all disease-related information present in MRI scan. In contrast, our method learns relevant representations from raw data end-to-end using Deep Learning, and uses them for progression prediction. The method employs a 2D CNN to process the data slice-wise and aggregate the extracted features using a Transformer. Evaluated on a large cohort (n=4,866), the proposed method outperforms conventional 2D and 3D CNN-based models and achieves average precision of 0.58 ± 0.03 and ROC AUC of 0.78 ± 0.01. This paper sets a baseline on end-to-end KOA progression prediction from structural MRI. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/MIPT-Oulu/OAProgressionMR.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease progression prediction; structural MRI; deep learning; 2D convolutional neural network; transformer models; end-to-end learning; imaging biomarkers

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Prediction Using Machine Learning
source: International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Computer Science for Interdisciplinary Applications (ICETCS)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common disease and the fourth leading cause of disability worldwide. It is the most common type of arthritis and degenerative knee disease that causes pain and limitation of motion, independence, and quality of life for millions of people. It is the most common type of arthritis, with more than 30 million people in the United States and more than 10 million people in Europe, South America, Asia, and the Middle East. Although there is currently no known cure, several biological, pharmacological, and environmental risk factors are thought to play a role in the emergence and advancement of this illness. This increases medical costs and the associated financial burden. Current standard treatments for osteoarthritis, including both pharmacological and symptomatic treatment, have limited effect on function and pain. In this proposed study, we used machine learning to create a model that predicts the risk of knee osteoarthritis. Machine learning techniques such as LSTM and CNN were used to create the models. Our model predicted the risk of knee osteoarthritis with an accuracy of 74%. Using the CNN method with small updates, the accuracy of the proposed model is improved to 96%. These models can be used to identify people at high risk of disease and assist them in taking preventive measures. This result has prompted stakeholders and large organizations to develop accurate models to predict the risk of knee osteoarthritis.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease risk prediction; convolutional neural networks; long short-term memory; degenerative knee disease; risk factors; disease prevention

title: Recent Advancements in Automated Detection and Grade Classification of Ankle Osteoarthritis on Clinical Images
source: International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
abstract: The chronic, progressive degenerative joint disease known as ankle osteoarthritis (AOA) has a major impact on daily activities, movement, and general quality of existence. AOA can cause a comparable level of discomfort and disability to hip or knee osteoarthritis (KOA), despite the fact that it is less frequently reported. To successfully manage signs and slow their course, a precise and prompt diagnosis is essential. Yet conventional diagnostic methods, which are mostly based on radiographic imaging, are frequently insensitive and dependent on subjective interpretation, particularly when the disease is still in its initial phases. Although commonly used, traditional grading schemes like the van Dijk (vD) and Kellgren–Lawrence (KL) scales are constrained by variable evaluation of radiographic characteristics and low interobserver reliability. With an emphasis on both conventional and technologically advanced approaches, this systematic review examines a wide range of studies on the diagnosis and classification of AOA. The study looks at new developments in quantitative radiography analysis, such as completely and semi-automated methods for determining osteophytes, recognizing subchondral alterations, and evaluating joint space width (JSW). Particular attention is paid to image processing programs like MATLAB, which make objective analysis easier by using techniques like segmentation, edge detection, preprocessing, and Euclidean distance calculations. These computational methods offer possible integration into healthcare workflows, improve reproducibility, and lower diagnostic variability. The article emphasizes how crucial it is becoming to combine digital imaging, computer vision, and artificial intelligence (AI) in musculoskeletal diagnostics. It comes to a decision that using quantitative and semi-automated grading methods can greatly increase the clinical relevance, objectivity, and accuracy of AOA assessments, which will ultimately result in improved patient outcomes and more individualized treatment plans.
keywords: ankle osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis grading; automated detection; radiographic evaluation; osteophytes; joint space width; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; computer vision; artificial intelligence; image segmentation; edge detection

title: Quantum-Enhanced Ordinal Deep Learning for Automated Kellgren-Lawrence Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Radiographic severity staging of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL)grading system is a routine yet subjective clinical task, with inter-observer agreement among experienced radiologists rarely exceeding a quadratic weighted kappa (к) of 0.82. Existing automated approaches predominantly treat the five KL grades as unrelated nominal categories through categorical cross-entropy, neglecting the monotonic progression of articular degeneration. Meanwhile, the only hybrid quantum classical network applied to KOA is restricted to binary classification, omitting intermediate grades entirely. This paper presents a dual-branch hybrid architecture that fuses a ConvNeXtBase backbone for localized osteophyte and sclerosis detection with a lightweight global context branch modelling joint-space geometry, unified through learned attentional gating. The fused representation is projected into a four-qubit variational quantum circuit (VQC) via PennyLane, where strongly entangling layers exploit quantum superposition for non-linear feature disentanglement before ordinal classification. The terminal output layer employs the Consistent Rank Logits (CORAL) ordinal regression framework, transforming the five-class task into four rank-consistent binary sub-problems enforcing monotonically decreasing cumulative probabilities. Evaluated on the KneeKL224 dataset under stratified five-fold cross-validation with inverse-frequency class weighting, the pipeline is assessed through quadratic weighted kappa, balanced accuracy, macro F1-score, and per-class precision-recall analysis. Grad-CAM visualizations confirm that the model attends clinically relevant tibiofemoral joint regions.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; ordinal classification; variational quantum circuits; ordinal regression; coral; attentional gating; Grad-CAM

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Grading Using Optimized Deep Learning and LLM-Driven Intelligent AI on Computationally Limited Systems
source: International Conference on Emerging Computational Intelligence (ICECI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is among the musculoskeletal disorders that considerably restrict joint mobility, cause severe chronic pain and impact negatively on quality life. It is one of the persistent health issues worldwide. Generally, subjectivity and inter-observer variability undermine conventional practices and evaluation process that are adopted to address such health issues. Hence precise and timely diagnosis would be one of the effective ways for the assessment of its severity. This paper proposes an automated diagnostic approach for severity grading of KOA by blending a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) with a device-based inference platform powered by TensorFlow Lite. It proposes a model based on the ResNet-18 convolutional neural network. The designed model is trained on publicly available database. Through a transfer learning approach obtained knee images are first classified into five KellgrenLawrence (KL) grades. Further the developed model is optimised. During the training of the model test accuracy of 94.48%. with stable convergence has been achieved. Subsequently the optimised model transformed into a lightweight TensorFlow Lite format, facilitating seamless deployment on resource-constrained devices. The designed model is capable enough to operate in the environment having no continuous internet connectivity. Also, an auxiliary Large Language Model (Gemini-2.0-flash) is applied to generate structured interpretive findings like potential symptoms, risk factors, and preventive majors etc. The LLM component functions as interface without influencing the classification process. The proposed model articulates the feasibility of an ondevice, interpretable decision-support tools for early diagnosis and improve accessibility to Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted knee screening tool.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; severity classification; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; convolutional neural networks; ResNet-18; transfer learning; TensorFlow Lite; model optimization; lightweight deployment; resource-constrained devices; large language models; Gemini; knee radiographs; decision support

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis With Unimodal and Multi-Modal Neural Networks: Data From the Osteoarthritis Initiative
source: IEEE Access
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent musculoskeletal condition affecting millions worldwide, posing significant health and economic burdens. Characterized by the degeneration of joint cartilage, the progression of knee OA varies significantly among individuals, making its prediction a complex issue. Previous studies on automated knee OA diagnosis have primarily relied on unimodal data, often overlooking the valuable information present in multi-modal data. Multi-modal learning, which integrates information from various modalities, is increasingly recognized for its potential to enhance diagnostic performance in medical applications. However, such models incur a higher computational load due to the additional data required. This research investigates the feasibility of multi-modal neural networks in knee OA diagnosis by integrating structural demographic data with unstructured imaging data. Three deep learning unimodal models (InceptionV3, DIKO, and EfficientNetv2) were transformed into multi-modal architectures (MF_InceptionNet, MF_DIKO, and MF_Eff) to compare their diagnostic capabilities. The proposed multi-modal models share a common architecture, with unimodal models acting as image feature extraction backbones and separate embedding layers for demographic data. The image features and demographic embeddings are combined into a unified vector before classification. Extensive experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of these models across different class categories and dataset sizes. MF_DIKO and InceptionV3 emerged as the best multi-modal and unimodal neural networks, respectively, with overall accuracies of 0.67 and 0.75 for 3-class severity classification. Contrary to existing literature, our findings reveal that unimodal neural networks using only imaging features outperform multi-modal networks, suggesting unimodal models might suffice in certain applications.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; automated diagnosis; multimodal neural networks; Osteoarthritis Initiative; knee MRI; osteoarthritis severity classification; InceptionV3; EfficientNetV2; image feature extraction

title: Automatic Detection of Knee Osteoarthritis Severity with SOTA Deep Learning Models and Ordinal Loss
source: Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most common bone diseases that causes pain, stiffness, and limited mobility due to the damage to cartilage. The diagnosis of the disease is made by medical doctors based on the individual's symptoms and findings on X-ray. During this process, different evaluations among medical doctors usually based on experience can make the diagnosis of the disease difficult. In this paper, deep learning models were used for automatic detection of knee OA stages according to the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system in order to facilitate the disease diagnosis process. Pre-trained SOTA deep learning models including ConvNeXt and ConvNeXt V2 are fine tuned using the ordinal loss function. This loss function imposes a penalty, taking into account the distance difference between the real class and the predicted class, in cases where there is a order between the labels, like KL grades that representing OA severity. In this study that we classified the knee OA stage according to KL grades, we obtained the best performances with 73.91% accuracy, 73.77% F1 score and 0.28 mean absolute error (MAE) values on test set obtained on ConvNeXt V2-Tiny and ConvNeXt-Base models that we trained with the ordinal loss function.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; ConvNeXt; ConvNeXt V2; fine-tuning; X-ray image classification; automated diagnosis

title: CNN-Attention Hybrid Models for Efficient and Interpretable Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Assessment
source: International Conference on Computing Technologies (ICOCT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) progresses through worsening stages as a degenerative joint condition which heavily impacts joint mobility along with patient life quality. The standard method of evaluating osteoarthritis severity through radiographic readings uses the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system although manual grading proves inconsistent across different observers. This research design develops an Attention-CNN hybrid model unifying SE-Net self-attention modules with CBAM spatial attention modules to boost the classification of OA severity. The model received training and evaluation through assessment of knee radiographs with KL grades in both the OAI and MOST databases containing numerous images. The proposed model established superior performance metrics compared to ResNet-50 and its counterparts by delivering 88.9% accuracy and 0.87 F1-score alongside 0.95 AUC-ROC rating. The model demonstrates effective attention towards clinically significant features including joint space narrowing and osteophyte formations according to Grad-CAM visualizations which enhances the interpretability of results. Expert radiologist evaluation demonstrated that the model agreed with their interpretations in 91.3% of cases thus helping reduce grading variations. The research illustrates how attention mechanisms boost tedy medical image investigation conducted by CNN networks thus producing better results in identification and making systems more understandable. This proposed method delivers a usable automated system which enables radiologists to perform knee OA severity grading and monitor disease evolution. The researchers plan to investigate Vision Transformers (ViTs) together with multimodal learning methods to boost performance levels and clinical applicability in future work.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; attention mechanism; knee radiographs; Grad-CAM interpretability; joint space narrowing; osteophytes

title: Rheumatoid Arthritis Detection method based on Mask R-CNN
source: China Automation Congress (CAC)
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune rheumatic disease with the feature of joint erosion. The disease mainly occurs in middle age, and women are more susceptible than men. In clinical, radiologists mainly use hand radiographs to observe the appearance of joints to determine the degree of disease. In order to reduce the pressure of long-term repetitive work of radiologists and improve screening efficiency, we propose a detection method based on Mask RCNN. We use an in-house dataset that contains 99 images and is annotated by professional rheumatoid arthritis doctors. Using this method, we can quickly identify the diseased joints from all hand joints and determine their exact positions. This network can automatically detect diseased joints with higher detection accuracy and faster detection speed than other methods.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; hand radiographs; Mask R-CNN; medical image annotation; radiologist workload reduction; disease screening

title: SWE-Net: Sliced-Wasserstein EfficientNet for Learning Discriminative Texture Features in Early Diagnosis of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Image Processing Theory, Tools and Applications (IPTA)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease that affects the cartilage and bone of the knee. Early diagnosis of OA can prevent further joint damage and improve patients' quality of life. In this paper, we propose a novel deep-learning approach for detecting the presence of OA in both the tibia and femur from plain radiographs. First, we used the Fast-SAM model to segment the knee joint areas to study the presence of OA within the femoral and tibial compartments. Then, we introduced a new Sliced-Wasserstein EfficientNet (SWE-Net) to promote discriminability and texture analysis in the feature space of the EfficientNet network. Specifically, we introduced a Sliced Wasserstein Texture (SWT) loss to break down high-dimensional distributions of the feature space into several one-dimensional marginal distributions. With this SWT loss, we capture higher-order statistics representing the texture feature distributions, helping to distinguish between similar classes, such as non-OA and early OA. Comprehensive experimental results over a large public database demonstrate the potential of the proposed network and facilitate a deeper understanding of localized pathological features associated with OA.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; early diagnosis; EfficientNet; texture features; radiographic evaluation; knee joint segmentation; discriminative feature learning

title: Enhanced Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatment Optimization Through Deep Learning
source: International Conference on Disruptive Technologies (ICDT)
abstract: Inflammation and joint destruction are hallmarks of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), a chronic autoimmune condition. To improve patient outcomes, it is essential to optimize treatment plans. According to this research, integrating deep learning (DL) methods into a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) provides a new method to optimize RA treatments. The CNN model is used to decipher intricate medical data, such as imaging and patient records, find trends, and predict how patients react to treatment. To assess the efficacy of the proposed model in predicting ideal treatment methods, it was trained on a large dataset that included patient images and clinical data. The CNN model offers a potential tool for doctors to adapt RA management plans since results show it significantly improves prediction accuracy and treatment personalization. This method allows for data-driven decisions in RA management, improving patient care and enhancing treatment performance.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; treatment optimization; treatment response prediction; convolutional neural networks; personalized medicine; joint destruction; diagnostic imaging; clinical data; data-driven decision support

title: Beyond the Horizon: Exploring Osteoarthritis Predictive Models
source: International Conference on Smart and Intelligent Systems (SISCON)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent chronic rheumatic condition causing pain and disability worldwide, mostly affecting weight-bearing joints like the knees. The diagnosis relies on criteria such as osteophyte development, cartilage loss, and anatomical abnormalities, with primary and secondary classifications based on various factors. Knee OA, in particular, is a important health concern due to its impact on mobility and quality of life. Cartilage degradation plays a crucial role in the progression of OA, leading to stiffness, pain, and reduced joint function. Traditional radiographic techniques, such as X-rays, are generally used for OA diagnosis, with grading systems like the Kellgren-Lawrence scale helping classify disease severity. However, challenges persist in accurately identifying and grading OA, prompting the exploration of advanced technologies like machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). In recent years, DL algorithms have shown promise in automatically diagnosing and tracking OA progression from various imaging modalities, offering personalized risk assessments and guiding treatment decisions. Similarly, ML approaches have demonstrated effectiveness in enhancing OA diagnosis accuracy by leveraging features extracted from knee X-ray images. Hybrid models combining DL, ML, and other techniques have emerged as well, further improving OA detection and classification. This review provides insights into recent advancements in AI-based approaches for knee OA diagnosis, highlighting their potential to revolutionize patient care and outcomes in OA management.
keywords: osteoarthritis; knee osteoarthritis; machine learning; deep learning; computer-aided diagnosis; radiography; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; cartilage degeneration; disease progression; risk prediction; hybrid model; osteophytes

title: Deep Learning on Knee CT Scans from Osteoarthritis Patients for Joint Space Assessment
source: International Conference on Signal-Image Technology & Internet-Based Systems (SITIS)
abstract: Computed tomographic radiography (CT) can be potentially used for knee osteoarthritis (OA) diagnosis and follow up. It is possible to quantify knee joint space three-dimensionally. The main purpose of this study was to investigate an accurate, precise, and memory-saving convolutional neural network to accomplish the segmentation of lateral joint space and medial joint space (LJS and MJS) of knee joints. A novel deep learning structure, based on two state-of-the-art networks — RegNet and DeepLabV3P, was constructed for automatic prediction. And a new attention mechanism called "Feature-Location" module was proposed to be added into the models for comparison. The predictions were post-processed by area opening and alpha shape to get the complete segmentations. From the joint space segmentations, morphological measurements clinically pertinent for knee OA diagnosis and follow up such as the volume, mean thickness, and standard deviation were measured. Finally, compared with the standard U-Net and DeepLabV3P, our new model called "DeepRegY" reduced the memory footprint by more than double. The model also produced the highest Dice coefficients, 0.8378 for LJS and 0.8655 for MJS in the validation set. The morphological parameters showed strong correlations, 0,9356 for volume, 0.99 for mean thickness, and 0.9876 for standard deviation of thickness in the testing set. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean thickness bias about -0.2 mm which is very low compared to the mean thickness results.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; computed tomography; RegNet; attention mechanism; alpha shapes

title: Deep Learning based Knee OsteoArthritis Grade Classification: A Review
source: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
abstract: State-of-the-art methods for knee OsteoArthritis (OA) disease grade classification using Deep learning (DL) based techniques are reviewed in the current work. Early detection-cum-classification of the knee is of substantial learning on X-ray and magnetic resonance (MR) images. Further classification allows estimating the great civility which is utilized for accessing the disease progression topics in the scope including various data set experiments and the performance evaluation metrics. The purpose of the current work is to introduce the methods in the field and highlight the shortcomings to be addressed as potential considerations in clinical practices the need for better preprocessing techniques and experimentation on the classification model is summarized at the end. Furthermore, the review concludes the published work in terms of highest performance and future work in the direction of improving classification accuracy.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; deep learning; X-ray images; magnetic resonance imaging; early detection; image preprocessing; disease progression

title: Texture Analysis in MRI of the Knee for an Early Diagnosis of Osteoarthritis
source: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
abstract: Osteoarthritis is one of the most disabling diseases in developed countries. Its etiology is not firmly established, and the diagnosis is made by observing radiographs, assigning a degree of severity based on the information displayed. For this reason, the diagnosis is usually late and determined by the subjectivity of the doctor, which implies a restriction of the treatment. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has allowed us to see in greater detail the alterations produced in soft joint structures. In this work, biomarkers for an early diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis have been developed by means of textures analysis on MRI. For this purpose, 50 subjects underwent T1-weighted MR image acquisitions: 25 controls and 25 diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis between grades I and III. Six regions were segmented on these images, corresponding to the femorotibial cartilage, femoral condyles, and tibial plateau. 43 textures were extracted for each region of interest (ROI) employing 5 statistical methods and 5 different predictive models were trained and compared. In addition, a study of the thickness of the cartilage was carried out to make a comparison with the texture analysis. The best result has been obtained using a K-nearest neighbor model with the combination of 33 textures (maximum value of AUC = 0.7684). Furthermore, in the analysis of the cartilage thickness, no statistically significant differences were found. Finally, it is concluded that the texture analysis has great potential for the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis. Clinical Relevance - The current study establishes a methodology for an early diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis by means of MRI-based texture analysis, in a fast and objective manner.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; early diagnosis; texture analysis; MRI biomarkers; T1-weighted imaging; femorotibial cartilage; cartilage thickness; femoral condyle; tibial plateau; k-nearest neighbors; cartilage degeneration

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Detection Using an Improved CenterNet With Pixel-Wise Voting Scheme
source: International BIT Conference (BITCON)
abstract: The primary objective of the project is to identify and diagnose knee osteoarthritis using knee images obtained through X-ray scans. X-ray images are a common and cost-effective modality for examining knee joint health, and the project focuses on leveraging these images for accurate detection of osteoarthritis. Current methods for knee osteoarthritis detection, which rely on image processing techniques, face challenges in terms of accuracy and precision. This technique involves the development of a specialized Center Net,A state-of-the-art object detection architecture. This Center Net is tailored with a pixelwise voting scheme, a, method that allows for the extraction of the features at a granular level. By customizing the Center Net in this way, the project aim to enhance the accuracy and reliability of knee osteoarthritis detection the model incorporates Dense Net 201 as a basic network for future extraction. By utilizing DenseNet201, the model aims to capture the most representative features for knee samples,enhancing the robustness of the feature extraction process.
keywords: CenterNet; X-ray images; DenseNet201; object detection; feature extraction; medical image analysis

title: Explainable Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis Using a Hybrid Vision Transformer–CNN Model with Grad-CAM Visualization
source: International Conference on Advancement in Futuristic Technologies (ICAFT)
abstract: The early and precise identification of the knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is crucial in preventing irreparable cartilage loss and functional disability. The proposed paper uses a hybrid architecture as Vision Transformer-Convolutional Neural Network (ViT-CNN) architecture of automatic classification of KOA severity based on radiographic images and combines deep feature learning with model interpretability using Grad-CAM visualization. CNN module scales capture local morphological evidence including osteophyte margins and joint-space texture, whereas ViT encoder scales patterns reflect global relationships between knee joint structures. The proposed system was tested on top of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset (4,500 X-ray images) annotated with Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scores (0-4) and achieved an overall accuracy of 95.4, a macro-F1 of 0.94, a precision of 0.95, and a recall of 0.94 as compared to the standalone ResNet-50 (90.1%) and ViT-Base (92.7%) models. The micro-AUC (0.984) and macro-AUC (0.978) values validate the presence of extremely good class separability with five-fold cross-validation producing a mean accuracy of 94.9 +- 0.3% with Cohen k = 0.93 which is a very high level of agreement with grading of an expert radiologist (p < 0.01). Grad-CAM heatmaps always localized regions of clinical relevance such as medial tibiofemur joint space and subchondral bone plate, which made them more trustworthy and transparent. The proposed ViT-CNN framework provides a 5-9% increase compared to the earlier CNN-only methods (86-90% accuracy) at the same time being interpretable. In general, the approach provides statistically and anatomically significant KOA classification and identifies a stable basis of AI-aided diagnostic systems within the field of musculoskeletal radiology.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; radiographic images; X-ray images; vision transformer; Grad-CAM; explainable AI; model interpretability; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; Osteoarthritis Initiative; osteophytes; joint space; subchondral bone plate; musculoskeletal radiology; computer-aided diagnosis

title: Multiview Radiographic Osteoarthritic Anomaly Detection Utilizing Enhanced Liquid Neural Network Architectures and Advanced Computational Imaging Techniques
source: International Conference on Advances in Modern Age Technologies for Health and Engineering Science (AMATHE)
abstract: In this digital era, Osteoarthritis (OA) could be a predominant degenerative joint clutter that altogether impacts the quality of life for millions around the world. Early location and exact conclusion are significant for compelling treatment, but routine radiographic investigation strategies frequently battle with exactness and consistency. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to Multiview Radiographic Osteoarthritic Irregularity Location by utilizing improved profound learning models and progressed computational imaging procedures. Our strategy consolidates Convolutional Neural Systems (CNN), Long Short- Term Memory (LSTM) systems, cross breed models combining CNN and LSTM, CNN with bidirectional LSTM (biLSTM), and LNN (Liquid Neural Network) with simple RNN layers. The models were trained on a comprehensive multiview radio- graphic dataset of osteoarthritic knee joints. Among the designs tried, LNN beated others, accomplishing the most noteworthy classification exactness of 91 percent, illustrating predominant include extraction and learning capacity in recognizing $O A$ related irregularities. The integration of progressed computational imaging and productive profound learning systems appears guarantee in progressing demonstrative exactness, clearing the way for mechanized and vigorous OA location frameworks in clinical settings. Our discoveries highlight the potential of LNN (Liquid Neural Network) as a state-of-the-art arrangement for radiographic peculiarity location, with critical suggestions for both demonstrative viability and persistent care
keywords: osteoarthritis; knee joint; radiographic image analysis; liquid neural networks; CNN-LSTM hybrid model; bidirectional LSTM; early diagnosis; computational imaging

title: Prediction of severity of Knee Osteoarthritis on X-ray images using deep learning
source: IEEE North Karnataka Subsection Flagship International Conference (NKCon)
abstract: The most prevalent kind of arthritis is osteoarthritis (OA). Radiologists use to employ the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system to identify the aggressiveness of OA based on the information shown on the pair of knee joints. Computer-assisted strategies have recently been proposed to enhance the accuracy of OA diagnosis. Previous semiautomatic segmentation approaches, on the other hand, required human interaction, limiting their use on huge datasets. Furthermore, CNN is used to quantify OA rigorousness to investigate the relationships among distinct local regions. SSD reduces human interaction and provides a back-to-back approach to computerized osteoarthritis detection by incorporating the object detection model. The rating is based on X-ray scans from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset. At the cost of training on a huge dataset with over 8260 knee joint samples, our method accurately segments 96.37% of data.

title: Application of Vision-Language Models for Assessing Osteoarthritis
source: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) poses a global health challenge, demanding precise diagnostic methods. Current radiographic assessments are time-consuming and prone to variability, prompting the need for automated solutions. The existing deep learning models for OA assessment are unimodal single-task systems and they don't incorporate relevant text information such as patient demographics, disease history, or physician reports. This study investigates employing Vision-Language Processing (VLP) models to predict OA severity using X-ray images and corresponding reports. Our method leverages X-ray images of the knee and diverse report templates generated from tabular OA scoring values to train a CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training) style VLP model. Furthermore, we incorporate additional contrasting captions to enforce the model to discriminate between positive and negative reports. Results demonstrate the efficacy of these models in learning text-image representations and their contextual relationships, showcase potential advancement in OA assessment, and establish a foundation for specialized vision-language models in medical contexts.
keywords: osteoarthritis; vision-language models; CLIP; X-ray images; knee radiography; radiology reports; multimodal learning; automated diagnosis

title: Wavelet-Enhanced Transformer for Automated Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Classification
source: IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics, Cognition and Machine Learning Applications (ICCCMLA)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease that requires accurate radiographic assessment for effective clinical management. This study introduces a wavelet-enhanced Swin Transformer for automated KOA severity classification from X-ray images. The method integrates discrete wavelet transform (DWT) with the hierarchical attention of Swin Transformers to capture both multi-scale texture patterns and global contextual features. Specifically, Daubechies-4 wavelet decomposition extracts texture features that are concatenated with RGB channels, forming a 7-channel input to a modified Swin Transformer backbone. Experiments on the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset comprising 7,260 knee X-rays use clinically relevant severity groupings (healthy, moderate, severe). The proposed model achieves 95.23% test accuracy, surpassing the baseline Swin Transformer (94.44%), with AUCs of 0.99, 0.98, and 1.00 for healthy, moderate, and severe cases, respectively. These results establish a new benchmark for KOA grading and underscore the clinical utility of hybrid wavelet-transformer architectures in medical imaging.

title: AP-DPM: A Dual-Path Merging Network Via Adversarial Anatomical Prior Guidance for Wrist Bone Segmentation
source: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of wrist bones from conventional radiographs remains a significant challenge due to severe anatomical overlap and blurred bone boundaries, particularly in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. To address these issues, we propose AP-DPM, a novel Dual-Path Prior-constrained Merging model with adversarial anatomical priors. AP-DPM employs a dual-path architecture to separately predict complete bone masks and overlapping regions, which are subsequently integrated through a residual merging network. To enhance anatomical plausibility, we incorporate an adversarial prior guided by a pre-trained discriminator. Extensive experiments on the publicly available RAM-W600 dataset demonstrate that AP-DPM outperforms state-of-the-art methods across seven quantitative metrics, achieving superior performance particularly in diagnostically critical overlapping regions. Ablation studies further validate that both the dualpath structure for enhanced focusing on overlap regions and the adversarial anatomical prior contribute significantly to performance gains, enhancing local boundary sensitivity and global structural consistency. These results highlight the potential of AP-DPM to improve automated radiographic assessment of rheumatoid arthritis progression. Code is available at https://github.com/YSongxiao/AP-DPM
keywords: X-ray images; dual-path network; rheumatoid arthritis

title: Interpretation of KOA by KL Grading System using Deep Learning
source: International Conference on Communications and Signal Processing (ICCSP)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis poses a significant global health challenge, often diagnosed using conventional radiographic grading systems such as the Kellgren-Lawrence scale, which primarily rely on X-ray images and may result in delayed diagnosis. Recent efforts to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency have turned to deep learning methods, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNN). In this study, we examined eight adaptive neural network models that utilize CNN for knee osteoarthritis detection. These models were trained and validated on a substantial dataset of knee $\mathbf{X}$-rays and underwent thorough evaluation to assess their capability in classifying knee osteoarthritis severity. Our results demonstrate that the top-performing model achieved an impressive accuracy of 98.73 %, outperforming its counterparts. This research highlights the potential of deep learning models, specifically CNN, in enhancing the precision and speed of knee osteoarthritis diagnosis.

title: Automated Hand Osteoarthritis Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
source: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common form of arthritis and often occurs in joints such as the knees, hips, and hands. Given there is no cure for OA, early detection and prevention are required to avoid further damage to the joint. Typically, joints are given a Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grade of 0 to 4 with KL ≤ 1 meaning non-OA and KL ≥ 2 being positive for OA. Overall hand OA is determined by a positive OA rating of a joint on more than one finger. Therefore, to detect hand OA, one needs to detect worrisome hand joints first. This study uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) and proposes a custom architecture to automatically classify joints from hand X-rays into 5 KL categories as well as 2 categories of non-OA/OA. Post-processing is used to determine overall hand OA. Using a dataset of 3,556 hand X-rays, our custom CNN architecture was able to achieve a 5-category finger joint classification accuracy of 82.7% with a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.61. For 2-category classification, our model achieved an accuracy of 92.9% with an MCC of 0.74 and an area under the curve (AUC) score of 0.965. Based on the joint-level classification results of each hand, our model achieved an accuracy of 88.6% to classify the hand-level OA, i.e., to distinguish hand X-rays with and without OA. To our knowledge, this is the first work that uses CNN to classify hand joints into KL grades and detect overall hand OA based on individual hand joints.
keywords: hand osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; hand radiographs; osteoarthritis detection; convolutional neural network architecture

title: Deep Learning-based Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis Severity: Enhancing Diagnostic Precision and Efficiency
source: International Conference on Innovative Data Communication Technologies and Application (ICIDCA)
abstract: Radiologists have historically used the Kellgren–Lawrence (KL) system, which is based on visual evaluation of knee X-rays, to grade osteoarthritis (OA), the most prevalent type of arthritis. This manual method, however, is subject to subjectivity and diagnostic variability. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used in a novel deep learning-based system to automatically classify knee OA severity from X-ray images into five KL grades (0–4) in order to address this issue. The customized KneeNet model performed exceptionally well after being trained on a sizable, annotated dataset, attaining 94.16% accuracy, 0.9265 recall, 0.9458 precision, and a 0.9361 F1 score. These outcomes greatly surpass those of conventional techniques. The model provides standardized, effective OA diagnosis and is a good candidate for clinical integration due to its accuracy and scalability. This AI-powered system facilitates better patient care and individualized treatment planning for knee osteoarthritis by facilitating early detection and precise grading.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray images; convolutional neural networks; automated image classification; computer-aided diagnosis; diagnostic variability

title: Cascading Residual Graph Convolutional Networks for Knee Osteoarthritis Prediction and Classification from X-Ray Images
source: International Conference on Innovative Data Communication Technologies and Application (ICIDCA)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a widespread degenerative joint disease where early and precise classification is vital for effective treatment. Traditional deep learning methods for OA detection often exhibit limited accuracy and high error rates, hindering clinical reliability. To overcome these challenges, this study presents an innovative framework consisting of a Cascading Residual Graph Convolutional Network (CRGCN) and Zebra Optimization Algorithm (ZOA) to ensure more accurate prediction and classification of knee OA. First, the image pre-processing step is performed using Adaptive and Propagated Mesh Filtering (APMF) on standardized knee X-rays from the OAI dataset. This method efficiently removes noise and still preserves joint features such as narrowing of space between joints and osteophyte growth. Next, segmentation is performed using the Attention Aggregation Feature Pyramid Network (A2-FPN), leveraging multi-scale feature extraction and a linear attention mechanism to accurately delineate knee joint regions. Feature extraction utilizes the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to capture key spatial and frequency domain patterns indicative of osteoarthritic changes. For classification, Cascading Residual Graph Convolutional Network (CRGCN) models complex interactions between imaging and clinical data through residual blocks and graph-based neighborhood aggregation, enabling robust diagnosis across OA severity stages. Parameter optimization is enhanced by Zebra Optimization Algorithm (ZOA), a metaheuristic inspired by zebra herding behavior, which balances exploration and exploitation to improve model convergence and reduce errors. The CRGCN-ZOA framework is shown to perform better than existing models, achieving 98.7% accuracy, 98.6% precision and less than a 0.2% error rate. The convergence in training and validation curves and the high performance of ROC-AUC scores all confirm strong performance for different OA severity levels. Overall, this integrated approach shows significant promise for supporting timely and personalized clinical decision-making in knee osteoarthritis diagnosis and staging.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; X-ray images; graph convolutional networks; residual graph convolutional network; zebra optimization algorithm; image denoising; joint segmentation; short-time Fourier transform; metaheuristic optimization

title: Deep Learning with 3D CNN for Knee Osteoarthritis Detection and Classification
source: International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Of all joints, the knee is the most commonly afflicted with osteoarthritis (OA), which is the most common form of arthritis. Even though CNNs are seriously being utilized in medical imaging, 3D CNNs are yet to be applied as a standard for diagnosing knee OA. In this, the 3D CNN model was applied on the knee MRI sequences to classify the presence of osteoarthritis (OA). Probably the strongest point of 3D CNNs over 2D CNNs is that 3D CNNs can process the whole MRI sequence in one go, while 2D CNNs can only analyze a single photograph. In this, the KL grading ranking the intensity of OA from 0 to 4 was used for each one of the knees based on MRI data taken. The result showed that the 3D CNN model could differentiate the OA and non-OA knees well both in test and validation phases. Another model used for comparison is a 2D CNN model that uses X-ray images. Although much less accurate than the 3D CNN on MRI data, this model was also able to be used quite well. Thus, the diagnosis of knee OA is much more accurate by the method combining MRI and 3D CNN technology as compared to just with X-ray imaging, although both of these models have some clinical values. The work concludes by depicting how 3D CNN can be useful in the detection of OA through complex sequences of MRI images compared to traditional 2D methods.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; 3D convolutional neural networks; knee MRI; osteoarthritis grading; computer-aided diagnosis; X-ray images; medical image classification

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Based X- Ray Images Detection and Classification Using RCNN
source: International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Osteoarthritis is the most common disease that affects joints, and its presentation mainly occurs among the aged population. Although an appropriate diagnosis of OA has been determinant in avoiding drastic progression in joint deterioration, the presently available radiographic methods depend on personal judgment. This paper proposes a deep learning-based CNN model for the automatic detection and classification of OA stages from knee X-ray images. The model was trained and tested on the OAI dataset and achieved a satisfactory accuracy of 99%. Advanced image preprocessing techniques, such as contrast enhancement and knee joint segmentation, were used to optimize the performance of the model. Extensive evaluation metrics, such as confusion matrices and ROC curves, confirmed the robustness of the proposed model. The results suggest the promise of AI systems in reinforcing clinical decision-making processes, especially in the early detection of OA. We also present ethical considerations within the applications of AI to healthcare, discussing future research directions.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; R-CNN; knee joint segmentation; contrast enhancement; automated diagnosis; early detection; clinical decision support; ethics of AI in healthcare

title: Minimal Knee Joint Space Width Detection in Digital X-Ray Images using Deep Learning
source: International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of a deep learning-driven method to locate minimal knee joint space width area (KJSW) and see how successfully a deep learning approach can locate mKJSW area from digital x-ray images. In 1848 knee data (digital X-ray images), I used 1752 data (X-ray images) for the study. This proposed method compares the KJSW area in lateral and medial sides, and detect the mKJSW area. Faster RCNN architecture and incorporate VGG -16 with transfer learning are trained to extract the image features to locate the mKJSW area in the digital knee joint X-ray images. The proposed approach located the mKJSW region with a localization accuracy of 98.6 %, indicating the potential use of mKJSW area detection. We have presented the automated deep learning approach to locate the mKJSW area. In addition to that, our proposed deep learning approach trained on both femur and tibial bone region from knee Anterior-Posterior (AP) view digital X-ray images perform better at locating mKJSW area than the reference model. The proposed approach will be used to evaluate knee joint OA and pain assessment.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; knee radiography; Faster R-CNN; object detection; femur and tibia

title: Detection and Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis Using Convolutional Neural Network
source: International Conference on Advanced Research in Computing (ICARC)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease that significantly impacts the quality of life for millions of individuals worldwide. Early and accurate detection of KOA is crucial for timely intervention and effective management of the disease. This study propose a deep learning model to enhance the accuracy and cost-effectiveness of KOA detection using X-ray images. Initially this study evaluate the performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for the detection and classification of KOA using X-ray images. The CNN model will be trained on a large dataset of knee X-ray images, annotated by expert radiologists, to learn the patterns and features indicative of KOA. Then analyze the impact of different image preprocessing techniques and hyper-parameters on the performance of the CNN model. By systematically exploring various preprocessing methods, such as image normalization, filtering, and enhancement, along with hyper-parameter tuning. Finally develop a web interface that allows individuals to conveniently upload their knee X-ray images and receive a quick and accurate prediction of having KOA. Furthermore, insights gained from the analysis of image preprocessing techniques and hyper-parameters will contribute to the optimization of KOA detection systems. Overall, this research study aims to advance the field of KOA detection by harnessing the power of deep learning and developing a practical tool for screening and assessment. Especially this study achieves the accountable amount of accuracy as 89%. The proposed model and web interface have the potential to improve healthcare outcomes by enabling timely diagnosis and intervention, ultimately enhancing the management of KOA and improving the quality of life for affected individuals.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis detection; X-ray images; convolutional neural networks; image classification; image preprocessing; hyperparameter optimization; web-based diagnostic tool; radiographic screening

title: Privacy-Preserving Knee Osteoarthritis Classification: A Federated Learning Approach with GradCAM Visualization
source: International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) poses a significant global health challenge, impacting a substantial population. The conventional detection process involves multiple tests and meticulous examination by experienced physicians, which is time-consuming and susceptible to misclassification due to subtle variations in X-ray images. Additionally, privacy concerns hinder the sharing of sensitive data like X-rays. This study employs Federated Learning with pre-trained architectures (DenseNet-169, Inception-v2, and MobileNet-v2) to classify three KOA severity grades, utilizing two clients to ensure data privacy. The aim is to develop a generalized model for disease classification, improving efficiency while ensuring the confidentiality of patient information. DenseNet-169 excelled with an F1 score of 81% and an accuracy of 82%, while Inception-v2 and MobileNet-v2 performed well with slight F1 score variations. Moreover, the exploration of GradCAM visualization techniques is conducted to improve interpretability, highlighting the capability of this approach to effectively tackle the intricate challenges linked to Knee Osteoarthritis detection.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; federated learning; privacy-preserving machine learning; Grad-CAM; X-ray image classification; osteoarthritis severity grading; DenseNet169; Inception V2; MobileNetV2; model interpretability; pre-trained convolutional neural networks

title: Automated Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Classification Using ResNet: A Deep Learning Approach for X-ray Analysis
source: International Conference on Augmented Reality, Intelligent Systems, and Industrial Automation (ARIIA)
abstract: In this work, the ResNet-based CNN was applied to the classification of knee OA using X-ray images. Osteoarthritis is a crippling degenerative joint disease that affects millions worldwide; hence, the importance of early diagnosis for effective management. A total number of 1,656 knee X-rays were utilized in order to train the ResNet model, which represents grades from 0-a healthy one-to 4-severe osteoarthritis. The classification was performed according to clinical criteria that define the development of osteoarthritis by characteristic radiological features, including narrowing of joint space and formation of osteophytes. Overall accuracy for the model performance on the test set at sight is 94.57%. The classification report emphasizes mostly excellent performance over most grades. In Grade 0, which means healthy knees, the precision is 0.99, recall is 0.93, and F1-score is 0.96. This was done with Grades 1, 2, and 3, which returned F1-scores of 0.96, 0.95, and 0.94, respectively. In Grade 4, that is, severe OA, the performance was far worse, with a precision of 0.66 and an F1-score of 0.77, although this can be expected given to the smallest sample size in this category. These results further develop the conclusion that ResNet performs effective automation of knee osteoarthritis classification based on X-ray images with strong accuracy and robustness for most of the severity grades. This approach is a potentially useful tool to help diagnose and monitor osteoarthritis, especially in resource settings where access to expert radiological assessment is limited.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; X-ray images; ResNet; convolutional neural networks; automated diagnosis; joint space narrowing; osteophytes; radiological features; resource-limited settings

title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models for the Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis in X-Ray Images
source: International Conference on Mechatronics Engineering (ICOM)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative j oint disease that causes significant pain and disability. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective management, traditionally relying on manual assessment of X-ray images by medical experts. This manual approach can be time-consuming and subject to variability. Recent advancements in deep learning offer promising automated solutions for knee OA diagnosis from X-ray images. This study evaluates and compares the performance of three state-of-the-art deep learning models - Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), ResNet-50, and DenseNet-121 - for the classification of knee osteoarthritis using X-ray images. A comprehensive dataset of 10,930 knee X-ray images, labeled as normal or osteoarthritis, was utilized for training and testing the models. Rigorous hyperparameter tuning and optimization were performed to achieve optimal performance. The results demonstrate that the CNN model consistently outperformed the ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 models across various evaluation metrics, including overall accuracy (97.01%), precision (95.94%), recall (98.97%), specificity (95.85%), and F1 score (96.98%). The CNN model exhibited superior capability in distinguishing between normal and osteoarthritis knees, attributed to its ability to effectively learn hierarchical features and its relatively simpler architecture.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; automated diagnosis; convolutional neural networks; ResNet50; DenseNet121; model comparison; radiographic classification; osteoarthritis

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Prediction Using Deep Learning

The ability to detect knee OA early and accurately can lead to proactive measures and individualized treatment plans. CNNs and the VGG model are two examples of Models of deep learning that recently displayed notable performance in a range of image recognition applications. The goal of this research paper is to use CNN and the VGG architecture to create a knee osteoarthritis model for prediction. The suggested method involves a sizable dataset of knee radiography images to train a CNN model, specifically the VGG model.

title: Automated Knee OA Severity Prediction via CNNAttention Hybrid Framework
source: International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) shows degenerative joint disease progression that affects mobility and quality of life forcefully. Manual severity grading methods based on radiographic images present problems due to inconsistent results across different observers as well as for individual observers across multiple evaluations. The study introduces a hybrid model that uses both convolutional neural networks to extract image features combined with attention mechanisms to increase interpretability to automate grading of KOA severity levels. This model implements multi-scale feature fusion as a technique for KOA classification which enables capture of important local details and global patterns. The study used radiographic image data from both OAI and MOST datasets which included more than 10,000 images annotated with KL grades. Comparison results showed that the proposed model achieved 92.3% accuracy beating both ResNet50 at 85.7% and DenseNet121 at 87.3%. The performance metrics of precision at 0.93 with recall at 0.91 and F1-score at 0.92 demonstrate strong classification results throughout KOA severity levels. Based on Cohen's kappa calculations the model secured a score of 0.87 which shows substantial agreement with expert annotations. Attention heatmaps from qualitative analysis displayed that the model correctly identifies important areas such as joint space narrowing and osteophytes, which increases its interpretability for clinical use. The newly suggested automated method offers reliable solutions to assess KOA severity grades which reduces human bias in interpretation and supports clinicians during their evaluation process. Ongoing research will investigate the use of multi-modal imaging data combined with real-time clinical deployment capabilities.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; radiographic images; automated severity assessment; convolutional neural networks; attention mechanism; multi-scale feature fusion; interpretability; attention heatmaps; joint space narrowing; osteophytes
