title: A Deep Learning Framework for Diagnosing and Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks
source: International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative disorder that significantly impacts mobility and diminishes the overall quality of life, particularly in individuals who are obese. The disease progression is exacerbated by inflammatory processes involving cytokines and metabolic factors. The irreversible damage caused by KOA often leads to the necessity for total knee replacement (TKR), a procedure that is expensive and has a limited lifespan. Current diagnostic methods heavily rely on manual segmentation and annotation of X-ray images, which are labor-intensive and prone to observer variability. This research proposes a deep learning framework that employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to automate the classification of knee X-ray images, enhancing the early and accurate detection of KOA. The Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading scale is the most widely accepted method for predicting the severity of KOA based on radiographic evidence from knee X-rays. The dataset utilized in this study comprises $\mathbf{1, 8 0 0}$ digital X-ray images obtained from the global hospitals and diagnostic centers, captured using the PROTEC PRS 500E X-ray machine. Our CNN model achieved a high diagnostic accuracy, demonstrating its potential for practical clinical use. The CNN model undergoes extensive training and validation to achieve high diagnostic accuracy, followed by its integration into a webbased application developed with the Flask framework. This deep learning framework employing CNN frameworks enhances the accuracy of diagnosing and classifying knee osteoarthritis severity, improving early detection, clinical efficiency, and patient outcomes.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray image classification; automated diagnosis; convolutional neural networks; web-based diagnostic tool; early detection

title: Bridging Clinical Expertise and AI: Deep Learning for Automated Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis
source: Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis affects the knee sections, and its severity gets worse over the course of 10 to 15 years. Knee osteoarthritis makes it tougher for older people to stay active and do what they need to do. The skill level of doctors has a big effect on how they analyze visual exams. Finding problems early on requires methods that provide quick operation and accurate detection while yet being cost- effective. Deep learning (DL) uses convolutional neural networks (CNN) to find the best way to diagnose knee osteoarthritis. Convolutional neural networks need a lot of input data to learn. An automated X-ray analysis that uses deep learning technology makes it easier to extract features and shortens the time it takes to train models. Researchers have found that a deep learning system that uses a trained VGG16 network on five-class knee X-rays can use SoftMax to accurately tell the difference between normal, questionable, mild, moderate, and serious issues. Two deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used by an automated system to grade patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA) using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) criteria. The study included 1650 different knee X-ray scans, which were split into two separate groups. The dataset has 514 normal cases, 477 questionable cases, 232 mild cases, 221 moderate cases, and 206 severe cases of knee osteoarthritis. The suggested model for finding knee osteoarthritis (OA) using X-ray radiographs has a classification accuracy of over 95%. The training results were 95% accurate, and the validation results were 87% accurate.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; automated diagnosis; convolutional neural networks; VGG16; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; osteoarthritis severity grading; medical image classification; early detection

title: Deep Learning for Knee Osteoporosis Classification: Leveraging Inception-ResNet-v2 for Accurate X-ray Analysis
source: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)
abstract: An investigation of deep learning techniques reveals its potential to classify knee osteoporosis through analysis of X-ray images. A total of 190 images were obtained from Kaggle, with 36 Normal images and 154 osteopenia images. The researchers used Inception-ResNet-v2, which received ImageNet training and subsequently underwent further specialization for X-ray knee classification. The researchers applied data augmentation together with a weighted loss function to resolve imbalanced data classes. The images were pre-processed by resizing to 299x299 pixels, normalizing pixel values, and splitting the dataset into training, validation, and test sets with an 80:10:10 ratio. Evaluation results showed that the model achieved 91.26% accuracy for training data, yet reached 93.02% accuracy for validating data. The model expressed its power for differentiating Normal and osteopenia cases through a confusion matrix and classification report, which demonstrated 87% global accuracy. Future development of the model can happen via larger training data sets, together with a hybrid architectural research design that will enhance both generalization power and accuracy measurements.
keywords: osteopenia; X-ray image classification; InceptionResNetV2; transfer learning; class imbalance; weighted loss function; data augmentation; bone mineral density

title: Enhancing Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Classification using Improved Efficientnet
source: IEEE Uttar Pradesh Section International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (UPCON)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA), caused by the gradual degradation of joints resulting in discomfort and limited mobility, poses a significant healthcare challenge, emphasizing the importance of early detection for effective management. In this study, we present an improved EfficientNet-B0 based approach aimed at enhancing the accuracy of osteoarthritis (OA) severity classification. On publicly available dataset, the proposed model resulted in an accuracy rate of 69.74% which is better to other cutting-edge approaches.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; EfficientNetB0; early detection; medical image classification

title: A Sophisticated Method for X-Ray Image-Based Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis Utilising Moblienetv3 Large
source: Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: A common deteriorating joint condition that impacts millions of individuals worldwide is osteoarthritis. For optimal care and avoidance of its development, early and accurate identification is essential. Algorithms utilizing deep learning are currently showing promising outcomes in medical image analysis applications, such as disease categorization. Through the use of the MobileNetV3 architecture, a compact and effective convolutional neural network (CNN) created for deployment on devices with limited resources, such as smartphones, this study proposes a unique method for the categorization of knee osteoarthritis. The suggested approach entails building a deep learning model using MobileNetV3 and assembling a sizable dataset of knee X-ray images containing both knee osteoarthritic and healthy patients. To achieve accurate and trustworthy ground truth labeling, the dataset is tweaked and marked by qualified radiologists.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; MobileNetV3; convolutional neural networks; osteoarthritis classification; early diagnosis; lightweight convolutional neural network

title: Deep Learning Approach for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Classification Using ResNet18- A Review
source: IEEE India Council International Subsections Conference (INDISCON)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) develops as a common degenerative joint condition by deteriorating cartilage tissue to produce joint pain that combines with joint stiffness and restricted knee movement range. The disability burden worldwide has maximized due to this health condition which targets elderly patients primarily. The predictive model employs deep learning technology to construct a forecasting system by processing different patient datasets that combine demographic information with past medical records as well as medical imaging scans for knee osteoarthritis advancement prediction. The ResNet deep learning networks enable the model to detect early markers of OA thus enabling doctors to identify suitable treatment options at an optimal time. The proposed method demonstrates great potential for knee osteoarthritis management because it provides precise noninvasive early diagnosis and prognosis capabilities through an easily scalable platform.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease severity classification; ResNet-18; deep learning; early diagnosis; prognosis; cartilage degeneration; diagnostic imaging; patient data integration

title: ArthoInsights: Predictive Knee Degeneration analysis
source: International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Communication Systems (ICKECS)
abstract: This study presents ArthoInsights, an intelligent clinical decision support framework developed to enable automated assessment of knee osteoarthritis using radiographic imaging. The framework integrates medical image standardization, ensemble-driven deep learning prediction, explainable AI mechanisms, and a deployable web platform to support practical clinical implementation. Initially, knee X-ray scans are passed through a consistent preprocessing workflow involving resizing, intensity normalization, and noise suppression to reduce variations introduced by different acquisition sources.For diagnostic prediction, the framework applies a true ensemble approach constructed using four complementary convolutional neural network architectures: InceptionResNetV2, ResNet50, MobileNetV2, and Xception. The probability outputs generated by these models are combined to improve prediction consistency, limit individual model bias, and strengthen robustness across heterogeneous clinical inputs. To enable real-world usability, the ensemble model is deployed within a secure Flask-based web application that supports user authentication, structured patient information entry, and controlled image uploading. A radiograph validation module ensures that only X-ray images are accepted for analysis, thereby reducing the chance of unreliable or unsafe predictions.In addition to classification, the system provides an estimation of short-term disease progression by interpreting ensemble confidence levels using clinically motivated decision rules. To enhance interpretability and improve clinician confidence, Grad-CAM–based explainability is integrated, producing heatmaps that emphasize joint areas most responsible for the predicted outcome. Furthermore, a model monitoring dashboard reports per-model contribution values and ensemble readiness indicators for each case. By combining ensemble learning, interpretable inference, and secure deployment, ArthoInsights delivers a dependable and transparent solution intended to support clinical decision-making.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; clinical decision support; ensemble convolutional neural networks; explainable AI; Grad-CAM; web application deployment

title: Detecting Knee Osteoarthritis Using CNN Enhanced With Alex Net
source: International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology
abstract: This research proposes a new technique for the early diagnosis of Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) based on the latest generations of Convolutional Neural Networks in combination with the latest architectures, namely AlexNet, MobileNet, and ResNet. The project explores the analysis of medical imaging data to boost the accuracy and efficiency in the diagnosis process through X-ray or MRI scans. The incorporation of these powerful models enables the system to detect the early stages of osteoarthritis with higher accuracy, enabling better and timely treatment. Image recognition can be thought of as a strong base for AlexNet, computationally efficient for Mobile Net, mainly for mobile health applications, and skip connections in ResNet enhance the depth and performance of the model by reducing the problem of vanishing gradients. This approach will have the effect of strengthening the diagnosis while greatly reducing the number of false positives and false negatives, thereby reducing the burden on the healthcare provider. This system is also scalable and can be applied to a wide range of different imaging modalities and medical conditions. By tapping into deep learning power, this technique is all set to transform the ability to detect early knee osteoarthritis, with benefits in improved patient outcome and expedited delivery of care. It serves as an essential tool for clinicians, recommending a proactive approach that espouses preventive care and individualized treatment planning.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; early diagnosis; X-ray images; MRI images; medical image classification; AlexNet; MobileNet; ResNet; convolutional neural networks; deep learning for medical imaging; false positive reduction

title: Performance Comparison of YOLOV8 and RT-DETR Models in Multi-Stage Detection and Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: In the developing world of technology, computers can accurately detect Osteoarthritis (OA) in the early knee, which is crucial for patients. Conventional diagnostic methods that rely on subjective interpretation of X-ray images lead to variability and inconsistency. Leveraging recent advances in Deep Learning and object detection, the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical diagnosis is opening up. This study presents YOLOV8 and RT-DETR models to compare the detection and classification of knee OA severity on a comprehensive dataset consisting of doubtful, healthy, mild, moderate, and severe X-ray images. Through this training process, the models understand the characteristics and identify patterns and features in Osteoarthritis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy. Experimental results show that both models achieve very high detection performance, with an overall mAP50 value above 0.97. Although RT-DETR has higher model complexity and slightly better accuracy (mAP50 0.973), YOLOV8 offers a much faster inference speed (5.4 ms per image) than RT-DETR (8.3 ms per image), suggesting a trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. Per-class analysis indicated strong performance in Healthy and Severe, but little challenge in Minimal. These findings underscore RT-DETR’s potential as an efficient diagnostic aid for knee osteoarthritis, whereas YOLOV8 might be more suitable for real-time applications. Future work will focus on optimizing the models for minority classes and exploring more advanced Deep Learning architectures.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; X-ray images; YOLOv8; RT-DETR; object detection; multi-stage detection; inference speed; accuracy-efficiency trade-off; computer-aided diagnosis

title: A Comprehensive Study on Rheumatoid Arthritis Diagnosis using Deep Learning Techniques
source: International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is a form of arthritis, which affects joints, wrist, and knee resulting in pain, swelling and stiffness. Also, it affects other parts of the body. Hence, detecting RA at early stage is required. In medical field, image screening and decision making is the complex task, because it is error prone. Hence, experts are needed to make decision and treat them before RA becomes severe. However, it is time-consuming and unreliable. Therefore, a computational technique is required to do identification more accurate and trustworthy. Conventional imagining techniques namely radiography, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound, and fluoroscopy are widely used to analyze and diagnose RA; but they have limitations including radiation exposure, and soft tissue details. As a result, deep learning (DL), a subcategory of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been used in various medical industries to perform image segmentation and classification. DL classifiers are providing promising result and precise. Numerous DL techniques have been in use to classify RA. This study offers a comprehensive overview on the steps to be followed in image classification and comparing the performance of the DL based classification techniques that are widely used. Also, this study highlights the significance of identifying RA in early stage and examines its prolonged skeletal changes that can occur if it remains untreated.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; early diagnosis; medical image classification; deep learning; radiographic images; computed tomography; magnetic resonance imaging; ultrasound; fluoroscopy; image segmentation; skeletal changes; diagnostic accuracy comparison

title: Classification Anterior and Posterior of Knee Osteoarthritis X-Ray Images Grade KL-2 Using Deep Learning with Random Brightness Augmentation
source: International Conference on Computer Engineering, Network, and Intelligent Multimedia (CENIM)
abstract: Osteoarthritis of the knee (KOA) is a narrowing of the joint space area (JSA) due to lack of fluid in the knee joint, resulting in pain when moving and when it is severe, the femur and tibia meet. Medical personnel and existing computer-based methods have been able to detect patients with X-rays but have not been able to detect where visually the posterior AJ is still wide while the anterior AJ is actually narrow, so that the patient still feels joint pain. A new approach is proposed for the classification of X-Ray Grade Kellgren-Lawrence (KL)-2 Osteoarthritis Initiative image datasets using Deep Learning Neural Networks (DCNN) by setting the Random Brightness Augmentation hyperparameter. The experimental results obtained X-Ray Grade KL-2 narrowing image classification “Anterior View KOA” and “Posterior View KOA” with training accuracy of 83.33% and validation accuracy of 54.69% at Random Brightness with a value of 30.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; joint space narrowing; data augmentation; deep convolutional neural networks; Osteoarthritis Initiative

title: Osteo-Doc: KL-Grading of Osteoarthritis Using Deep-Learning
source: International Conference on Digital Futures and Transformative Technologies (ICoDT2)
abstract: Various deep learning frameworks are being proposed for autonomous detection of diseases to contribute towards telemedicine. Moreover, in spite of low doctor to patient ratio, such algorithms aid physicians in tracking the disease with more accuracy. According to WHO, Osteoarthritis has been declared as the most common form of arthritis. Additionally, it is one of the major reasons of physical disability among older age. Different deep learning framework-based approaches exist for evaluation of Knee osteoarthritis but none of them incorporate the feedback or symptoms of the patients. We have proposed a tri-weightage classification model i.e. a hybrid approach for grading osteoarthritis using structural features from X-Ray images, KOOS questionnaire and flexion angle. Moreover, we conducted a comparison of various deep learning model on our dataset and achieved the highest accuracy of 89.29% for RESNET152V2 and INCEPTIONRESNETV2.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; X-ray images; KOOS questionnaire; flexion angle; hybrid deep learning model; telemedicine

title: Pathological Classification of Knee Disorders via Hybrid Spatial-Spectral Neural Network
source: International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and knee osteoporosis (KOP) are prevalent orthopedic conditions in which early diagnosis is essential to prevent disease progression. In knee X-ray analysis, existing pathological feature extraction approaches often struggle to effectively integrate local fine-grained details with global structural information. To address this challenge, we propose a hybrid convolutional-spectral network that combines frequency-domain transformation with a spectrum-based global filter, embedded within a ResNet-101 architecture. This design enables joint learning of detailed textures and holistic morphological patterns. We conduct comparative experiments against six state-of-the-art baseline models and evaluated performance using five quantitative metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in KOA and KOP classification, significantly improving the recognition of both subtle textural cues and global shape variations. In addition, ablation studies were performed to assess the contribution of each component. The proposed framework provides an solution for diagnosis from knee X-ray images and offers valuable insights for medical image analysis tasks.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; knee X-ray images; pathological classification; frequency domain transformation; ResNet-101; early diagnosis

title: OsteoNet: A Multimodal Deep Learning Model for Predicting Osteoarthritis Severity and Progression
source: International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most prominent degenerative diseases of the joints that seriously impacts quality of life and incurs considerable socioeconomic costs. There is hardly any way of clinically subjectively evaluating and grading through radiographic systems that can reasonably make predictions about the long-term development of the disease. The authors here present OsteoNet, a multimodal deep learning model to predict OA severity and progression. The proposed model fuses radiographic image features with relevant clinical and demographic information in a hybrid architecture combining convolutional neural networks for image representation and transformer-based fusion for cross-modal learning. In evaluation on the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset, OsteoNet showed improved performance over unimodal baselines on metrics related to accuracy, area under the curve (AUC), and prediction of progression. These findings convey the great promise multimodal fusion has in aiding the development of robust and interpretable clinical decision support systems for the treatment of osteoarthritis.
keywords: osteoarthritis; disease severity prediction; disease progression prediction; multimodal fusion; radiographic images; clinical and demographic data; cross-modal learning; transformer-based fusion; convolutional neural networks; Osteoarthritis Initiative; clinical decision support

title: A Complete Approach to Detect Rheumatoid Arthritis using CNN
source: International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune condition characterized by excess swelling, stiffness, and pain in synovial joints. Men are less likely to suffer from this disorder than women between 30 and 50. Down the line, RA hinders to perform regular activities where, in extreme cases, this will be a reason to lose their jobs. Speaking about the curable rate of RA which entirely depends on how early the disorder is been detected and diagnosed further. Here in this paper, we have taken a step towards detecting RA in a Deep Learning way, specifically performing feature extraction using CNN model on Xray images.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; early detection; X-ray images; convolutional neural networks; feature extraction; joint inflammation; autoimmune disease diagnosis

title: Knee osteoarthritis detection an AI driven severity estimation
source: IET conference proceedings.
abstract: In this work, we use the Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grading system to investigate deep learning models or the automated detection and classification of knee osteoarthritis (OA) from radiographs. For prompt care, early identification of knee arthritis is essential, and radiography is an affordable, widely available diagnostic method. We evaluated the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of a number of cutting-edge models, including VGG16, Xception, DenseNet121, InceptionV3, ResNet50, and EfficientNet07. With testing accuracy of 96.90% and 95.90%, respectively, and strong F1 scores of 0.9690 and 0.9790, Xception and InceptionV3 outperformed the other models under evaluation, demonstrating robust performance and trustworthy generalization. While ResNet50, EfficientNet07, and an ensemble model had lower accuracy and F1 scores, indicating possible limitations, DenseNet121 and VGG16 also shown strong performance in dealing with the complex knee arthritis grading system. According to our research, Xception and InceptionV3 are very good at automatically classifying knee OA, providing potential instruments for clinical treatment planning and early identification.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; radiograph classification; deep learning; Xception; InceptionV3; transfer learning; automated diagnosis; severity estimation

title: Prediction of Knee-Replacement using Deep-Learning Approach
source: International Conference on Edge Computing and Applications (ICECAA)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (OA) is seen in both young and older people. It is a musculoskeletal disorder. If diagnosed at an early stage of development, the lifestyle of the patient can be altered in order to slow down the progression of osteoarthritis by adapting measures such as weight loss and exercise. When diagnosed at later stage, the only option available is Knee Replacement (KR). Only about 66.67% of patients have the possibility of operation being successful and problems can occur later that may require treatment. A representation is needed to recognize people having more possibility of KR, so the required treatment can be provided in order to slow down the progression of OA at early stages. This paper exhibits a deep learning predictive model which uses X-ray pictures with analytical along with statistical particulars to foretell KR having AUC 0.86 (p < 0.05).In addition, this predictive model is developed using both Xception and Inception models of CNN, where the graphs for Training and validation accuracy for both Training and Testing datasets and also the confusion Matrix for both the models used in CNN are compared, thereby identifying accurate KR predicting models for clinical utility.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; convolutional neural networks; Xception; Inception; clinical decision support; radiological features

title: Prediction of Knee Osteoarthritis Severity from X-Ray Images Using Ensemble Learning
source: International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
abstract: Millions of people worldwide are affected by knee osteoarthritis (OA), a prevalent condition involving the deterioration of joint cartilage and underlying bone. Consequently, it causes discomfort, restricted movement, and diminished mobility. It is crucial to accurately and promptly assess the severity grading of the disease for effective clinical management. In this study, the important issue of predicting knee OA severity using X-ray images is addressed through the utilization of deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs). An ensemble model that combines the strengths of different architectures was proposed to show the enhanced accuracy in Knee OA. The proposed work used the best features extracted using EfficientNet, DenseNet and ensemble models to attain an accuracy rate of 94.76%. The exceptional performance of the ensemble model underscores its reliability in classifying knee OA severity and provides a comprehensive and precise solution for health assessment. The proposed systematic approach demonstrates how deep learning can enhance diagnostic capabilities for knee osteoarthritis and improve clinical decision-making.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; X-ray images; ensemble learning; convolutional neural networks; EfficientNet; DenseNet; feature extraction; computer-aided diagnosis

title: Modelling Clinical and Radiographic Data for Early Detection and Prediction of Osteoarthritis
source: IEEE International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative disease in joint area that impacts the quality of life of people who face it. This chronic disease causes lifelong pain and affects mobility, thus causing lifelong suffering. The early detection and prediction of this disease can aid in timely treatment thus saving quality of life and reducing healthcare costs. Despite numerous researches, accurate early detection of this disease has always been a challenge in the medical field due to the complex and multifactorial nature of the disease. This research provides a comprehensive approach to the detection and prediction of OA by two different types of data: symptoms, clinical data embedded with radiological data and patient’s X-ray images of knee joints. By integrating diverse data, the model uses EfficientNetB3, a powerful Convolution Neural Network (CNN)-based algorithm for the X-ray image analysis and XGBoost and a Deep Learning approach for analyzing clinical data which is diverse and has a wide spectrum of clinical fields for analysis. The EfficientNetB3 achieves an accuracy of 95.2% for detecting the presence of OA and accuracy of 84% for grading the severity of OA. The XGBoost model achieves an accuracy of 85.35% for detecting the presence of OA and accuracy of 72.46% for grading the severity of OA. The proposed deep learning achieves validation accuracy of 84.26% for detecting OA and 70-72% for grading the severity of OA. The independent analysis of the data with various models has given us promising results and the research has shown us the advantage of using several types of data thus enabling further early prediction and improving clinical outputs for patients with OA.
keywords: osteoarthritis; early detection; disease severity classification; knee X-ray images; clinical data; multimodal data integration; EfficientNetB3; XGBoost; convolutional neural networks

title: Automated Severity Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis using Deep Learning and Image Sharpening
source: International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common orthopaedic condition that needs correct severity evaluation to ensure adequate clinical management. The purpose of this paper is to introduce an automatic deep-learning-based technique for knee radiographs classification into five Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grades (0-4) through the combination of image preprocessing, Local Center of Mass (LCM) segmentation and fine-tuning the InceptionResNetV2 model. The preprocessing approach works through normalization, image sharpening, contrast enhancement, and contour-based region of interest extraction methods to achieve better visibility of the signs of the disease process. The system was assessed on the dataset which included 4130 knee radiographs (8260 knees annotated). The results showed that the finally achieved accuracy of classification was 94.12% which is higher than that of previously used models like ResNet-50, VGG-16 и DenseNet-121. The image sharpening along with the LCM-based segmentation methods enhances the distinguishing feature of the classification task. It is expected that the future work in this field will include verification in one of the clinic centers for more validity and applicability.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; severity classification; knee radiographs; image sharpening; InceptionResNetV2; region of interest extraction; contrast enhancement

title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Opportunistic Knee Osteoporosis Screening via Multi-Class X-Ray Analysis and ResNet-18 Feature Attention
source: International Conference on Sustainability, Innovation & Technology (ICSIT)
abstract: Osteoporosis remains underdiagnosed globally due to limited access to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), particularly in resource-constrained settings. This study proposes a fully automated, explainable deep learning framework for classifying knee anteroposterior (AP) radiographs into three categories: Normal, Osteopenia, and Osteoporosis. A dataset of 5,400 expertly annotated knee X-rays was used to train a fine-tuned ResNet-18 backbone, supported by advanced preprocessing techniques including CLAHE, anisotropic diffusion filtering, Retinex normalization, and adaptive gamma correction. Automated region-of-interest (ROI) extraction was applied to focus on clinically relevant areas. For interpretability, Grad-CAM visualizations and feature embeddings using PCA, UMAP, and t-SNE were employed to analyze model focus and feature separability. The model achieved 96.1 % accuracy, a macro F1-score of 0.96, and an AUC of 0.95 on an independent test set, significantly outperforming baseline models such as SVM+HOG, VGG-16, and DenseNet-121. The proposed framework is clinically transparent, computationally efficient, and well-suited for opportunistic osteoporosis screening in primary care, particularly in mobile or rural healthcare contexts.
keywords: osteopenia; opportunistic screening; ResNet-18; Grad-CAM; explainable deep learning; image preprocessing; region of interest extraction; primary care; resource-limited settings

title: Discovering Knee Osteoarthritis Using CNN Enhanced with AlexNet
source: International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
abstract: Pain and a decline in gait function are symptoms of knee osteoarthritis (KOA). With the use of machine learning methods, developed regression models to identify KOA-related gait variables according to outcome measurements (PROMS) that the patient reports. 375 people with a range of KOA scores took part in the study. Making use of the McMaster Universities and Western Ontario Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), the severity of KOA was assessed. The severity of the diseases was divided into three groups based on WOMAC scores. From the gait data, 1087 characteristics in total were retrieved. After doing an ANOVA and student's t-test, the machine learning system selected only significant features. Each of the three subscales of the WOMAC: stiffness, discomfort, and physical function has three categories. To ascertain which chosen traits were substantially correlated with the subscales, an ANOVA was conducted. To estimate the patient's WOMAC values, a random forest regression as well as linear regression models were utilized. Based on the outcomes of the student t-test and ANOVA, 43 characteristics were chosen. Twelve characteristics from the hip, one from the pelvis, seventeen from the foot, three from the spatiotemporal characteristics, nine from the knee, and one from the ankle were chosen from each joint. This research proposed a novel approach utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with the AlexNet architecture to enhance the diagnostic accuracy and severity assessment of knee osteoarthritis. The study leverages a large dataset of knee radiographic images, encompassing diverse cases of OA progression. The AlexNet architecture, renowned for its deep learning capabilities in image classification tasks, is employed to automatically extract hierarchical features from the input radiographs. The CNN model is trained to discern subtle patterns and nuanced information indicative of OA-related structural changes, enabling it to differentiate between varying stages of the disease.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; AlexNet; convolutional neural networks; radiographic image analysis; WOMAC; disease severity assessment; gait analysis; feature selection; random forest regression

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Detection and Classification using Ensemble Model of Xception and Inception ResNetV2
source: International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis is one of the predominant types of arthritis, affecting joint tissues and afflicting millions of people globally. Currently, there are no curative medications exist for this condition, so there is a need to focus on early detection to manage disease progression. X-ray imaging serves as a primary method for osteoarthritis prediction, but manual prediction may sometimes be error-prone due to limited radiologist expertise. Recent studies have explored many machine learning systems for efficient osteoarthritis prediction from X-ray images, yet upgraded predictive accuracy is essential for early-stage detection. This study targets knee osteoarthritis detection and classification using Kellgren and Lawrence’s grading scheme, utilizing an ensemble model combining Xception and InceptionResNetV2 architectures. The ensemble model excels with a 95.1% accuracy score, contributing to medical image analysis and providing clinicians with a robust tool for early diagnosis and treatment planning in knee osteoarthritis.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis detection; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray images; ensemble learning; Xception; InceptionResNetV2; computer-aided diagnosis; radiographic image classification

title: Enforcing Explainable Deep Few-Shot Learning to Analyze Plain Knee Radiographs: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
source: IEEE International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI)
abstract: The use of fast, accurate, and automatic knee radiography analysis is becoming increasingly important in orthopedics, and it is becoming more important in improving patient-specific diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. Precise characterization of plain knee radiographs can greatly impact patient care, as they are usually used in preoperative and intraoperative planning. Rapid yet, deep learning medical image analysis has already shown success in a variety of knee image analysis tasks, ranging from knee joint area localization to joint space segmentation and measurement, with almost a human-like performance. However, there are several fundamental challenges that stop deep learning methods to obtain their full potential in a clinical setting such as orthopedics. These include the need for a large number of gold-standard, manually annotated training images and a lack of explainability and interpretability. To address these challenges, this study is the first to present an explainable deep few-shot learning model that can localize the knee joint area and segment the joint space in plain knee radiographs, using only a small number of manually annotated radiographs. The accuracy performance of the proposed method was thoroughly and experimentally evaluated using various image localization and segmentation measures, and it was compared to baseline models that utilized large-scale fully-annotated training datasets. The current deep few-shot learning methods achieved an average Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.94 and a mean Average Precision @0.5 of 0.98, using 10-shot learning in the localization of the knee joint area, and an average IoU of 0.91 in the knee joint space segmentation using only 10 manually annotated radiographs.
keywords: explainable deep learning; few-shot learning; knee radiographs; knee osteoarthritis; Osteoarthritis Initiative; interpretability; manual annotation

title: GraphConvNet: A Dual Network Utilizing Local Features Coupled with Structural Information for Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis
source: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common joint disease that severely affects the normal lives of patients. In clinical practice, the severity of KOA is commonly evaluated by observing radiographs of the knee joint However, this approach heavily relies on a doctor’s clinical experience and exhibits a certain degree of subjectivity. In previous studies, various advanced deep convolutional neural network (CNN) models have been used to diagnose KOA. As known, CNN models often focus on learning the local detailed features for decision-making and lack attention to global structural information. In this study, we propose a dual network called GraphConvNet that integrates a visual graph neural network with a deep CNN to enhance representation learning by leveraging both local detailed features and global structural information. Our proposed method was evaluated using an Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset and achieved an overall accuracy, recall, precision, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 75.24%, 77.75%, 74.33% and 0.283, respectively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method significantly improves the performance and achieves state-of-the-art performance. All codes are available at https://github.com/ddw2AIGROUP2CQUPT/GraphConvNet.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; graph neural networks; convolutional neural networks; dual-network architecture; local features

title: Deep Learning-Based Ensemble Model for Automated Severity Assessment of Osteoarthritis from Medical Images
source: International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This work aims to solve the difficulty of recognizing knee osteoarthritis using deep learning methodologies. Conventional methods of manual classification of osteoarthritis severity tend to result in an error when rated according to the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) degree a situation that complicates its utility in clinical practice. To address this problem, we are suggesting a strong framework using the most recent deep neural network approaches, namely InceptionV3 and EfficientNetB4, to improve the classification performance. In our study, we examine the performance of each model separately, defining the goal as identifying the correct Kellgren-Lawrence grade for the X-ray images of patients. We then explore how the models could be combined in an ensemble to gain the advantage of the strengths of both in their prediction task and enhance the accuracy. The results of our experiments show that the combined approach not only improves classification performance but also minimizes the risk of classification errors. The goal of this research is to present clinicians with a dependable tool in the form of deep learning methodologies to help diagnose knee osteoarthritis and ultimately improve the quality of treatment, thereby improving the patient’s quality of life.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity assessment; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray images; ensemble learning; InceptionV3; EfficientNet-B4; automated diagnosis; medical image classification

title: Machine Learning based Detection and Severity Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Emerging Research in Computational Science (ICERCS)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common musculoskeletal condition that has a significant worldwide influence on patient well-being. Despite its importance, manually detecting KOA poses tremendous obstacles. Traditional diagnostic methodologies heavily depend on the visual interpretation of radiographic images by certified radiologists. This approach leads to laborious assessments and introduces the potential for discrepancies among observers. Effective manual identification is further complicated by the intricate structure of the KOA grading system, which evaluates joint space narrowing, osteophyte production, and overall degeneration. This paper presents a method for addressing these challenges by integrating the capabilities of Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) models. The dataset utilized in this research was acquired from Kaggle and comprises image samples that have been assigned KOA grades between 0 to 4. The data source is utilized to generate two distinct datasets. The initial dataset is structured as a binary classification task, wherein images are categorized as 'KOA' (grades 2 to 4) or 'healthy' (grades 0 and 1). The second dataset is the same as the original dataset, with five classes for each KOA grade. An important objective of this research is to assess the performance of the model in both binary and multi-class classification. The datasets go through pre-processing phases such as segmentation and normalization before being fed to a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) model to extract significant features. Following this, the gathered features are utilized to train and validate numerous ML models. The assessment is predicated on several critical metrics that give information about the effectiveness of the model. The results of our study indicate that the Support Vector Machine (SVM) demonstrates outstanding efficiency in the area of binary classification. In contrast, the Random Forest (RF) model performs exceptionally well in multi-class classification, yielding promising outcomes. The suggested method not only addresses the complications of KOA grading, but it also presents a viable technique for early diagnosis and severity categorization, hence assisting clinicians and lowering the diagnostic burden on primary radiologists.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; radiographic image classification; joint space narrowing; osteophytes; early diagnosis; convolutional neural network feature extraction; support vector machine; random forest; multi-class classification; binary classification

title: Detecting Severity Level of Knee Osteoarthritis using CNN
source: International Conference on Computing, Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a condition where joints degenerate, leading to pain, stiffness, and decreased mobility. Identifying it early is crucial for timely diagnosis and management as persistent pain and limitations linked to knee osteoarthritis may contribute to mental health challenges like anxiety, depression, and stress. To exploit the continuous increase in medical patients con-cerning KOA and provide precise detection results, various studies employ machine learning analytics for KOA prognosis or treatment, however precise results are a concern. The purpose of this work is to analyze X-ray images for classification of KOA on their severity level. To this, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used as it is effective in image recognition and classification. For investigation purposes, PROTEC PRS 500E X-ray machine was utilized for collecting a dataset consisting of 1650 digital knee joint X-ray images. The data is split into training and testing sets. Then, the model is trained for $\mathbf{1 0 0}$ epochs with a validation split of 20%. For evaluation purposes, the grading of the dataset is done using Kellgren and Lawrence’s (KL) scheme consisting of doubtful, normal, mild, severe, and moderate knee arthritis X-ray images. Experimental results depict that the model successfully classifies X -ray results on the model with an accuracy of 89%.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; X-ray images; convolutional neural networks; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; early diagnosis

title: Classifying Pre-Radiographic Osteoarthritis of the Knee Using Wearable Acoustics Sensing at the Point of Care
source: IEEE Sensors Journal
abstract: This study was undertaken to determine if knee acoustic emissions (KAE) measured at the point of care with a wearable device can classify knees with pre-radiographic osteoarthritis (pre-OA) from healthy knees. We performed a single-center cross-sectional observational study comparing KAE in healthy knees to knees with clinical symptoms compatible with knee OA that did not meet classification criteria for radiographic knee OA. KAE were measured during scripted maneuvers performed in clinic exam rooms or similarly noisy medical center locations in healthy (n=20), pre-OA (n=11), and, for comparison, OA (n=12) knees. Acoustic features were extracted from the KAE and used to train models to classify pre-OA, OA, and control knees with logistic regression. Model performance was measured and optimized with Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation. Regressive sensitivity analysis was performed to combine acoustic information from individual maneuvers to further optimize performance. Test-retest reliability of KAE was measured with intraclass correlation analysis. Classification models trained with KAE were accurate for both pre-OA and OA (94% accurate, 0.96 and 0.99 area under a receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), respectively). Acoustic features selected for use in the optimized models had high test-retest reliability by intrasession and intersession intraclass correlation analysis (mean intraclass correlation coefficient 0.971 +/- 0.08 standard deviation). Analysis of KAE measured in acoustically uncontrolled medical settings using an easily accessible wearable device accurately classified pre-OA knees from healthy control knees in our small cohort. Accessible methods of identifying pre-OA could enable regular joint health monitoring and improve OA treatment and rehabilitation outcomes.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; acoustic emission; wearable sensors; point-of-care diagnosis; audio feature extraction; test-retest reliability

title: Automating Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Grading with CNN-Attention Hybrid Models
source: International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: To this end, this research proposes a dual CNN attention model to self-attend and assign severity to KOA autonomously. It employs CNNs for feature extraction and attention processes in an effort to enhance the interpretability over personal judgments and variations during manual evaluation. The recommended pipeline using publically available datasets like OAI and MOST had an average accuracy of 92.0 percent in diagnosing the severity classes of KOA, thus justifying its reliability and effectiveness. Other key performance indicators also emphasize the model's stability to some extent. For all severity levels, the hybrid method achieved the assessment of average precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.89, 0.88, and 0.89, fortunately. All the grades' ROC-AUC scores were above zero point nine, with the maximum of point nine five for the grade two indication of the model's capability of classifying different KOA severity levels with good levels of certainty. The Grad-CAM visualizations made it experientially evident that the model is focusing on features clinically relevant - the joint space narrowing, as well as the presence of osteophytes – further enhancing the model's clinical interpretability. The identical average accuracy for all the levels of severity and minimum misclassification errors that have been shown in the confusion matrix substantiate the practical usefulness of the model in clinical practice. The developed approach could potentially improve patient's and the general health care enterprise's benefit and effectiveness through the objectification of the diagnosis process. Future work will focus on increasing the variety of the dataset to enhance the utility and the potential usage of the additional modalities.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; severity classification; computer-aided diagnosis; self-attention; Grad-CAM; joint space narrowing; osteophytes; radiographic image analysis; model interpretability

title: Combining Knee Acoustic Emissions, Patient-Reported Measures, and Machine Learning to Assess Osteoarthritis Severity
source: Wearable and Implantable Body Sensor Networks
abstract: Current methods for quantifying osteoarthritis severity have limited resolution and accessibility. Patient-recorded outcome measures such as the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) capture symptom severity, but are subjectively reported and have little correlation with quantifiable metrics of disease such as Kellgren-Lawrence x-ray grade or MRI findings. Knee acoustic emissions (KAEs) offer a convenient, noninvasive option for quantifying joint health. Here, we use machine learning and wearable design to create an interpretable two-stage algorithm for combining KAEs and KOOS scores into an objective, more accessible method of quantifying disease severity. Our algorithm successfully discriminated between early and late-stage osteoarthritis (balanced accuracy = 85%, ROC-AUC = 0.88). The addition of KAEs improved classification of osteoarthritis severity over the use of KAEs (balanced accuracy = 53%, ROC-AUC = 0.786) or KOOS scores alone (balanced accuracy = 63%, ROC-AUC = 0.593). The findings suggest that KAEs combined with patient-recorded metrics can be used to make a more objective and accessible metric for digitally monitoring knee joint health.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity; patient-reported outcome measures; KOOS; wearable sensors; machine learning classification; interpretable algorithms

title: Intelligent Knee Osteoarthritis Detection Using Deep Learning Fusion
source: IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a chronic degenerative condition that impairs joint function and reduces patient mobility. This work introduces a hybrid deep learning framework that combines multiple convolutional backbones with recurrent units to improve automated KOA grading. Specifically, features extracted by EfficientNetB3, MobileNetV2, and ResNet50V2 are merged and then processed through GRU and LSTM layers to model both detailed spatial patterns and implicit sequential relationships in image representations. A dedicated feature refinement stage is incorporated to recalibrate and emphasize the most discriminative attributes before final classification, promoting better adaptability to previously unseen cases. Experiments on a well-known public knee X-ray dataset demonstrate that the proposed fusion architecture attains a classification accuracy of 95.68%, outperforming individual backbones and simpler ensembles. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each component-multi-backbone fusion, recurrent modeling, and the refinement mechanism-in elevating performance. These findings underscore the value of integrating diverse feature extractors with temporal-aware units and targeted refinement to distinguish KOA severity levels reliably. The presented approach lays groundwork for practical, AI -assisted diagnostic tools that can flag early-stage osteoarthritis, supporting clinicians in prompt intervention. Future extensions will investigate the inclusion of patient metadata and multi-modal imaging to further enhance detection robustness.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; X-ray image classification; EfficientNetB3; MobileNetV2; ResNet50V2; GRU; LSTM; feature refinement; automated diagnosis; deep learning

title: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Dual Diagnosis of Osteoporosis and Osteoarthritis from Knee X-Rays
source: IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
abstract: This study presents an explainable machine learningbased framework for the dual diagnosis of osteoporosis and osteoarthritis in knee X-ray images by identifying specific visual indicators, such as trabecular bone patterns, osteophyte formation, and joint space reduction, providing an accessible and inexpensive assessment option. A unified pipeline integrating image processing and deep learning techniques is developed, where each component corresponds to a specific radiographic feature. The framework links each diagnosis to the appropriate radiographic markers and facilitates the identification of instances in which osteoporosis and osteoarthritis coexist within the same radiograph. By emphasizing visual explanation, the proposed approach enhances interpretability and supports clinically meaningful decision-making.
keywords: osteoporosis; osteoarthritis; dual diagnosis; knee radiography; explainable machine learning; radiographic findings; trabecular pattern; osteophytes; joint space narrowing; computer-aided diagnosis; image processing pipeline

title: An Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Knee Osteoarthritis Classification Using Multiple Pre-trained CNNs and Binary Red Panda Optimization
source: International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint disorder that affects joint function and is a global social and economic burden. Identify and intervene early to slow the progression of the disease and achieve effective treatment strategies. In a clinical environment, knee joints are usually manually diagnosed and require image segmentation and annotation to identify osteoarthritis. The process is long-winded, operator dependent, and prone to interobserver variance. Recent advances in deep learning focus on improving diagnostic efficiency and reliability. The use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is implemented. The purpose of the study is to develop a state-of-the-art deep learning-based risk assessment framework to predict pain progression in patients with KOA and those at high risk of KOA. The proposed strategy uses a transfer learning ensemble to extract deep discriminative features from KOA images using VGG19, ResNet50, and InceptionV3 architectures. Using the Binary Red Panda Optimization (bRPO) algorithm, optimized feature subsets were extracted from the originally extracted highdimensional feature space, which has the average fitness value of 0.4137 and the best fitness value of 0.3155. The optimized feature set was then classified via deep learning and traditional machine learning classifiers. Moreover, bRPO was employed for the tuning of CNN hyperparameters for better performance enhancement. The performance of the newly devised system surpasses those of the older systems and achieved accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity values of$0.9887,0.9802$, and 0.9901. Consequently, we performed statistical analyzes to ensure the robustness of the findings assessed in this study.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis classification; feature selection; VGG19; ResNet50; InceptionV3; knee imaging; risk assessment

title: DeepKneeExplainer: Explainable Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis From Radiographs and Magnetic Resonance Imaging
source: IEEE Access
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease, which significantly affects middle-aged and elderly people. Although primarily identified via hyaline cartilage change based on medical images, technical bottlenecks like noise, artifacts, and modality impose an enormous challenge on high-precision, objective, and efficient early quantification of OA. Owing to recent advancements, approaches based on neural networks (DNNs) have shown outstanding success in this application domain. However, due to nested non-linear and complex structures, DNNs are mostly opaque and perceived as black-box methods, which raises numerous legal and ethical concerns. Moreover, these approaches do not have the ability to provide the reasoning behind diagnosis decisions in the way humans would do, which poses an additional risk in the clinical setting. In this paper, we propose a novel explainable method for knee OA diagnosis based on radiographs and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which we calledDeepKneeExplainer. First, we comprehensively preprocess MRIs and radiographs through the deep-stacked transformation technique against possible noises and artifacts that could contain unseen images for domain generalization. Then, we extract the region of interests (ROIs) by employing U-Net architecture with ResNet backbone. To classify the cohorts, we train DenseNet and VGG architectures on the extracted ROIs. Finally, we highlight class-discriminating regions using gradient-guided class activation maps (Grad-CAM++) and layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP), followed by providing human-interpretable explanations of the predictions. Comprehensive experiments based on the multicenter osteoarthritis study (MOST) cohorts, our approach yields up to 91% classification accuracy, outperforming comparable state-of-the-art approaches. We hope that our results will encourage medical researchers and developers to adopt explainable methods and DNN-based analytic pipelines towards an increasing acceptance and adoption of AI-assisted applications in the clinical practice for improved knee OA diagnoses.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; explainable AI; X-ray images; magnetic resonance imaging; Grad-CAM; layer-wise relevance propagation; region of interest extraction; U-Net; DenseNet; VGG; domain generalization; image preprocessing; hyaline cartilage; AI-assisted diagnosis

title: Self-Supervised Multimodal Fusion Network for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Grading
source: International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a highly prevalent form of arthritis and a leading cause of physical disability, given the growing aging population. To assist the knee OA assessment, there is a demanding interest in computer-aided grading algorithms. Existing grading methods generally require resource-intensive annotated datasets for supervised training. Moreover, they only consider unimodal data, whilst multimodal medical images are rarely utilised to formulate better knee OA patterns. Therefore, in this study, a novel Self-supervised Multimodal Fusion Network (S-MFN) is proposed for multimodal unsupervised knee OA grading with X-ray and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities. Specifically, S-MFN involves two modality-specific streams to obtain knee OA representations from the two corresponding modalities. A modality-aware information exchange mechanism is devised to interactively formulate cross-modal patterns in a multi-scale manner regarding the scales of feature maps. To this end, a multimodal contrastive learning is introduced in a self-supervised manner through modality-specific and cross-modal modelling. Comprehensive experimental results on the widely used dataset, Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI), demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; multimodal fusion; self-supervised learning; contrastive learning; X-ray images; magnetic resonance imaging; multi-scale feature maps; computer-aided diagnosis; Osteoarthritis Initiative

title: DeepOA: Clinical Decision Support System for Early Detection and Severity Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Computer, Communication and Signal Processing (ICCCSP)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (OA) is a medical condition affecting the knee joint that causes pain due to the cartilage wear-and-tear. The severity of the impairment is graded by experienced radiologists as per standardized grading systems like the Kellgren-Lawrence(KL) grading scheme. Early detection and classification of knee OA in a patient before it increases in severity can significantly aid in corrective measures and benefit humankind. In this work, we propose a DL model to automatically segment the knee region and predict onset of Knee OA with X-ray scans. A comparative study using an ensemble model consisting of a YOLOv5 object detection algorithm for knee joint segmentation is also proposed. Various classification models such as VGG16, Resnet etc., are experimented with for the KL grade classification. The detailed experiments are conducted to understand the need for the region of interest segmentation step in KL grade classification. The proposed Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) can help the medical practitioners perform preemptive screening based on X-ray scans for detecting onset earlier and for enabling required treatment.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; clinical decision support systems; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray image classification; knee joint segmentation; YOLOv5 object detection; early disease detection; radiographic screening; severity classification

title: Predictive Modeling of Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Using Machine Learning Techniques: A Comparative Analysis
source: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication and Materials (ICACCM)
abstract: Machine learning has significantly transfigured healthcare by providing innovative solutions across numerous domains, with its impact on knee osteoarthritis being particularly notable. In healthcare, ML facilitates early disease detection, personalized treatment strategies, and outcome prediction, all of which are critical for effective patient care. Specifically in Knee Osteoarthritis, Machine learning techniques have significantly advanced diagnostic capabilities by analyzing patient data such as demographics, symptoms, and imaging results to predict disease progression and grade patients based on severity. This study examines how well machine learning algorithms work with X-ray images to assess the degree of osteoarthritis in the knee. By effectively predicting severity levels using attributes taken from X-ray pictures, machine learning (ML) presents a possible option. Various ML algorithms, including convolutional neural networks and ensemble methods, are explored for their ability to analyze X-ray images and extract relevant patterns indicative of OA severity. Challenges such as data preprocessing, feature extraction, and model interpretation are addressed, aiming to enhance the reliability and clinical utility of ML-based severity assessment models for knee OA.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; radiographic evaluation; convolutional neural networks; ensemble methods; feature extraction; model interpretability; disease progression

title: Unsupervised Contrastive Refinement With Graph-Aware Multimodal Interaction for Radiology Report Generation
source: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Automatic Radiology Report Generation (RRG) reduces medical workload by automatically generating diagnostic reports from X-ray images. In recent studies, an improved performance has been observed by first classifying the image and then incorporating clinical outcomes into the RRG pipeline, with cross-modal interactions between image and text. However, these studies have limitations (specifically on chest X-ray), including : (1) inconsistent cross-modal learning due to under-utilization of textual information, and (2) reliance on noisy classification labels, resulting in inaccurate attention and invariant report generation. To address these issues, a Medical Context-aware RRG Framework (MedCARF) is proposed, which introduces a Disease-Aware Visual Textual Alignment (D-ViTAlign) module to capture organ-abnormality relationships from scene graphs and visual features. Label refinement is achieved using an unsupervised Augmentation Distillation with Contrastive Refinement (AuDiCoR) loss, which iteratively refines the visual features via augmentation alignment and loss modelling. In addition, the knee OAI dataset is benchmarked for the RRG task, and the performance of MedCARF contributions is explicitly tested on this dataset. Furthermore, Knee RRG performance is evaluated using multimodal information, including biomechanical data. Experimental results showed that a minimum 3.2% improvement in METEOR and a 4.22% AUC gain over classification SOTA are achieved for chest X-ray, while a 9.69% average improvement across all NLG metrics is observed for knee RRG with biomechanical data integration. Overall, contextually accurate reports are generated, and consistent classification performance is achieved, including for minority classes, demonstrating the robustness and clinical applicability of the proposed framework. The Code is available at: https://github.com/adaydar/MedCARF.
keywords: radiology report generation; unsupervised contrastive learning; scene graph; cross-modal alignment; label refinement; biomechanical data; chest radiography; clinical text generation

title: An Efficient Deep Learning System for Multi-Class Knee Osteoarthritis Classification Leveraging Fine-Tuned Xception
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a common degenerative joint disorder that has a significant impact on mobility and quality of life highlights the need for accurate and automated diagnostic solutions. This work provides a high-performance deep learning for the multi-class classification of knee osteoarthritis by a fine-tuned Xception model for knee X-ray images. The proposed approach makes the most of depthwise separable convolutions and transfer learning to appropriately catch subtle structural variations related to different grades of osteoarthritis. A publicly available dataset that was extracted from the Kaggle platform is used, consisting of five clinically relevant classes of different progressive stages of the disease. Comprehensive preprocessing, data splitting, and fine-tuning methods are used to improve generalization and stability. Experimental evaluation proves that the proposed model achieves an overall classification accuracy of 97%, which outperforms the performance of conventional deep learning architectures like VGG16, ResNet50 and EfficientNet by a significant margin. The results point to the robustness, efficiency and clinical relevance of the proposed framework with its strong potential for integration into computer-aided diagnosis systems for support of early and accurate assessment of osteoarthritis of the knee.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; multi-class classification; Xception; fine-tuning; transfer learning; knee X-ray images; depthwise separable convolution; computer-aided diagnosis; automated diagnosis

title: Hybrid ML/DL Framework for Arthritis Risk and Severity Prediction
source: International Research Conference on Smart Computing and Systems Engineering (SCSE)
abstract: Arthritis is a common chronic disease with significant consequences for the quality of life among older populations. Early diagnosis of arthritis can help in preserving positive health outcomes through mitigating the progression of the disease. In this study, a hybrid predictive framework was introduced that takes individual lifestyle parameters along with the radiographic imaging of the patient as parameters that have not been studied in the Sri Lankan context before. Data were collected from Gampaha Wickramarachchi Ayurveda Hospital, and the data were split into two main data sets:$\mathbf{1 2 0 0}$records of lifestyle factors and clinical manifestations, and 598 diagnostic X-radiography images of knee joints. Supervised Machine Learning algorithms have been applied to the textual dataset, and the best validation accuracy of 96 % for the prediction of the likelihood of Arthritis by employing the Random Forest (RF) classifier. Patients at high risk were graded into three groups using deep learning architectures (ResNet-50 and a convolutional neural network). CNN validation accuracy was 95 % and 97 % for training accuracy. The outcomes of this research have been operationalized through a web application that integrates the two models, enabling arthritis risk prediction based on lifestyle and symptom data, followed by severity classification through X-ray analysis when risk is detected.
keywords: knee X-ray images; lifestyle factors; clinical features; hybrid machine learning and deep learning; random forest; ResNet50; convolutional neural networks; web application; Sri Lankan population

title: A method for the grading and recognition of osteoarthritis X-ray images based on the MED-HED detection
source: Annual Conference of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society (IECON)
abstract: The manual Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading of osteoarthritis (OA) X-ray images is prone to inter-rater variability owing to the subjective nature of the evaluation process. In this study, we constructed an automatic KL grading system to realize intelligent assessment of OA severity in X-ray images through preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, and classification. The primary steps are as follows: First, preprocessing: This step integrates wavelet denoising, median filtering, and Medical_HED (MED-HED) edge detection to enhance image contrast and extract contours of key knee joint regions. Second, regional segmentation: The region of interest (ROI) is intercepted based on joint space localization, and the images of key regions of the knee joint are obtained by combining the connected region labeling method. Third, feature extraction: Fourier descriptors are employed to convert joint contours into shape vectors, facilitating extraction of geometric features that reflect OA severity. Fourth, grading classification: A template matching framework is constructed to compare shape vector similarity between samples and KL-grade templates, enabling automatic grading. Experimental results show that the system achieves an overall grading accuracy of 92.3% in 400 knee X-ray tests, outperforming conventional operators such as Canny and LOG. The proposed recognition method mitigates subjectivity in manual evaluation through multi-step image processing and shape analysis. Its high accuracy and efficiency make it a reliable computer-aided decision-making tool for clinical OA diagnosis, with potential to replace manual grading.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; automated grading; X-ray images; wavelet denoising; knee joint segmentation; Fourier descriptors; shape features; template matching; computer-aided diagnosis; interobserver variability

title: Explainable Optimizing Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis: Leveraging Multi-label Learning and Clinical Features for Enhanced Accuracy
source: International Conference on Multimedia Analysis and Pattern Recognition (MAPR)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a widespread degenerative joint condition impacting millions worldwide, resulting in gradual decline over time and hindering patients’ daily functions due to persistent pain and discomfort. Despite recent strides in Artificial Intelligence facilitating automated diagnosis using X-ray or MRI scans, many current approaches neglect the role of clinical variables in predictions, relying solely on imaging data for classification. In this study, we introduce an innovative methodology for evaluating KOA severity that incorporates both medical images and clinical information. We focus on applying multi-label classification to medical images aiming to generate a more comprehensive prediction compared to solely assessing disease severity. By incorporating multi-label classification, we can identify the presence of additional vital risk factors. To further enhance the prediction’s accuracy, we also integrate relevant clinical information with the image analysis. We then showcase the efficacy of our approach by outperforming existing methods. Furthermore, our model sheds light on the patient risk factors like joint space narrowing, osteophytes, and sclerosis through multi-label classification, rendering it using an explainable AI technique. To be more precise, each prediction from our model is accompanied by an explanation, thereby augmenting the interpretability of the diagnostic process.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease severity prediction; multi-label classification; clinical features; explainable AI; joint space narrowing; osteophytes; radiography; risk factors

title: A Knee OA Diagnosis Method via the Attention Mechanism and MSGD-Based Automatic Learning Rate Decay Strategy
source: IEEE International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Artificial Intelligence (PRMVAI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) stands as a highly prevalent degenerative joint disorder, imposing significant physical and psychological burdens on affected patients. Typically, clinicians rely on X-ray images for OA diagnosis, which is susceptible to subjective bias and fatigue-related errors. Thus, computer-aided diagnostic systems for knee OA utilizing X-rays have been developed. Current approaches primarily adopt a two-stage framework involving knee joint localization and OA severity prediction, but face several challenges: (1) Existing methods fail to adequately capture rich contextual semantic information from knee joint regions, compromising diagnostic performance. (2) Conventional learning rate decay strategies in neural network training often rely on manual configuration, potentially leading to excessively small learning rates that slow convergence, while adaptive methods like Adam may exhibit suboptimal generalization. To overcome above limitations, a novel knee OA diagnosis method incorporating the attention mechanism and an automated learning rate decay strategy via MSGD is presented. Our framework first preprocesses input data and localizes knee joint regions using KneeDetNet. Detected regions are then fed into the ResNet34 backbone network, where we integrate a coordinate attention module to enhance positional and contextual semantic information extraction. Additionally, we extract five local feature maps, which are concatenated with global features before the fully connected layer for comprehensive feature representation. The model employs a weighted joint loss function combining Center loss and Softmax loss, optimized through our MSGD-based automated learning rate decay strategy. Extensive evaluations on the public OAI dataset demonstrate that our approach significantly improves knee OA classification accuracy, showing promising potential for clinical decision support.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; computer-aided diagnosis; X-ray images; attention mechanism; coordinate attention; learning rate decay; center loss; softmax loss; clinical decision support

title: Automatic Diagnosis of Knee Osteoarthritis Using Deep Learning Approaches
source: International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a common degenerative joint disease that affects millions of people worldwide, especially those aged over 50 years. It is characterized by gradual breakdown of the cartilage in the knee joint, leading to pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility. Knee osteoarthritis can develop because of a variety of factors, including genetics, old injuries, obesity, and repetitive stress on the knee joint. It is a chronic condition that often worsens over time if not treated properly. Various treatment options are available for managing knee osteoarthritis symptoms, including medication, physical therapy, and surgery. Early diagnosis and intervention can help individuals with knee osteoarthritis to manage their symptoms and maintain their quality of life. In this research, a range of deep learning models are utilized to aid clinicians in the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis, reduce the workload on primary radiologists, and facilitate early detection and treatment. The deep learning model EfficientNetB7 implemented and compared with DenseNet169 and Inception ResNet V2. The EfficientNetB7 model achieved the highest results, with Accuracy 93.90%.
