keywords: knee osteoarthritis; automated diagnosis; radiographic image classification; EfficientNetB7; DenseNet169; InceptionResNetV2; cartilage degeneration; early detection; deep learning model comparison

title: A Comparison Study in Detecting Knee Osteoarthritis Severity with Deep Leaning
source: International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (Knee OA or KOA) presents a significant medical challenge due to its prevalence and the complexities involved in diagnosis. Manual diagnosis of KOA is time-consuming and susceptible to errors, particularly considering that a majority (60%) of Knee OA cases occur in elderly individuals. Thus, the development of an accurate and reliable diagnostic system is imperative. Deep neural network (DNN) models offer a promising avenue for automating the identification and classification of Knee OA images. Leveraging their capability to discern intricate patterns within images, DNNs facilitate a comprehensive analysis of KOA images. In this study, we conduct a comparison study in diagnosing Knee OA with two different datasets. We employ several DNN models including Custom CNN, ResNet101, EfficientNet, and ConvNextBase, assessing their performance on a withheld test dataset. Our proposed approach stands to revolutionize the diagnosis of Knee OA, offering potential benefits such as enhanced diagnostic accuracy and the prospect of early detection. Early diagnosis facilitated by this method holds the promise of prompt intervention, thereby mitigating the progression of knee joint damage. Overall, ConvNeXtBase performs the best in our comparison study.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; medical image diagnosis; deep neural network; ConvNeXt; ResNet-101; EfficientNet; custom CNN; early diagnosis; knee joint damage

title: Automated Temporomandibular Joint Disorder Detection Using Deep Learning-Based Condylar Morphometric Analysis from Dental Radiographs
source: International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders are often associated with structural changes in the mandibular condyle, including degenerative changes, asymmetry, and abnormal condylar growth. Early identification of these abnormalities is important for diagnosis and treatment planning. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework for detecting temporomandibular joint disorders from dental radiographs by combining disease classification with condylar morphometric analysis. A ResNet-101 model was used to classify radiographs into normal, condylar hyperplasia, and osteoarthritis-related degenerative categories. The dataset consisted of 800 dental radiographs, including 267 normal cases, 266 condylar hyperplasia cases, and 267 osteoarthritis-related cases. In addition to classification, left condyle length, right condyle length, and asymmetry index were measured to provide quantitative support for the diagnostic output. The proposed model achieved an overall accuracy of approximately 95% on the evaluated dataset. However, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary because external validation and formal calibration analysis were not performed. The results suggest that combining deep learning with morphometric measurements may support computer-aided assessment of temporomandibular joint disorders.
keywords: temporomandibular disorders; mandibular condyle; condylar hyperplasia; temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis; dental radiographs; computer-aided diagnosis; ResNet-101; disease classification

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Knee Osteoarthritis Diagnosis: A Survey on Classification and Severity Grading
source: IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing, VLSI, Electrical Circuits and Robotics (DISCOVER)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a pervasive degenerative joint disease where there is a gradual breakdown of the cartilage in joints causing pain, stiffness, reduced mobility and swelling. Osteoarthritis is a debilitating condition affecting millions globally and mainly occurs because of the unhealthy and improper diet rising among the urban population. Osteoporosis can have a major impact on the tibiofemoral joint (Weight bearing joint of knee) because of its reduced bone density and increased risk of fractures. These joints are the most commonly occurring pressure points in the entire body as they bear majority of the body weight. These hinge joints are critical for many activities and Osteoarthritis in these areas significantly impact the mobility and movement of the entire body causing pain and stiffness. In extreme cases, requirement of knee replacement surgery which have complex procedures and time for recovery. Planning an appropriate diagnosis and course of treatment for osteoporosis requires an expertise understanding of the degree of joint degeneration. Machine Learning methods and deep learning algorithms can be implemented to enable AI for image recognition through which we can reduce reliance and interpretation by Radiologist and clinical experts. This research provides an extensive literature review on the use of X-ray imaging, GAN models for Synthetic image generation and various deep learning models and ML algorithms implemented to identify and classify the degree of tibiofemoral joint degeneration in osteoporosis. The review summarises various Machine learning models and algorithms previously implemented for Knee Osteoarthritis Detection and classification (including both binary and multi class classification) of osteoporosis on the tibiofemoral joint and also covers the difficulties, developments, and potential paths in this field.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; X-ray image classification; generative adversarial networks; synthetic image generation; computer-aided diagnosis; cartilage degeneration; osteoporosis; knee arthroplasty

title: Performance Evaluation of Standard CNN Models for Osteoporosis Detection
source: International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
abstract: During the design of the model for Osteoporosis detection, studying the reference standard CNN models and their response to the detection of Osteoporosis from X-ray images is the first step considered. With respect to model's characteristic architectural composition, this paper presents a comprehensive review and performance evaluation of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for osteoporosis classification using X-ray images. The study examines standard CNN architectures, VGGNets, Residual Nets, the latest version of MobileNet and Efficient-Nets which are trained on multiple benchmark datasets to classify bone images into osteoporosis, osteopenia, or healthy conditions. Key performance metrics such as accuracy for respective classification of conditions, sensitivity towards osteoporosis, specificity towards healthy conditions and balanced analysis with F1-score. The review highlights the role of attention mechanisms, transfer learning, and multi-scale feature extraction in enhancing classification performance. Comparative results demonstrate the superiority of advanced CNN models in automated bone health assessment, with EfficientNet-B7 achieving the highest classification accuracy. The findings provide valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of different CNN architectures, guiding future research in AI-driven osteoporosis detection. This study contributes to developing reliable, scalable, and interpretable deep learning frameworks for improved early diagnosis and clinical decision-making in osteoporosis screening.
keywords: osteoporosis detection; convolutional neural networks; X-ray images; osteopenia; EfficientNetB7; MobileNet; VGG; ResNet; transfer learning; attention mechanism; multi-scale feature extraction; automated diagnosis

title: Three-Dimensional Shape Statistical Analysis of Tibial Plafond Deformed by Ankle Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Intelligent Informatics and Biomedical Sciences (ICIIBMS)
abstract: The etiology of primary ankle osteoarthritis is not enough elucidated. Ankle osteoarthritis wears away cartilage and causes pain in daily life same as the hip and knee osteoarthritis. However, the prognosis of ankle osteoarthritis is less favorable than hip and knee osteoarthritis. The investigation of the bone shape in ankle osteoarthritis is significant in choosing adequate surgery for patients. Choosing appropriate surgery leads to improving prognosis. X-ray images and Computed Tomography (CT)-scan images are usually used for the classification of ankle osteoarthritis, however, the classification by the two-dimensional measurements of the X-ray images and CT images can vary between physicians. The aim of this study is to investigate the three-dimensions geometrical deformity characteristics of the tibial plafond by statistical analysis. High severity ankle osteoarthritis had deformity characteristics. In particular, statistically significant differences were found in the varus deformity of the articular facet of medial malleolus and tibial plafond between stage 3B and mild group (p < 0.006), and the hyperostosis of the edge of anterior tibial plafond and the medial malleolus between stage 4 and mild group (p < 0.002). The results suggest that patients with high severity ankle osteoarthritis have tibial plafond common deformity characteristics. This study contributes to scientific advances in ankle osteoarthritis surgery.
keywords: ankle osteoarthritis; tibial plafond; three-dimensional shape analysis; varus deformity; medial malleolus; hyperostosis; articular cartilage wear

title: Deep Learning-Based Osteoarthritis Severity Classification from Radiographic Images (X-Ray)
source: International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology for Sustainable Development (ICRAIS)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease that has a major global health effect. For efficient treatment planning and illness management, early identification and precise OA severity assessment are essential. In this work, we use deep learning techniques to present a complete method for classifying the severity of osteoarthritis (OA) from radio-graphic images. Preprocessing the dataset, optimizing pre-trained models, utilizing ensemble learning strategies, and assessing model performance are all part of our methodology. The X-ray images from different sources that are preprocessed to improve quality and uniformity make up the knee OA dataset utilized in this study. In order to tailor various pre-trained deep learning models—DenseNet, EfficientNet, InceptionNet, MobileNet, and ResNet—to the particular job of classifying OA severity, we fine-tune them. Then, to aggregate predictions from several models for increased accuracy and resilience, ensemble learning techniques are applied. The outcomes of our experiments show how successful our strategy is, since our models diagnose OA severity levels with a high degree of accuracy. Our work advances the field of medical image analysis and has potential benefits for improving OA diagnosis and treatment.
keywords: osteoarthritis; knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; X-ray images; radiographic images; transfer learning; pre-trained convolutional neural networks; ensemble learning; DenseNet; EfficientNet; InceptionNet; MobileNet; ResNet; medical image analysis

title: Transfer Learning-Based Smart Features Engineering for Osteoarthritis Diagnosis From Knee X-Ray Images
source: IEEE Access
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a deteriorating joint disease affecting millions worldwide. Osteoarthritis is a chronic condition that develops over time due to joint wear and tears. The degeneration of joint cartilage is the underlying cause of osteoarthritis, resulting in bone-to-bone contact and contributing to stiffness, discomfort, and restricted movement. People with osteoarthritis struggle to perform simple tasks such as walking, standing, or climbing stairs. Moreover, osteoarthritis can also cause psychological distress, including depression and anxiety, due to the chronic pain and disability associated with the condition. Improving the quality of life requires the development of efficient methods for early detection. Our study aims to create a model that can effectively diagnose osteoarthritis in knee X-ray images at an early stage. The advanced deep learning-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and several machine learning-based techniques are applied in comparison. A novel transfer learning-based feature engineering technique CRK (CNN Random forest K-neighbors) is proposed to detect osteoarthritis with high performance. Using a 2D-CNN, the proposed CRK smartly extracts the spatial features from the X-ray images. The spatial features are input to the random forest and k-neighbors techniques, creating a probabilistic feature set. The probabilistic feature set is utilized to build the applied machine learning-based techniques. Extensive study experiments demonstrate that the proposed model outperformed with a 99% accuracy score for predicting osteoarthritis. The performance of each applied model is validated using hyperparameter optimization and k-fold-based cross-validation. The proposed study has the potential to revolutionize the prediction of osteoarthritis from X-ray images with high-performance scores.
keywords: osteoarthritis diagnosis; knee X-ray images; transfer learning; feature engineering; 2D convolutional neural network; random forest; k-nearest neighbors; early detection; joint cartilage degeneration

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Prediction and Progression Using Multi Modal Deep Learning
source: IEEE Region 10 Symposium (TENSYMP)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint disease that needs precise detection, severity estimation, and continuous monitoring. This work presents a unified multimodal decision-support framework for comprehensive KOA evaluation integrating structured clinical and biomarker data, medical imaging (X-ray and MRI), and wearable IoT sensing. Machine learning models are used for KOA presence prediction based on demographic and laboratory data, while deep learning architectures are used for automated classification from radiographic images. Late fusion of imaging and clinical predictors aligned with the Kellgren–Lawrence grading system predicts KOA severity. Furthermore, a wearable IoT subsystem is developed to collect vibration and temperature signals for continuous severity monitoring with interpretable rule-based models. Experimental results demonstrate strong multi-modal performance. The clinical and biomarker-based KOA presence prediction component achieved 89% accuracy using Gradient Boosting; the imaging-based disease detection component achieved 91.04% validation and 90.83% test accuracy with ROC–AUC up to 97.46% for X-ray classification and 83.31% validation and 83.98% test accuracy with ROC–AUC up to 92.02% for MRI classification using YOLOv8; the imaging-based severity grading component achieved 80% test accuracy using EfficientNetB0; and the IoT-based severity monitoring component achieved 92.80% test accuracy using a decision tree classifier.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; disease prediction; disease progression; multimodal fusion; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; X-ray classification; MRI classification; clinical biomarkers; decision support system

title: Pathology-Informed Augmentation Improves Cross-Cohort IMU-to-vGRF Estimation Between Healthy Adults and Adults With Osteoarthritis
source: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
abstract: Estimating vertical ground reaction forces (vGRF) from wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) degrades when models are applied across populations with different gait characteristics. We evaluated pathology-informed augmentation to improve generalization between healthy adults and adults with lower-limb osteoarthritis. We collected instrumented-treadmill walking data from 47 adults, including 29 healthy participants and 18 with radiographic osteoarthritis, predominantly knee osteoarthritis. Force-plate vGRFs were synchronized with body-worn IMUs. We developed a Transformer-based IMU model with low-rank multi-stream fusion (LMF), which learns compact shared patterns linking accelerometer and gyroscope signals across segments. We then applied a novel ratio-based augmentation that transforms source-cohort strides into target-like strides using donor-derived gait-feature ratios for stance duration, peak vGRF magnitude, dominant acceleration frequency, and segment-level acceleration amplitude. Generalization was tested in two directions, healthy-to-osteoarthritis (H2K) and osteoarthritis-to-healthy (K2H), using participant-disjoint splits. Augmentation reduced source-target separation in a low-dimensional gait feature space by 87% in H2K and 88% in K2H. On held-out participants, mass-normalized root-mean-square error (RMSE, N/kg) decreased by 10.5% in H2K and 11.4% in K2H. Expanded training without augmentation yielded smaller changes, with 4.9% in H2K and 0.2% in K2H. Peak accuracy was high: 96.7% of matched peaks in H2K and 97.0% in K2H were within 10% of the reference peak height. An interpretable, ratio-based augmentation that targets temporal, kinetic, spectral, and segment-amplitude features improves cross-cohort generalization of IMU-to-vGRF models and may reduce reliance on large target cohort datasets.
keywords: inertial measurement unit; knee osteoarthritis; cross-cohort generalization; data augmentation; transformer models; wearable sensors; gait analysis; force plate validation

title: Greylag Goose Optimization-Driven Convolutional Neural Network for Multi-Class Knee Osteoporosis Classification from X-Ray Images
source: IEEE World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is one critical musculoskeletal state. Early detection of knee OA is a significant challenge in clinical settings. Automated analysis of knee X-ray images can provide a way forward for accurate OA diagnostic support. This study proposes a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) optimized by the Greylag Goose Optimization (GGO) algorithm. The aim is multi-class classification of knee X-rays into Normal, Osteopenia, and Osteoporosis categories. The baseline CNN achieved an accuracy of 74.80%, sensitivity of 83.20%, specificity of 85.60%, precision of 74.10%, and F1-score of 73.60%. After the graylag goose optimization accuracy improved to 83.52% with gains across all metrics. The results indicate that nature based optimization is an effective strategy for accurate medical image diagnosis through deep learning methods for classification tasks

title: Diagnostic Imaging Support System for Rheumatoid Arthritis Using Ultrasound Images
source: IEEE Annual International Computer Software and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
abstract: In recent years, image inspections have become a useful tool in the early diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, evaluations in RA ultrasound inspections are visual inspections by doctors, evaluation tends to become somewhat subjective, meaning that it is difficult for less-experienced doctors to make an assessment. In this study, therefore, we propose a system that alleviates the burden on doctors, by automating RA image diagnosis, that is to say an RA image diagnosis support system using ultrasound images. With this system, as it is necessary to automate RA image diagnosis, it is necessary to propose an image classification method with higher classification accuracy. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an image classification method with higher precision, by comparing methods of image classification. We also show our evaluation results. As a result, it is considered that image classification via CNN using automatic extraction images of synovial thickening surrounding areas is effective for image classification of ultrasound images for the purpose of automating RA image diagnosis.
keywords: rheumatoid arthritis; ultrasonography; image classification; convolutional neural networks; synovial thickening; computer-aided diagnosis; early diagnosis

title: Comparative Analysis of Performance of Deep Learning Models in Knee Arthritis Classification
source: International Conference on Sustainable Communication Networks and Application (ICSCNA)
abstract: To keep away from irreversible joint damage and systemic issues, knee septic arthritis, a important joint contamination, desires to be recognized rapid and accurately. Traditional analysis techniques that rely on laboratory consequences and medical assessment can be hard and reason healing delays. The era uses modern day image characteristic extraction strategies to boom precision and dependability, giving scientific specialists a useful tool for choice-making. title: A Novel Knee Joint Space Detection Model With Y-Sensitive Euclidean Distance
source: IEEE Access
abstract: Knee joint space is a critical indicator for diagnosing osteoarthritis (OA). This study introduces a novel CNN model, Knee Joint Space Net (K-JSNet), designed for the precise detection of knee joint space keypoints. K-JSNet integrates the strengths of GoogLeNet and ResNet, utilizing Inception and residual blocks to effectively extract and preserve key joint space width (JSW) features. To ensure accurate alignment with bone edges, a Y-sensitive Euclidean distance loss function was developed. Conceptual validation using the OAI dataset demonstrated that K-JSNet achieved a point-to-point Euclidean distance error of 0.69 mm, an 18% reduction compared to ResNet50. To evaluate real-world performance, the model was tested on a large-scale clinical cohort of 4,184 radiographs from Taichung Veterans General Hospital. While the model exhibited a slight but consistent overestimation of JSW compared to expert annotations (mean difference: 0.372 mm medial, 0.162 mm lateral), these discrepancies remain well within the clinically acceptable range of 0.5–1.0 mm. Keypoint localization analysis showed high consistency, particularly in the vertical direction critical for JSW estimation (ICC: 0.963–0.972). These findings confirm that K-JSNet meets radiological precision standards and provides a reliable, reproducible tool for clinical deployment.
keywords: osteoarthritis; keypoint detection; convolutional neural networks; radiographic evaluation; GoogLeNet; ResNet; knee radiographs

title: KOA-VGG19: A Fine-Tuned Deep Learning Framework for Automated Knee Osteoporosis Classification
abstract: Knee osteoporosis is a condition that calls for a timely diagnosis to ensure the prevention of the disease progression and reduced risks of a fracture occurrence. The current diagnosis techniques rely mostly on the interpretation of radiographic images by the expert, which is subjective, takes time and can vary. To overcome these limitations, the research proposes using the binary classification neural network of deep learning in combination with fine-tuned VGG19 convolutional neural network (CNN) to ensure fully automatic diagnosis of the knee osteoporosis. In this study, 5,000 tagged knee joint images belonging to healthy and osteoporotic categories are going to be utilized. All of these images were converted to the RGB format and resized to 224x224 pixels, and flipped and rotated in order to generalize the models and prevent the overfitting. The pre-trained weights of ImageNet were used and fixed, and then the fine-tuning of the other layers followed. Training has been performed for 200 epochs, using the Adam optimizer, with Batch Normalization and early stopping, using an 80:20 split for training and validation, achieving an accuracy score of 97.5%, F1-score of 0.97 and virtually zero false positive rates. From the confusion matrix, it is clear that the number of false positives is also zero, and the number of false negatives is also virtually zero, which implies the effectiveness of the model proposed. This is in agreement with the findings of the research study with regard to the effectiveness of the fine-tuned VGG19 network in aiding the detection of knee osteoporosis non-invasively and automatically.
keywords: automated diagnosis; VGG19; fine-tuning; radiographic images; binary classification; convolutional neural networks; ImageNet pre-trained weights; non-invasive detection

title: Active Latent Space Shape Model: A Bayesian Treatment of Shape Model Adaptation with an Application to Psoriatic Arthritis Radiographs
source: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
abstract: Shape models have been used extensively to regularise segmentation of objects of interest in images, e.g. bones in medical x-ray radiographs, given supervised training examples. However, approaches usually adopt simple linear models that do not capture uncertainty and require extensive annotation effort to label a large number of set template landmarks for training. Conversely, supervised deep learning methods have been used on appearance directly (no explicit shape modelling) but these fail to capture detailed features that are clinically important.We present a supervised approach that combines both a non-linear generative shape model and a discriminative appearance-based convolutional neural network whilst quantifying uncertainty and relaxes the need for detailed, template based alignment for the training data. Our Bayesian framework couples the uncertainty from both the generator and the discriminator; our main contribution is the marginalisation of an intractable integral through the use of radial basis function approximations. We illustrate this model on the problem of segmenting bones from Psoriatic Arthritis hand radiographs and demonstrate that we can accurately measure the clinically important joint space gap between neighbouring bones.
keywords: shape models; uncertainty quantification; convolutional neural networks; radial basis function approximation; bone segmentation; psoriatic arthritis; hand radiographs

title: Evaluating Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Class Classification of Medical X-Ray Images
source: Future International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity (FICAC)
abstract: The demand for healthcare continues to promote the importance of intelligent systems that could effectively assist medical experts in disease diagnosis. However, discrepancies and errors are often caused by subjective interpretation by radiologists of medical X-ray images, hence creating a dire need for more accurate and automated diagnostic tools. The work Multi-Class Classification of Medical X-ray Images addresses this challenge by providing a comprehensive solution for the analysis of medical X-ray images using advanced deep learning technologies. Unlike previous studies that usually focus on a single disease, this project tackles multiple diseases simultaneously, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, and osteoarthritis, offering a more versatile and scalable diagnostic tool. The system utilizes CNNs for the detection and classification of these diseases with high accuracy. This project compares three deep learning architectures: Custom CNN, VGG-16, and ResNet on a diverse set of medical X-ray datasets, which yields an overall accuracy of 94.48% with the VGG-16 model, outperforming both Custom CNN, which has an accuracy of 92%, and ResNet, which has an accuracy of 87%. It also does pretty well in precision, recall, and F1-score, particularly for normal X-rays (F1-score: 0.99 for VGG-16) and diseases like pneumonia (F1-score: 0.93) and tuberculosis (F1-score: 0.93). The difference of this work with the related works is the multi-disease approach and the comparative evaluation of several models. Whereas most of the previous works generally dealt with single diseases, the proposed system gives a holistic approach to multiple conditions, hence finding extreme applicability in realistic clinical scenarios. Advanced preprocessing techniques that were used in this study included grayscale conversion, resizing, and normalization, accompanied by fine-tuning and augmentation of the data to ensure each category of the diseases showed very high performance. The system further outperforms other approaches by being able to handle class imbalance problems and showing much better performance on the detection of complex cases like moderate osteoarthritis. The result is saving much precious time taken by health professionals in diagnosis and also helping patients with more complete and timely information about their condition. This indeed averts much-undue anxiety among patients and improves the overall healthcare outcome. This project really shows how AI can improve the experiences of patients seeking healthcare with a reliable, efficient, and correct diagnosis capable of dealing with many diseases in a single framework.
keywords: tuberculosis; pneumonia; osteoarthritis; VGG16; ResNet; custom CNN; model comparison; class imbalance; data augmentation; automated diagnosis; chest radiography

title: An Intelligent Knee Osteoarthritis Disease Prediction using Hybrid Deep Learning with Classification Principles
source: International Conference on Frontier Technologies and Solutions (ICFTS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a prevalent degenerative joint disease that significantly impacts patient mobility and quality of life.This study presents a novel hybrid deep learning approach that integrates a LeNet-based Convolutional Neural Network with a Random Forest classifier for predicting knee osteoarthritis severity. The model leverages robust feature extraction from knee X-ray images and couples it with ensemble classification to yield highly accurate predictions. Extensive cross-validation experiments demonstrated an overall accuracy of 93.3%, with sensitivity and specificity values of 92.0% and 93.9%, respectively, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.95. These performance metrics underscore the model's strong discriminative power in differentiating between various osteoarthritis grades. The methodology incorporates meticulous data preprocessing, augmentation, and hyperparameter tuning to address the challenges posed by variations in image quality and patient demographics. The promising results indicate that the hybrid Lenet-RF model is a potent tool for early and reliable disease detection, potentially leading to improved clinical outcomes. Overall, this approach not only outperforms traditional standalone models but also offers a scalable solution for real-time clinical diagnostics, paving the way for its integration into routine healthcare practices.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; knee X-ray images; LeNet; convolutional neural networks; random forest; hybrid deep learning model; ensemble classification; image feature extraction; early disease detection; diagnosis

title: A Comprehensive Review on Knee Osteoarthritis Classification Using Machine Learning Techniques
source: International Conference on Internet of Things: Smart Innovation and Usages (IoT-SIU)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disorder that considerably affects quality of life. Precise evaluation of KOA severity is essential for efficient treatment planning and management. This research introduces an innovative method for categorizing the severity of knee osteoarthritis through sophisticated image processing and machine learning approaches. Early and correct categorization of OA severity is critical for timely intervention and therapy planning. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a useful method for automating the diagnosis and categorization of knee OA, leveraging medical imaging data and clinical factors. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current ML techniques applied to knee $\mathbf{O A}$ classification, highlighting advancements in feature extraction, image preprocessing, model selection, and performance evaluation. The paper also explores the role of deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), in enhancing diagnostic accuracy. Challenges such as data imbalance, lack of standardized datasets, and model interpretability are discussed, along with potential solutions. Finally, the review outlines promising directions for future research, emphasizing the integration of multi-modal data and explainable AI for improved clinical applicability.

title: AI-Powered Diagnostic Tool for Early Osteoporosis Prediction: Development and Insights
source: International Conference on Metaverse and Current Trends in Computing (ICMCTC)
abstract: Osteoporosis, a widespread and debilitating condition characterised by weakened bones, significantly increases the risk of fractures, especially among the elderly. Early detection is crucial to managing and mitigating the disease's progression. This study presents the development of an intelligent diagnostic tool that leverages artificial intelligence (AI) to predict osteoporosis in its early stages. The proposed system integrates advanced machine learning algorithms with X-ray images of knee bone datasets to assess bone health, identify at-risk individuals, and accurately predict the onset of osteoporosis. By using deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), the model analyses medical images, bone mineral density (BMD) scans, and other clinical indicators to detect subtle patterns indicative of bone deterioration. The AI-based system outperforms traditional diagnostic methods in terms of accuracy of 98% and early-stage prediction, offering a non-invasive, cost-effective solution for healthcare providers. The tool can aid clinicians in making timely decisions regarding preventive interventions, ultimately reducing the incidence of fractures and improving patient outcomes. This research underscores the potential of AI in enhancing healthcare analytics and delivering predictive solutions for chronic conditions like osteoporosis.
