title: AI-Driven Transformer Model for Knee Arthritis Detection: Advancements in X-ray-Based Diagnosis and Severity Classification
source: IEEE International Conference on Emerging Computing and Intelligent Technologies (ICoECIT)
abstract: Knee arthritis functions as a degenerative joint condition which creates strong impact on joint movement and patient lifestyle quality. Medical professionals need early and precise arthritis severity assessment through X-ray imaging to facilitate appropriate medical actions and care design. CNNs and other basic deep learning frameworks have demonstrated successful performance in medical image evaluation yet experience challenges when identifying extensive interconnections and intricate configurations. The research explores transformer models as a solution for knee arthritis recognition and image-based severity assessment through X-ray scans. The proposed approach adopts Swin Transformer because it conducts hierarchical feature processing with global context preservation capabilities. Research prepared and tested their model by processing X-ray images from public databases through enhanced contrast along with augmented data normalization techniques. The research findings demonstrate transformer models achieve superior performance than convolutional neural networks by providing both higher total precision and adaptability to images and better detection accuracy when used for classification. Modern research has utilized AI transformers to enable better automated arthritis diagnosis capabilities thus developing new prospects in medical imaging.
keywords: knee arthritis; X-ray images; Swin Transformer; transformer models; automated diagnosis; medical image analysis; data augmentation; image normalization

title: Transforming Precision: A Comparative Analysis of Vision Transformers, CNNs, and Traditional ML for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Diagnosis
source: International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Information Communication Technology
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease that can cause severe pain and impairment. With increased prevalence, precise diagnosis by medical imaging analytics is crucial for appropriate illness management. This research investigates a comparative analysis between traditional machine learning techniques and new deep learning models for diagnosing knee osteoarthritis severity from X-ray pictures. This study does not introduce new architectural innovations but rather illuminates the robust applicability and comparative effectiveness of preexisting ViT models in a medical imaging context, specifically for knee osteoarthritis severity diagnosis. The insights garnered from this comparative analysis advocate for the integration of advanced ViT models in clinical diagnostic workflows, potentially revolutionizing the precision and reliability of knee osteoarthritis assessments. This study does not introduce new architectural innovations but rather illuminates the robust applicability and comparative effectiveness of pre-existing ViT models in a medical imaging context, specifically for knee osteoarthritis severity diagnosis. The insights garnered from this comparative analysis advocate for the integration of advanced ViT models in clinical diagnostic workflows, potentially revolutionizing the precision and reliability of knee osteoarthritis assessments. The study utilizes an osteoarthritis dataset from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) comprising images with 5 severity categories and uneven class distribution. While classic machine learning models like GaussianNB and KNN struggle in feature extraction, Convolutional Neural Networks such as Inception-V3 and VGG-19 achieve better accuracy between 55–65% by learning hierarchical visual patterns. However, Vision Transformer architectures like Da-VIT, GCViT and MaxViT emerge as indisputable champions, displaying 66.14% accuracy, 0.703 precision, 0.614 recall, and AUC exceeding 0.835 thanks to self-attention processes. This analysis strongly promotes the deployment of sophisticated vision transformers over CNNs and traditional ML for increased precision in knee osteoarthritis diagnosis using X-ray picture categorization.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity classification; X-ray images; vision transformer; convolutional neural networks; traditional machine learning; Osteoarthritis Initiative; class imbalance; self-attention; medical image classification

title: A Deep Neural Network Based on Masked Strategy and Fuzzy Pooling for Diagnosing Osteoarthritis in X-Ray Images
source: IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems
abstract: The computer-aided diagnostic method based on deep learning can automatically identify whether X-ray images exhibit symptoms of osteoarthritis, thereby improving the quality and speed of early osteoarthritis diagnosis. However, osteoarthritis involves changes in structures such as soft tissue and joint spaces, and X-ray images of osteoarthritis have low contrast and high noise. These factors can blur the boundaries of osteoarthritic lesion areas, making feature extraction from X-ray images of osteoarthritis relatively difficult. In addition, the max-pooling operation in previous models tends to lose details and positional information in X-ray images, reducing the model's sensitivity to osteoarthritic structure features. To address the two issues in the diagnosis model mentioned above, we propose a deep neural network based on a masked strategy and fuzzy pooling (DNNMSFP) to automatically diagnose bone joint X-ray images to observe whether the image exhibits arthritis symptoms. The DNNMSFP model integrates the advantages of masked autoencoders and fuzzy pooling to address the aforementioned issues. First, the DNNMSFP model uses a self-supervised feature learning module designed using a masked strategy to learn effective features from noisy X-ray images. Furthermore, the DNNMSFP model replaces the max-pooling operation of the original feature learner with fuzzy pooling. Fuzzy pooling is a variant of traditional pooling operations that performs Gaussian blurring on pixel values in feature maps to extract features and reduce dimensionality. Comprehensive experiments on a real bone joint X-ray image dataset validate the superiority of the DNNMSFP model. Specifically, the DNNMSFP model achieves an excellent prediction performance on the real dataset, with precision, recall, and accuracy of 0.974, 0.948, and 0.965, respectively.
keywords: osteoarthritis diagnosis; X-ray images; computer-aided diagnosis; masked autoencoder; self-supervised feature learning; Gaussian smoothing; early osteoarthritis detection

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Detection of Knee Joint Injuries: A Comprehensive Review
source: International Conference on Recent Trends in Electrical, Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICRTEECT)
abstract: Knee joint injuries are a leading cause of musculoskeletal disorders, affecting millions worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as clinical examination and radiographic imaging, often have constraints in terms of performance parameters. Past one-decade, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has shown immense potential in enhancing the performing of diagnosis of knee joint injuries. The Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models are applied to medical images from modalities viz. X-ray, MRI, and CT scans for the detection of knee disorders. Common knee injuries include knee osteoarthritis (KOA), Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) tears, meniscal injuries, and fractures. This paper reviews the current state of AI applications in knee joint injury detection, AI models used, their advantages, challenges, and prospects. The findings suggest that AI can significantly enhance diagnostic performance, decrease detection time, speedup clinical decision-making, despite challenges related to data quality, interpretability, and generalization.
keywords: knee injury; artificial intelligence; knee osteoarthritis; anterior cruciate ligament rupture; meniscal injury; knee fractures; medical image analysis; magnetic resonance imaging; X-rays; computed tomography; deep learning; machine learning; computer-aided diagnosis; clinical decision support

title: Automated Deep Learning Based Knee Osteoarthritis Joint Extraction and Classification
source: International Conference on Open Source Systems and Technologies (ICOSST)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a widespread global condition, impacting over 300 million individuals as per the World Health Organization (WHO). Particularly prevalent among older adults, knee OA is a prominent cause of disability. Its occurrence increases with age, especially after 50, and is more frequent in women, particularly post-menopause. Several studies have been carried out so far for automated grading and classification of knee osteoarthritis (KOA), but none of them built strong foundations enough to make this system automated. This study focuses on machine-controlled knee joint extraction and grading classification with improved accuracy and performance. We used the osteoarthritis initiative (OAI) dataset of X-ray images for our study. Initially, a single-stage detector is used for joint extraction of the knee area as the X-ray images contain entire knees with both joints. Enhanced osteoarthritis feature extraction (OAFE) and osteoarthritis dimensionality reduction (OADR) blocks are used for grading classification. We have significantly improved state-of-the-art results. We have acquired joint extraction with a mean average precision (map) of 95.3% and grading classification accuracy of 78.93%. Furthermore, the performance due to the dimensionality reduction block has improved by a huge factor.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis grading; X-ray images; automated image analysis; feature extraction; dimensionality reduction; knee joint segmentation

title: Enhancing Knee Osteoarthritis Detection and Severity Grading Using Deep Learning and DenseNet169
source: International Conference on Computing, Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research project enhances knee osteoarthritis (KOA) detection using DenseNet169, a deep convolutional neural network. We introduce a novel adaptive early-stopping technique combined with gradual cross-entropy loss estimation to optimize training epochs and mitigate overfitting risks. Evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall demonstrate the model’s superiority over existing methods. DenseNet169, empowered by these adaptive techniques, achieves an exceptional 95% accuracy, surpassing previous models and underscoring its effectiveness in OA diagnosis. The study highlights the importance of accurate diagnostic tools in improving outcomes for KOA patients. Our versatile dataset supports both knee joint detection and OA severity grading in X-ray images, significantly impacting medical imaging and health informatics. Detailed sections on methodology, experimental design, findings, and commentary provide comprehensive insights into the research’s contributions and implications for advancing OA diagnosis and treatment.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; DenseNet169; overfitting reduction; X-ray image analysis; computer-aided diagnosis

title: Knee Osteoarthritis Image Classification Based on A Novel Multi-granularity Feature Fusion Network
source: IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent muscu-loskeletal disorder, and the accuracy of its clinical diagnosis often relies on the subjective experience of radiologists. Automated grading of KOA severity with computer assistance holds immense potential as an efficient solution to this challenge. However, previous methods primarily rely on convolutional neural network (CNN) and overlook the limitations of convolutional kernels in extracting global information from knee joint images. Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) effectively improves the global feature extraction performance by transferring and aggregating information through connections between different nodes. In this study, a KOA image classification method based on a novel multi-granularity feature fusion network is proposed by combining CNN and GCN. Firstly, GCN is used to further learn features from different layers of the CNN, aiming to simultaneously capture local and global information from each layer. Then, a spatial attention mechanism is introduced to fuse features of different layers and granularities to effectively alleviate the interference of redundant information. Finally, considering the problem of imbalanced dataset distribution, a specific loss function is introduced to balance the performance of the model on majority and minority classes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other comparable methods with a superior five-class classification accuracy of 0.746.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis severity grading; radiographic image classification; multi-granularity feature fusion; graph convolutional networks; convolutional neural networks; spatial attention mechanism; class imbalance; loss function design; local and global feature extraction

title: Analytical Inverse Kinematics for a Prismatic-Revolute Hybrid Joints Radiography Robot Mounted on the Ambulance
source: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
abstract: Installing digital subtraction angiography (DSA) equipment in an ambulance can provide crucial image guidance for the emergency medical service of cardiovascular diseases. However, the commonly used C-arm is too large to be directly installed in a narrow ambulance. This article presents a compact redundant prismatic-revolute hybrid joints radiography robot that can be installed inside an ambulance to provide DSA imaging. An analytical solution, along with a self-motion algorithm based on the continuous quantum particle swarm algorithm, is proposed to achieve accurate motion control and real-time joint avoidance for the radiography robot. The experimental results indicate that the maximum error of the radiography robot is 0.42 mm, which meets the requirements for DSA image collection. During the in vivo experiment, DSA images provided by the radiography robot guided the successful placement of a stent in the internal thoracic artery of a beagle. This verifies the feasibility of the proposed analytical solution in ensuring accurate motion control of the radiography robot.
keywords: inverse kinematics; digital subtraction angiography; C-arm; redundant manipulators; internal mammary artery

title: Deep learning-based analysis on X-ray images of full lower limbs
source: International Conference on Mechanical and Electronics Engineering
abstract: This study proposes an automated deep learning-based method for segmenting full lower limb X-ray images and calculating critical angles required in preoperative planning for High Tibial Osteotomy (HTO). The method utilizes an improved U-Net architecture, enabling accurate segmentation of the femur, tibia, fibula, and joint space. After segmentation, affine registration is applied to the resulting point cloud data, and key reference points are manually integrated to calculate the mechanical angles needed for surgery. Experimental results indicate that the proposed model achieves an average Intersection Over Union (mIOU) of 89.23% and pixel accuracy (mPA) of 94.63%, outperforming widely used models such as the standard U-Net (mIOU: 86.36%) and DeepLabv3-Net (mIOU: 81.21%) in segmentation accuracy. Additionally, the proposed method reaches a precision of 93.13%, significantly surpassing other baseline models. Compared to conventional manual methods, this automated preoperative planning process reduces the average processing time per image to 1 second, resulting in an approximate 98.33% improvement in efficiency. This approach demonstrates high accuracy, speed, and reliability in High Tibial Osteotomy preoperative planning. Future work will focus on enhancing the model’s robustness and adaptability to accommodate a wider range of imaging types and clinical scenarios.
keywords: high tibial osteotomy; surgical planning; bone segmentation; U-Net; affine registration; point cloud registration; knee joint; femur; tibia; fibula

title: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Detection of Knee Osteoarthritis Disease through Mobile Apps
source: International Conference on Wireless and Telematics (ICWT)
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by damage to joint cartilage and structural joint diarthrodial. As many as 80% of osteoarthritis patients will experience movement limitations, and 25% cannot carry out daily activities. At present, the stages of osteoarthritis diagnosis are through visual observations of the narrowing of joint and osteophyte gaps contained in X-ray images through the observation of radiology and assessing the severity of disorders. This study proposes a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) support system to detect knee osteoarthritis based on X-ray images with deep learning (DL) techniques. In the design of the CAD-related architecture evaluation, including ResNet, VggNet, EfficientNet, and InceptionV3 in building a predictive model using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based on Mobile Application and Cloud Computing to be able to classify normal knee and knee osteoarthritis with the percentage of testing accuracy each architecture is 93.17% on ResNet, 95.26% on VggNet, 94.64% in InceptionV3 and 96.59% on EfficientNet. The experimental results can be found through our project channel: https://youtu.be/EXj-7Dv6xGM
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; computer-aided diagnosis; X-ray image classification; convolutional neural networks; ResNet; VGG; EfficientNet; InceptionV3; mobile health apps; cloud computing; osteophytes; radiographic diagnosis

title: Adversarial Evolving Neural Network for Longitudinal Knee Osteoarthritis Prediction
source: IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) as a disabling joint disease has doubled in prevalence since the mid-20th century. Early diagnosis for the longitudinal KOA grades has been increasingly important for effective monitoring and intervention. Although recent studies have achieved promising performance for baseline KOA grading, longitudinal KOA grading has been seldom studied and the KOA domain knowledge has not been well explored yet. In this paper, a novel deep learning architecture, namely adversarial evolving neural network (A-ENN), is proposed for longitudinal grading of KOA severity. As the disease progresses from mild to severe level, ENN involves the progression patterns for accurately characterizing the disease by comparing an input image it to the template images of different KL grades using convolution and deconvolution computations. In addition, an adversarial training scheme with a discriminator is developed to obtain the evolution traces. Thus, the evolution traces as fine-grained domain knowledge are further fused with the general convolutional image representations for longitudinal grading. Note that ENN can be applied to other learning tasks together with existing deep architectures, in which the responses characterize progressive representations. Comprehensive experiments on the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset were conducted to evaluate the proposed method. An overall accuracy was achieved as 62.7%, with the baseline, 12-month, 24-month, 36-month, and 48-month accuracy as 64.6%, 63.9%, 63.2%, 61.8% and 60.2%, respectively.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; longitudinal disease progression; evolving neural networks; adversarial training; Osteoarthritis Initiative; knee MRI; disease severity classification

title: Automated Diagnosis of Knee Osteoarthritis: A Stacked Ensemble Deep Learning Approach With Explainable AI Techniques
source: IEEE Access
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a widespread degenerative joint disease that poses significant global challenges owing to delayed diagnosis and treatment, often resulting in severe disability. Despite extensive research on predicting KOA, many proposed methods lack reliability, because they fail to incorporate explainable AI (XAI) methodologies, robust preprocessing techniques, and appropriate hyperparameter tuning. This study introduces a deep learning framework for KOA classification, addressing both binary (diagnosis) and multi-class (severity prediction) classification tasks using the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset. Our approach is enhanced by a comprehensive image prepocessing pipeline that includes scaling, sharpening, denoising, histogram equalization, and contrast enhancement, which standardizes image quality and highlights crucial features for classification. The proposed stacked ensemble model, which integrates Xception, EfficientNetB5, and InceptionV3, surpasses individual models, achieving 86.29% accuracy in KOA diagnosis and 96.93% in KOA severity prediction. To ensure transparency and interpretability, we incorporated advanced explainability tools, including Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), Faster Score-CAM, and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), providing clear visual insights into the model’s decision-making process. Our findings present a balanced approach that combines performance with transparency, potentially leading to earlier and more accurate KOA diagnoses.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; automated diagnosis; stacking ensemble; explainable AI; Grad-CAM; lime; Xception; EfficientNetB5; InceptionV3; knee X-ray images

title: A Comparative Study for Optimizing Deep Learning Frameworks for Precise Osteoarthritis Prediction in X-Ray Images
source: International Conference on Smart Systems and Inventive Technology (ICSSIT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a condition that affects the knee joint, causing pain, stiffness, and loss of mobility, and is one of the most common musculoskeletal conditions. It is desirable to correctly recognize KOA from knee X-ray images for timely clinical intervention. In this research, different Deep Learning (DL) architectures have been studied to evaluate their ability in automated KOA detection in knee X-ray images. To compare five models (CNN, VGG16, ResNet, MobileNet, and DenseNet), a common framework was used. To enhance feature learning, more layers, including Conv2D, Global Average Pooling, Dropout, and Dense layers, were added to the base architectures. The dataset was preprocessed before training, including resizing, normalizing, and augmenting. The models' performance was evaluated using metrics. The experiments showed significant differences among the architectures considered. CNN had the worst classification accuracy, but better feature extraction capability in deeper architectures. The highest-performing model overall was the modified ResNet, with accuracies of 89.66% on the test set and 89.82% on the validation set. The residual learning mechanism enabled more stable training and the maintenance of radiographic characteristics of KOA. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using ResNet-based architectures as computer-aided tools for KOA screening of knee x-ray images and their ability to support clinicians in decision-making.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis detection; knee X-ray images; radiographic classification; ResNet; deep learning architecture comparison; computer-aided diagnosis; residual learning; image augmentation; feature extraction

title: MedCAM-OsteoCls: Medical Context Aware Multimodal Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis
source: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative musculoskeletal joint disorder that significantly impacts middle-aged and elderly individuals. Although X-rays and MRIs are clinically used to identify such disorders, combining these imaging modalities is challenging due to the distinct nature of the data, as MRI volume provides detailed views of cartilage and soft tissues, while X-rays offer a global perspective of bone anatomy and positioning in single scan. In this context, the proposed work aims to address two key challenges: (1) how to automatically select the most informative slices from large and dis-organized MRI volume in a clinically relevant way and (2) how to effectively capture the discriminative multimodal interactions between X-ray and MRI modalities. In order to solve these issues, the Context-Guided Slice Selection and Prioritization (CG-SSP) module and Xray-MRI Cross-Attention (XMRCA) module are proposed. The CG-SSP module focuses on rejecting non-efficient slices and prioritizing the efficient slices in a multi-stage approach, first by segmenting the Femoral Cartilage (FC) then extracting the sequential patches of FC located in each MRI slice followed by assigning the attention weight to each of these slices based on learned structural complexity, while the XMRCA module focuses on learning the global interactions between X-ray and MRI feature space in a computationally efficient manner. Overall, the proposed model achieved an accuracy improvement of 2.66% over the state-of-the-art in unimodal and multimodal baselines on the OAI dataset. The proposed model identifies key diagnostic slices from MRI and can provide valuable insights into interactions between X-ray and MRI data for radiological KOA diagnosis in an end-to-end manner. Code will be made available at: https://github.com/adaydar/MedCAM-OsteoCls
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; multimodal medical image classification; slice selection; cross-attention; radiographic diagnosis

title: Next Generation AI-Enhanced Intelligent Imaging for Automated Knee X-ray Interpretation in Osteoarthritis: Front office Integration and Employee Training
source: Modern Electronics Devices and Intelligent Communication Systems (MEDCOM)
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a long-lasting musculoskeletal ailment in which the degenerative alterations in the cartilage of the articles progressively arise. As the pathological anatomy develops to bone structure degeneration, it results in pain, stiffness and functional impairment. It results in immobility, reduced quality of life, more susceptibility to fractures, hospitalization, and mental health problems in the older adults and postmenopausal women. To address the increasing global prevalence of OA and the necessity to diagnose X-rays of the knee promptly, affordably and accessibly, this paper presents an AI-based imaging system based on the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and compares their results with the existing machine learning models. The framework will be structured to integrate the front-office workflows and streamline the diagnostic process of patient registration to report delivery and establish a well-organized staff training ecosystem aimed at enabling clinical staff to operate the AI-enabled workflow and adapt to it. The study offers a comprehensive, deployment ready, diagnostic platform through advanced automation, user oriented front-office functionality and the consistent upskilling of the workforce, to provide scalable, precise, cost effective OA detection, clinical efficiency, interpretative variability reduction, and workforce transition to scalable intelligent, patient centred care.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; AI-assisted diagnosis; convolutional neural networks; radiographic image analysis; employee training; clinical workflow automation

title: Anatomical Landmark Localization for Knee X-ray Images via Heatmap Regression Refined with Graph Convolutional Network
source: International Congress on Image and Signal Processing (CISP)
abstract: Accurate detection of anatomical landmarks for knee X-ray images holds paramount significance for the comprehensive assessment of knee osteoarthritis. Nevertheless, prevailing heatmap regression methodologies often fall short in fully leveraging the holistic structural information of landmarks, leading to potential inaccuracies in offsets owing to predicted integer coordinates. In this paper, we present a sophisticated end-to-end differential landmark localization model which amalgamates heatmap regression with a graph convolution network to precisely pinpoint anatomical landmarks in knee joint X-ray images. Our innovative approach represents the landmarks as a graph, enabling the capture of crucial structural information. It progressively refines the initially coarse integer landmark coordinates derived from heatmaps using cascade GCNs. Additionally, we incorporate the attention layer within the feature sampling module to augment the precision of regression outcomes. Our method attains remarkable results on the OAI dataset, achieving the Mean Radial Error of 0.84mm and the Successful Detection Rate of 71.18% at 1mm. These outcomes surpass the performance of alternative heatmap regression methods, significantly contributing to the facilitation of osteoarthritis assessment.
keywords: knee X-ray images; heatmap regression; graph convolutional networks; attention mechanism

title: Detection of Knee Osteoarthritis Using the Xception Model and Voting Classifier
source: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Trends and Pattern Recognition (ICAITPR)
abstract: The work proposed here deals with the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis by using X-ray images. Since they are the cheapest and most commonly used for evaluating the health of the knee joint, X-ray images are preferred more often. Currently available image processing techniques lack in terms of precision and sensitivity. For that purpose, a novel method has been developed, which is a custom implementation of Deep learning model coupled with a voting classifier to identify minute features. In this model, we have explored various models that's been customized specially for image classification. This would improve robustness in feature detection.The aim of the proposed model is the accurate detection and grading of the severity of knee osteoarthritis based on the Kellgren and Lawrence system. It is achieved using a combination of advanced classification models, such as Xception and InceptionV3, and efficient object detection frameworks, like YOLOv5 and YOLOv8. A user-friendly interface is developed using Flask to ensure smooth and reliable test conditions while interacting with the diagnostic system. Key concepts used in this study include deep learning, multi-scale features, machine learning, and human-computer interaction.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray image classification; Xception; voting classifier; InceptionV3; YOLOv5; YOLOv8; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; osteoarthritis severity grading; medical image diagnosis; Flask web interface

title: Detection of Osteoarthritis by using Multiple Edge Detections
source: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
abstract: Nowadays, Arthritis is a common disease among older people that influences the joints. It creates ache and inflammation, making it tough to walk, run or live active. Estimating the quantity or thickness of cartilage on the knee is critical for figuring out arthritis. In this study, MRI scans of the knee had been analyzed. Before segmentation, the picture is preprocessed with B-Splines creation. After that, canny and log facet detectors are used to obtain the boundaries or sharp edges or high variations in the grey values in the image. The proposed method extracts the cartilage thickness which plays a key role in determining the Osteoarthritis. The variety of pixels among edges is used to calculate the thickness. The abnormality of arthritis is then decided primarily based relating to the thickness of cartilage. The Joint Space Width (JSW) acquired is contrasted with standard joint space width esteem, 5.7mm for male and 4.8 mm for female. From this, the osteoarthritic knee can be distinguished from typical knee. This is a brief and smooth method to assess arthritis by relying on the thickness (viscosity) of the cartilage.
keywords: osteoarthritis detection; knee cartilage thickness; edge detection; Canny edge detection; Laplacian of Gaussian; joint space width; cartilage thickness measurement

title: A Task Scheduling Algorithm for Robotized X-Ray Tomography
source: International Conference on Robotics and Automation Engineering (ICRAE)
abstract: This paper addresses the Synchronized Dual-Arm Robotic Task Scheduling Problem (RTSP), which requires the synchronization between two robotic arms and the optimization of task sequences. We introduce MaxMatRTSP, a novel algorithm designed to handle the synchronization requirements of dualarm robotic systems where both arms must reach multiple successive target positions simultaneously. The algorithm integrates inverse kinematics, task configuration selection, task sequencing and motion planning to minimize both planning and execution durations while maintaining synchronized movements between the robots. Simulations and real-world validation using a robotic cell with two ABB IRB 4600 robots demonstrate the effectiveness of MaxMatRTSP in significantly reducing planning and execution durations compared to existing methods from the literature. The results confirm that MaxMatRTSP provides a robust solution for synchronized dual-arm task scheduling, making it well-suited for industrial applications such as X-ray tomography.
keywords: dual-arm robot; robot synchronization; inverse kinematics; task sequencing; motion planning; X-ray tomography; robotic cell

title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Acetabular Component Diameter Prediction in Total Hip Arthroplasty
source: IEEE Colombian Conference on Applications of Computational Intelligence (ColCACI)
abstract: Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) is widely used to treat conditions such as osteoarthritis, osteonecrosis, and rheumatoid arthritis. Its success relies on accurate preoperative planning, especially the selection of appropriate prosthetic components based on patient-specific anatomical dimensions. Manual planning using radiographic templates is prone to errors caused by image magnification and operator variability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework for predicting the acetabular cup diameter. The approach combines automated hip-structure segmentation using a U-Net with patient sex data in a deep regression network, providing a more precise and reproducible method for preoperative THA planning. The segmentation model achieved a global Dice coefficient of 0.886 ± 0.003, and the multimodal regressor reached R2= 0.604 for acetabular cup diameter prediction.
keywords: total hip arthroplasty; surgical planning; U-Net; multimodal regression

title: An Optimized YOLO Model with Local Attention for Arthritis Lesion Detection on X-Ray Images
source: International Annual Conference on Complex Systems and Intelligent Science (CSIS-IAC)
abstract: In the field of medical image processing and analysis, automated lesion detection in arthritis is crucial for clinical diagnostic assistance and presents a challenging task. To enhance the performance of automated detection, we integrated a Criss-Cross attention module into the YOLOv8 model in object detection within X-ray images of hand joints, which was aimed at better capturing pathological features between hand joints. We analyzed the relationship between the two distinct methods of utilizing attention, specifically extracting global attention weights and extracting local attention weights, and the features exhibited by arthritis, comparing the impact of different attention mechanisms on arthritis lesion detection within the object detection task. Specifically, we validated our approach on large-scale medical datasets for Osteoarthritis (OA) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that utilizing attention weights to extract attention within specific local regions in the YOLOv8 model yields superior results in arthritis lesion detection compared to using no attention mechanism or extracting global attention weights.
keywords: YOLOv8; criss-cross attention; local attention; X-ray images; osteoarthritis; rheumatoid arthritis; object detection; attention mechanism

title: Advanced Knee Osteoarthritis Detection using Deep Learning
source: IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This present research investigates the use of machine learning and deep learning models for the detection of knee osteoarthritis using the X-Ray images in depth. knee osteoarthritis is one of the most common joint disorders which affects numerous percentages of people across the world. And its detection of it at an early stage is very critical for effective management. This paper presents valuable dataset of X-ray images with a dual focus on detection of knee joint and KellgrenLawrence grading [kl]. The methodology which is proposed in this paper includes basic steps such as data loading and preprocessing. It also includes feature extraction and utilization of models of both machine and deep learning. In the phase of machine learning models which are used are Decision tree, KNN, MLP, Random Forest and ensemble methods. While in deep learning models used for evaluation are Nasnetmobile, VGG19, Darknet53, Darknet19 and Googlenet. The output of all the above-mentioned models are compared and evaluated based on four most important metrics of performance. The final output of the research shows that Random Forest and the Ensemble methods have outperformed in the phase of machine learning and when it comes to deep learning Googlenet and Darknet53 have done well in comparison. This study helps in the early detection of the knee osteoarthritis and also helps in management of it by giving valuable insights to medical practitioners and researchers.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; Kellgren-Lawrence grade; early disease detection; computer-aided diagnosis; convolutional neural networks; random forest; ensemble methods; image classification

title: Hybrid CNN–LSTM-based Vibroarthrography Signal Analysis for Automated Osteoarthritis Detection and Stage Classification
source: International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is yet to be accurately detected and assessed based on its severity because of the low-level differences in radiographs and subjective interpretation of imaging results. Most of the current deep learning approaches are based only on convolutional architectures, and this implies that they are incapable of differentiating similar stages of diseases. In order to overcome this drawback, the hybrid deep learning system is proposed to detect and classify the stage of osteoarthritis. The suggested implementation combines convolutional neural networks in discriminatory spatial feature extraction with long short-term memory networks in capturing structured dependencies in learned representations. A publicly available knee osteoarthritis dataset has been experimented with showing a multiclass classification accuracy of 94.2% with binary osteoarthritis detection showing an AUC of 0.94. Ablation analysis also proves the fact that the hybrid architecture has the best performance in comparison with the baseline convolutional models. These findings suggest that the suggested framework is a valid and objective tool of computer-aided osteoarthritis measurement, which can enhance better clinical decision-making.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis detection; vibroarthrography; CNN-LSTM hybrid model; radiographic evaluation; computer-aided diagnosis; multi-class classification; ablation study

title: Automated Arthritis Detection from X-Ray Images Using Efficientnet B3 and Image Processing
source: IEEE International Conference on Emerging Trends in Computing and Communication (ETCOM)
abstract: Deep learning algorithms have recently received substantial interest for detecting arthritis automatically in medical imaging context. The proposed research introduces a solid methodology to identify arthritis by applying deep learning algorithms to analyzed X-ray scans of bones. The processing method starts with an image preparation process consisting of histogram normalization and noise reduction alongside normalization along with segmentation which improves image quality. The EfficientNet-B3 model analyzes preprocessed images as its input because it represents a state-of-the-art CNN implementation that delivers high efficiency in medical image classification tasks. Using blocks with different convolutional kernel dimensions and resolutions the model learns complex representations of arthritis-pattern distribution in its deep feature extraction process. The feature maps proceed to a classification section that generates predictions for arthritis existence or non-existence. The classification process forms two output groups which include “Arthritis” and “No Arthritis.” The proposed model uses deep learning technology together with optimal image preprocessing capabilities to enhance arthritis detection accuracy and thus help doctors with early diagnosis and medical decision support. EfficientNet-B3 provides the perfect equilibrium between processing speed and diagnostic outcomes which leads to its suitability in medical equipment handling biological data in real time. The proposed detection method demonstrates its ability to accurately identify arthritic conditions compared to normal cases according to experimental findings. Experiments were performed on various datasets where the proposed method achieved Based on the experimental results proposed method achieved a significant amount of accuracy compared to state of art methods.
keywords: X-ray images; EfficientNetB3; medical image classification; image preprocessing; histogram normalization; noise reduction; image segmentation; convolutional neural networks; early diagnosis; clinical decision support

title: Diagnosis of Degenerative Joint Disease of The Knee
source: International Conference on Multimedia Processing, Communication & Information Technology (MPCIT)
abstract: Osteoarthritis, the predominant form of degenerative joint disease, imposes a considerable global health burden. The proposed innovative diagnostic approach not only meets the critical need for accurate detection but also holds promise in unraveling the intricate complexities of osteoarthritis. By leveraging clinical assessments, imaging technologies, and laboratory tests, the proposed system brings forth a transformative methodology for the early detection of degenerative knee joint disease. Through the incorporation of deep learning algorithms that consider risk elements, the system facilitates timely interventions. In the medical field, this project aims to pioneer a groundbreaking diagnostic system for the precise identification of degenerative joint disease in the knee. This study presents a novel approach for the automated diagnosis of DJD using knee X-ray images. The objective is to develop a classification model capable of accurately categorizing knee X-ray images into five distinct classes representing different stages of DJD severity: class 0 (normal), class 1 (doubtful), class 2 (mild), class 3 (moderate), and class 4 (severe). By seamlessly integrating clinical assessments, advanced imaging techniques, and state-of-the-art laboratory tests, This comprehensive system employs deep learning algorithms to analyze a wealth of data, including risk factors. The ultimate goal is to significantly enhance accuracy in detecting degenerative knee joint disease and enabling early intervention by grading their severity. Dataset contains 3341 images of different categories like normal,doubtful,mild,moderate,severe. A custom CNN is used in this paper, optimizer Adam, loss function spatial cross entropy, batch size 32 and epochs 300.This model gives the accuracy of 82%.
keywords: osteoarthritis; knee osteoarthritis; knee X-ray images; automated diagnosis; disease severity classification; convolutional neural networks; early detection; clinical risk factors

title: DNN-based Knee Osteoarthritis Disease Detection using X-Rays
source: International Conference on Inventive Computation Technologies (ICICT)
abstract: A degenerative condition of the knee joint, knee osteoarthritis (KOA), is brought on by deterioration of the ligaments that unite the tibia bones and femur. Clinically, KOA is categorized into four classes according to the degree of degeneration of the connective tissue that connects these two bones, which limits range of motion. It is highly subjective and challenging to determine this interosseous region with a front X-ray examination of the knee. In the automatic separation and categorization of different knee tissues and structures, including soft tissue, bone, and cartilage, DNN has demonstrated promising results. This is important since it helps diagnose the degree and course of osteoarthritis. This research presents a deep learning method utilizing knee radiographs to automatically identify and rate the severity of KOA. Our structure of deep neural networks is capable of precisely identifying knee X-rays as either unaffected or KOA-affected and estimating the degree of KOA. Our deep neural network model was created utilizing a large collection of knee joint X-rays that had been expertly annotated by radiologists.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; knee radiographs; disease severity classification; cartilage segmentation; knee joint degeneration; deep neural network; computer-aided diagnosis

title: A Novel Approach for Detection of Hand Arthritis using Convolutional Neural Network
source: International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
abstract: Arthritis is becoming a more common disease across the globe. Different types of arthritis diseases are affecting the human body, they are osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis, within which the osteoarthritis is considered as the most common disease. The recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) will eventually result in a fully automated workflow, which outperforms human performance. Advanced neural networks can recognize objects present in the images and further the objects will be categorized more precisely and quickly than humans. This research study has attempted to implement the machine learning technique to classify and categorize the different stages of hand arthritis in patients. This research study also investigates how Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is used for the detection and classification of Osteoarthritis in a descriptive and comparative manner. Recognizing the precise segment of RA is a difficult task because human abilities will frequently limit the methods applied. The Convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to recognize multiple examples of hand reputation. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has the ability to recognize human traits and is anticipating the sophistication of hand radiographs from a large dataset. As a result, a research discussion of various arthritis detection techniques, feature extraction techniques, and classification schemes has been conducted.
keywords: hand osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis detection; rheumatoid arthritis; psoriatic arthritis; convolutional neural networks; hand radiographs; automated diagnosis

title: CNN-Based Classification of Knee Arthritis Severity from X-ray Images
source: International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
abstract: This research work represents a convolutional neural network (CNN) technique for knee arthritis classification from X-ray images. The knee arthritis X-ray images are classified into five classes: Normal, Doubtful, Mild, Moderate, and Severe. Resizing, normalizing, and furnishing the steps of pre-processing aided in enriching the dataset and generalizing the strength of the model. The CNN model was carefully designed with multiple convolutional, activation, and max-pooling layers, followed by dense layers with dropout regularization to alleviate excessive fitting. The model’s training and validation were done at an 80:20 split of the dataset, attaining a final test accuracy of $58 \%$. The study highlights the potential of CNNs in the classification of images, especially for detecting knee arthritis despite relatively moderate accuracy. The areas highlighted for refinement include the performance evaluation, comprising accuracy, precision, and F1-score. Further study will focus on enhancing the accuracy of the model across deeper architectures, including additional clinical data and integrating advanced techniques such as transfer learning. This study focuses on facilitating the generalization of diagnostic tool automation that aids clinical decision-making and enriches the outcomes of patients in the context of knee arthritis, promoting healthcare innovation, well-being, and reduced healthcare disparities.
keywords: knee arthritis; X-ray images; convolutional neural networks; automated diagnosis; radiographic image analysis; dropout regularization; transfer learning

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Knee Osteoarthritis Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
source: IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disorder that has a substantial worldwide ramification, especially among the geriatric population. It is distinguished by the gradual deterioration of cartilage in the knee joint, resulting in manifestations such as stiffness, discomfort, and diminished range of motion. Knee OA, as reported by the World Health Organization, is positioned within the leading ten causes of disability in developed nations. Classification and early detection of knee OA are essential for its effective management. Standard diagnostic techniques, including radiography and clinical examinations, are susceptible to subjectivity and may fail to identify OA in its early stages. In response, a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method for knee OA classification is introduced in this study. The CNN model is designed to derive detailed features from knee joint images using a dataset of 8381 images from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI), that is divided into training (5923 images) and testing (2458 images) sets. As evidenced by evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, the model effectively classifies different phases of knee OA. This strategy exhibits potential in enhancing clinical decision-making and tailoring treatment regimens for patients diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis classification; convolutional neural networks; Osteoarthritis Initiative; early detection; cartilage degeneration; radiographic images; disease severity staging

title: KOA Management in CDS using AI: A Review
source: International Conference on Smart Devices (ICSD)
abstract: Joint degradation is a symptom of osteoarthritis in the knee. In the entire world, it is the most common disease. KOA primarily affects elderly individuals even though life is tough at the KOA. Significant progress in artificial intelligence (AI) has been made in recent years; deep learning for picture categorization, lesion recognition, cartilage division, and future KOA development prediction models are among the most notable examples. In this study AI is used in detection and management of knee osteoarthritis based on various x-ray images. Now-a-days AI shows a great potential in the treatment of knee osteoarthritis. It's prerequisite to remember that these applications are still in their early days and need to be proved through real-life applications and clinical studies. The utility and accuracy of CDS for KOA will probably be improved by AI technologies. AI-powered CDS for osteoarthritis (OA) in the knee offers a lot of promise to help patients as well as physicians. In order to ensure the virtuous and proportionately deployment of AI in KOA treatment, it is imperative that this investigation address challenges with data integrity, ethics, privacy, and legal compliance. There is great opportunity for future research on knee OA in CDS to improve patient outcomes and our understanding of this chronic condition, as well as to increase the efficiency of healthcare delivery.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; clinical decision support systems; artificial intelligence; deep learning; radiographic image analysis; cartilage segmentation; joint space narrowing; data integrity; privacy and ethics; legal compliance

title: Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Network for Knee Segmentation: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
source: International Conference on Healthcare Engineering (ICHE)
abstract: Automated knee segmentation plays an important role in knee osteoarthritis diagnosis as this disease exhibits different imaging biomarkers as it progresses. A good knee segmentation model that is practical and computationally efficient allows a more efficient clinical workflow. This paper presents a preliminary study on Depthwise Separable convolutional layers utilizing the end-to-end segmentation network, UNet architecture on knee segmentation. Results showed that DS2D-UNet and DS3D-UNet perform more efficiently with the adoption of Depthwise Separable convolutional layers with fewer cost of computations, without compromising the overall performance. The models produced strong results of Balanced Accuracy ranging between 90–93% and Dice Similarity Coefficient ranging between 91–93%. In conclusion, the potential of Depthwise Separable convolution should be further investigated to optimize the efficiency of 3D deep learning architectures, specifically on knee imaging volumes.
keywords: depthwise separable convolution; U-Net; knee osteoarthritis; Osteoarthritis Initiative; 3D deep learning; computational efficiency; knee MRI; imaging biomarkers

title: Detection and Classification Knee Osteoarthritis Algorithm using YOLOv3 and VGG-16 Models
source: International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The paper proposes an algorithm to help doctors identify Knee Osteoarthritis automatically on X-ray images by deep learning method with the YOLOv3 model and VGG-16. We collect data including 2874 knee X-ray images taken from the OAI dataset which is a large data set of Knees and joints. In this paper, all data are labeled and tested by chiropractors at Bach Mai Hospital which will be preprocessed by applying the CLAHE algorithm to improve image quality. Next, the YOLOv3 modelis trained with a preprocessed dataset as input. It then predicts the location of the knee joint on the X-ray image automatically. Finally, we use VGG-16 to classify the image. Besides, we alsouse preprocessing methods to enhance the image quality before training, and thus the accuracy of the problem is also significantly improved. The results display that the proposed method achievesan accuracy of up to 89%
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; X-ray images; YOLOv3; VGG16; osteoarthritis classification; CLAHE image enhancement; computer-aided diagnosis

title: Automatic Segmentation of Finger Bone Regions from CR Image Using the Improved HRNet
source: International Conference on Control, Automation and Systems (ICCAS)
abstract: In Japan, it is serious problems such as increasing nursing care of handicapped people requiring and the aging of caregivers which is caused in a super-aging society. One of the main causes of being classified as persons requiring nursing care include joint diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and bone fractures due to osteoporosis. Early detection and treatment of these diseases are considered important. Rheumatoid arthritis and osteoporosis are generally diagnosed by simple X-ray examination. However, there are problems with radiographic diagnosis by physicians, such as lack of objectivity and reproducibility of diagnosis, and increased workload on the radiologists. To solve these problems, a Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) system is being developed. Because the CAD system may use the results of quantitative computer analysis, it is expected to improve the reproducibility and accuracy of diagnosis and reduce the burden on physicians. Therefore, this paper proposes a segmentation method of phalanx region from CR images to develop a CAD system. The proposed method is based on HRNet + JPU + U-Net. The proposed method was applied to 101 cases of X-ray images, and mIoU=0.897 was obtained. Experiments for segmentation from images confirmed the usefulness of the proposed method by improving the extraction accuracy of the boundary of the phalanx region.
keywords: finger bones; computer-aided diagnosis; rheumatoid arthritis; osteoporosis; X-ray images; HRNet; U-Net; joint diseases; nursing care

title: An Efficient Deep Learning Framework for Osteoarthritis Diagnosis: Leveraging the Strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers Through Ensemble Integration
source: International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) represents a gradual joint disease requiring precise diagnosis methods along with severity assessments for efficient medical care. The diagnosis of KOA can be automated using new deep learning techniques which include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs). The Knee Osteoarthritis Dataset with Severity contains five deep learning model tests which include Xception, EfficientNetV2B3, VGG19, VGG16 and ViT to detect knee osteoarthritis with success rates of 92.7%, 91.4%, 87.3% and 91.7% and 95.9% accordingly. An ensemble learning approach for classification brought an accuracy rate of 96.28% to the system. Building KOA diagnosis systems by combining multiple deep learning models leads to superior diagnostic accuracy while generating an advanced automated medical assessment strategy according to the results presented.
keywords: knee osteoarthritis; osteoarthritis diagnosis; automated diagnosis; convolutional neural networks; vision transformer; ensemble learning; image classification; disease severity assessment; medical image analysis

title: Automated Grade Classification of Ankle Osteoarthritis Using Advanced Neural Network Classifier
source: Multimedia University Engineering Conference (MECON)
abstract: Ankle Osteoarthritis (AOA) is a form of joint degeneration that affects movement and overall quality of daily life, but it is more uncommon compared to knee or hip OA. Ankles joint is composed of three major bones: the tibia (shinbone), fibula (calf bone), and talus (ankle bone). As a result of the disorders' increasing cartilage deterioration, there is bone-on-bone friction and constriction of the joint space, which ultimately results in discomfort and decreased mobility. Prompt detection and classification of AOA using clinical imaging techniques, such as MRI and X-rays, is important for timely treatment and effective therapy. Precisely classifying the different grades of AOA is vital for timely identification and effective therapy selection. Traditional grading schemes depend on radiologists' subjective, inter-reader variability-prone subjective evaluation. The current research suggests a semi-automated method for assessing and rating AOA using MATLAB and Joint Space Width (JSW) assessment. Recognition of edges is used to emphasize bone edges after the raw X-ray picture has been preprocessed employing contrast enhancement and noise reduction procedures. The Euclidean distance within the talus, fibula, and tibia margins can subsequently be measured by individuals by choosing many pairs of points across the intersection region. These measurements are linked to predetermined OA severity classifications conforming to medical norms and normalized to millimeters applying an established metric. In addition, the method estimates the overall OA grade and calculates the average JSW. This method helps radiologists make increasingly precise and predictable findings while also increasing uniformity and lowering variability.
keywords: ankle osteoarthritis; joint space width; X-ray images; edge detection; cartilage degeneration; talus; fibula; tibia; inter-reader variability

title: Enhancing Biomedical Multi-modal Representation Learning with Multi-scale Pre-training and Perturbed Report Discrimination
source: IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
abstract: Vision-language models pre-trained on large scale of unlabeled biomedical images and associated reports learn generalizable semantic representations. These multi-modal representations can benefit various downstream tasks in the biomedical domain. Contrastive learning is widely used to pre-train vision-language models for general natural images and associated captions. Despite its popularity, we found biomedical texts have complex and domain-specific semantics that are often neglected by common contrastive methods. To address this issue, we propose a novel method, perturbed report discrimination, for pre-train biomedical vision-language models. First, we curate a set of text perturbation methods that keep the same words, but disrupt the semantic structure of the sentence. Next, we apply different types of perturbation to reports, and use the model to distinguish the original report from the perturbed ones given the associated image. Parallel to this, we enhance the sensitivity of our method to higher level of granularity for both modalities by contrasting attention-weighted image sub-regions and sub-words in the image-text pairs. We conduct extensive experiments on multiple downstream tasks, and our method outperforms strong baseline methods. The results demonstrate that our approach learns more semantic meaningful and robust multi-modal representations.
keywords: multimodal representation learning; contrastive pre-training; text perturbation

title: Development of Automated Hybrid Fusion System for Poisson Noise Mitigation in X-Ray Images of Osteoarthritis
source: International Conference on Advanced Computing and Communication Systems (ICACCS)
abstract: Denoising X-ray images is vital in medical image enhancement for Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems, especially in diagnosing conditions like knee osteoarthritis. X-ray image quality can be deteriorated by statistical noise such as Poisson noise. This corruption can be minimized by increasing the radiation intensity and detector exposure time. However, certain situations require low-dose detection and quick response, such as security checks and medical imaging assessments. These challenges often involve trade-offs between reducing noise and preserving important edge details, making the denoising process complex. This research work introduces a hybrid approach that fuses two distinct denoising techniques: Fused Wavelet Transform and Autoencoder networks. This fusion approach aims to combine the strengths of both methods to improve denoising performance and accuracy. Standard image quality metrics, such as the Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Frequency Based Error (FBE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Structural Similarity Index Matrix (SSIM) are employed for assessing performance (CNR). The discussed framework was comprehensively examined using 3,311 single-vendor scans ranging over the publicly exposed dataset (Dataset 1) and a real-time dataset (Dataset 2) containing 3,451 X-ray scans of various patients. The gathered results confirmed the potency of the initiated design over other cutting-edge architectures in terms of 4.21 percent improvement in PSNR (90.53), MSE (0.05), MAE (0.09), SSIM (0.91), FBE (1.17), and CNR (2.26) in decibels for the mean square fusion, and 3.72 percent improvement in PSNR (89.32), MSE (0.10), MAE (0.12), SSIM (0.87), FBE (1.16), and CNR (2.49) in decibels for DWT-based ASR fusion. Thus, the proposed hybrid fusion method generates more detailed and accurate denoised images than the conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based methods.
keywords: shot noise; knee osteoarthritis; hybrid denoising; wavelet transform; autoencoder; low-dose imaging; computer-aided diagnosis; image fusion; structural similarity index

title: Rheumatic Carditis Screening Unveiled on YOLO Algorithms Insights
source: International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Rheumatic Heart Disease (RHD is a chronic condition resulting from rheumatic fever, which is caused by a group A Streptococcal infection. It primarily affects children and young adults, especially in low- and middle-income countries, and is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in these populations. The disease manifests through inflammation and scarring of the heart valves, often leading to long-term complications like heart failure, arrhythmias, and valve dysfunction. Early detection and accurate staging of RHD are crucial for effective treatment and prevention of further complications. This publication explores the potential of integrating the YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithm with advanced imaging techniques, such as Echocardiogram and Cardiac MRI to automate RHD detection and staging. Echocardiogram offers detailed real-time volumetric imaging of the heart, allowing for improved diagnosis of valve abnormalities, while Cardiac MRI is invaluable in assessing myocardinal fibrosis and heart function in advanced RHD case. YOLO, a real-time object detection algorithm, can be applied to these imaging modalities to identify heart valve lesions, regurgitation, and fibrosis with high accuracy. This automated approach aims to provide real-time diagnostic insights, classify patients into different stages of RHD, and support clinicians in decision-making. However, challenges such as data availability, sensitivity to subtle image features, and regulatory hurdles remain. The integration of machine learning with medical imaging could revolutionize RHD diagnosis, particularly in resource-limited settings, by improving accuracy, reducing diagnostic time, and enabling large-scale screening programs. Further research and development are needed to refine these technologies for clinical use.
keywords: rheumatic heart disease; rheumatic carditis; YOLO; automated disease detection; echocardiography; cardiac MRI; heart valve lesions; valvular regurgitation; myocardial fibrosis; disease staging; screening; resource-limited settings

title: Robot-CT Scanning Oriented Synchronous Trajectory Planning of a Dual-Manipulator System
source: Chinese Control Conference (CCC)
abstract: At present, most CT scanning systems adopt the traditional horizontal O-frame, suspension or C-arm structures, which can not balance the flexibility and functionality. With the development of robot technology, CT scanning systems based on manipulators have gradually emerged. However, limited by the motion accuracy of the manipulator, most researchers sacrifice the flexibility or increase the mass to improve the accuracy. To overcome this limitation, a new master-slave teaching-based scanning method is proposed to improve the scanning accuracy of the dual-manipulator Robot-CT system with the auxiliary function of rigid links. First, a rigid link is employed to connect the end effectors of the two manipulators. Next, the sampled trajectory of each joint of the slave-manipulator is recorded while the master-manipulator pulls the slave-manipulator to perform a circular motion. Finally, when carrying out the scanning, the dual-manilupator system reproduces the recorded joint trajectory without the rigid element, thereby improving the accuracy of the dual-manipulator CT scanning system to achieve a high-accuracy spatiotemporal synchronization and alignment of pose. To this end, a fifth-order spline interpolation is used to interpolate the sampled trajectory of each joint of the slave-manipulator, which allows it to perfectly reproduce the joint trajectory recorded during the teaching process and ensures the smoothness of the angular velocity and acceleration curves. Simulations are investigated and the corresponding results confirm the effectiveness of the trajectory planning method of the slave-manipulator.
keywords: trajectory planning; rigid links; scanning accuracy

title: Analysis of Bones Abnormality Detection and Segmentation
source: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Numerous musculoskeletal disorders can be caused by bone diseases, which are widespread. Musculoskeletal conditions are estimated to affect 1.71 billion people worldwide. In addition to musculoskeletal fractures, knee osteoarthritis, fractures, and femoral neck injuries are all relatively prevalent bone illnesses. Missed fractures, on the other hand, are a frequent prognostic failure in accidents and emergencies. As a result, patients’ treatment and care are complicated and delayed. Deep Learning (DL) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are currently garnering a lot of interest for their potential to help physicians identify bone fractures. Studies in traumatology and orthopedics have demonstrated the utility and potential of DL in the radiograph-based diagnosis of fractures and illnesses. In this paper, different classification techniques have been compared to classify the bone. The methods used for detection and segmentation of wrist bones are Inception-v3, VGG16, Densenet-121, and Resnet-50while for elbow bones, Resnet-50, Inception-v3, Densenet-121, and Densenet-169 are used. Two datasets are used in the experiments.: Kaggle dataset and MURA dataset. The experimental results show that the Densenet-169 and Inception-v3 performed better than the other models using MURA dataset and Kaggle dataset respectively.
